*LP64-003 task 1, tooling (2026-11-16, commits 9a36c51 "See narrowed pointer-sized integers and unprototyped pointer calls at 64 bits" and 15df016 "Narrow the cast pattern's difference exclusion and correct the LP64-003 row", pushed):* no game, engine, port or renderer source and no build file changed; the 32-bit program is not touched. (1) `scripts/port/lp64_casts.py` `find_casts` also finds a truncating cast applied to a parenthesised pointer-width cast, `(u32)((uintptr_t)p)`, and the types `uint32_t`, `int32_t`, `uint16_t` and `int16_t`; it leaves out a cast of a difference of two addresses, `(s32)((uintptr_t)a - (uintptr_t)b)`, only when a top-level minus inside the wrapping parentheses is followed by a second `(uintptr_t)` or `(intptr_t)` cast; `(u32)((uintptr_t)p - 4)` is still found (the first version of the exclusion skipped any top-level subtraction, which the review caught; the count was 28 in 13 files before and after the fix). `lp64_casts.py check` still prints `OK: 28 truncating casts in 13 files, all allowed`, so `lp64_casts_allowed.txt` is unchanged (the planning run's widened pattern found 29, one being the difference at `src/init.c:129`, which this pattern excludes). (2) `lp64_diagnostics.py gate` also refuses, before compiling anything, an entry carrying `-Wno-error`, `-Wno-error=KIND` or `-Wno-KIND` for a kind that entry's language gates (all three in C, `int-to-pointer-cast` in C++), or an argument starting with `@` (a response file could hide a flag from the check); each refusal names its reason. (3) New commands `lp64_diagnostics.py narrowing [--check] [--all] BUILD_DIR...` and `unprototyped [--check] BUILD_DIR...`, kept in a new module beside it, `scripts/port/lp64_static_checks.py`, because `lp64_diagnostics.py` would otherwise pass 500 lines (it is 422 lines with the dispatch; the module is 182); the diagnostics file loads the module by path and passes it each tree's syntax-only commands. `narrowing` compiles every C and C++ entry with `-Wconversion -Wno-sign-conversion -Wno-float-conversion -Wno-error` under `LC_ALL=C` and lists each implicit conversion whose source type is `uintptr_t`, `intptr_t` or `romptr_t` as `file:line:column: SOURCE -> TARGET | source text`; `--all` adds the other 64-bit source types (`long`, `unsigned long`, `long long`, `size_t`, `ptrdiff_t`, `ssize_t`, `u64`, `s64`, `uint64_t`, `int64_t`) as a report that `--check` never counts. GCC drops the typedef name after arithmetic, so `(uintptr_t) a + b` narrowed to `u32` shows as `long unsigned int` and is found only by `--all`; the command's help and the module's docstring say so, and that a file with `#line` directives (`gunfire.c`, `gun.c`, `lv.c`, `env.c`) is listed at the compiler's line numbers. `unprototyped` compiles every C entry with `-Wimplicit-function-declaration` restored and `-aux-info`, and lists each call without a prototype, as `file:line:column: NAME | PROTOTYPE`, to a function whose definition (an `NF` or `OF` line of any file's aux-info) takes or returns a pointer or a 64-bit type; a name with no definition in the tree (a library function or a macro) is not listed. Both exit 2 when a tree is not a configured 64-bit tree, when no entry of the right language exists, or when any compile fails (such a file was not measured). `--check` compares each file's count with its line in `lp64_narrowing_allowed.txt` or `lp64_unprototyped_allowed.txt` (`path<TAB>count<TAB>reason`, exact match: more or fewer fails, the latter saying to lower or remove the line). (4) Both allowlists were written from this run, every line with the reason `existing before LP64-003`. (5) CI's tests step runs the two `--check` lines after `gate`, and the new test file after the diagnostics tests; `AGENTS.md`'s 64-bit paragraph and the LP64-003 row of the plan describe them. *Counts* (GCC 13.3, x86_64 container, both 64-bit trees): `narrowing` lists 112 places in 19 files and `unprototyped` 159 calls in 75 files, against the planning figures of 111 in 18 and 157 in 73. The headless tree alone gives 89 in 16 and 152 in 70, the video tree alone the same as both together. All the difference is video-only code in files both trees compile: the planning script compiled each file once, with the first tree's command, so it missed `port/src/port_state_effects_audit.c:31` (`uintptr_t` to `u32`, video-only code, the file the gate's task 10 found), and `strcmp` at `port/src/port_music_export.c:48` and `portDisplayCrosshairImage` at `src/game/options.c:2255` (unprototyped). Neither figure moves a Global Constraint. *What ran:* the new and extended tests (`test_lp64_casts.py` 23 tests, `test_lp64_diagnostics.py` 39, `test_lp64_static_checks.py` 22; each new test was seen to fail first: the cast tests on the missing pattern, the gate tests on the missing refusal, the new file's tests on the missing commands) pass with plain `python3`; task check step 1 in the x86_64 container (`329 files compiled, 0 failed` and `360 files compiled, 0 failed`); step 4 in the x86_64 container (`OK: 112 narrowings in 19 files, all allowed`, `OK: 159 unprototyped calls in 75 files, all allowed`); `lp64_casts.py check`, `test_lp64_env.py`, `test_compare_win32.py`, `test_settings_placement.py`, `settings_placement.py`, `test_hand_gallery.py`, `test_ci_dependencies.py`, `hand_gallery.py verify --allow-pending` (strict inputs fresh, deferred pending) and `bun scripts/bright-builds-check.ts all` (0 findings). Step 3, `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`: exit 0, `identical in loaded code and data` (63 s and 55 s). *Not run:* step 2 (the i686 build and 20-mission smoke) and the `-m32` bash harness lines of CI's tests step, since no C, C++ or build file changed; the aarch64 container; the ROM; anything in CI.

*LP64-003 task 2, the `-m32` harnesses at both pointer widths (2026-11-16, commits 8c01c6b "Run the ROM-free test harnesses at both pointer widths", f4215de "Let the tracer strip test accept both float arithmetics" and 4d90a65 "Fail a harness when an x86 host cannot build its 32-bit half", pushed):* no game, engine, port or renderer source and no build file changed; the 32-bit program is not touched. (1) New `scripts/port/harness_widths.sh`, sourced by a harness, provides `harness_widths` (prints `32` when `${CC:-gcc}` accepts `-m32` and `64` when its own pointers are 8 bytes, read from `__SIZEOF_POINTER__`; `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS="32"` or `"64"` restricts it; it fails, naming the request, when no width can run, when the `-dM` probe of the compiler fails (the compiler's message is printed), and, on a compiler whose `-dumpmachine` is x86_64 or i386 to i686, when `-m32` is rejected: that is a missing 32-bit toolchain, as it was a failure before this task, and the message says to install `gcc-multilib` or run `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=64`; a compiler that cannot make 32-bit code at all, such as aarch64's, just offers no 32), `harness_flags WIDTH [EXTRA...]` (`-m32` and EXTRA for 32, nothing for 64, so the x86-only `-msse2 -mfpmath=sse` are not given to x86_64 or aarch64 GCC, which use SSE or NEON arithmetic by default) and `harness_pending NAME WIDTH` (true when `NAME WIDTH` is in `HARNESS_PENDING`, at the top of the file). A harness takes `widths=$(harness_widths)` (so a failure stops it under `set -e`), loops over them, skips a pending half with the line `NAME: 64-bit half pending (LP64-003 task 11)` and prints `NAME: PASS (32-bit)` and `NAME: PASS (64-bit)`. (2) The 18 harnesses that compile with `-m32` run their body once per width, with the 32-bit compile and run commands as they were: `test_ads`, `test_buffers`, `test_build_time`, `test_dyn`, `test_hit_sound`, `test_hitmap`, `test_hud`, `test_image_bank`, `test_mission_cheats`, `test_mission_hints`, `test_mission_times`, `test_save_transfer`, `test_stan_callbacks`, `test_start_input`, `test_states`, `test_upstream_merge`, `test_wardrobe`, `test_web_logo`. Where a harness had `-m32 ... -msse2 -mfpmath=sse` the second pair moved into the `harness_flags` call, so for 32 bits those flags now sit where `-m32` was (after the compiler name) rather than further along the line; the compiled program is the same. Things that are not the plain loop: `test_ads.sh` still ends by running `test_dyn.sh`, which runs its own widths; `test_buffers.sh` runs the model, audio, memory-bank, token and allocator drivers and the C++ graphics driver once per width and the Python audit once; `test_hud.sh` runs `test_hud_clearance.c`, which has no `-m32`, once after the loop; `test_mission_cheats.sh` and `test_mission_times.sh` loop their runtime and compile-time variants inside each width; `test_states.sh` loops its two drivers per width and runs `test_state_layout.py` once; `test_image_bank.sh`, `test_stan_callbacks.sh` and `test_web_logo.sh` with `--web` run once with emcc as before and keep their old `... passed (emcc)` line, without asking for widths; `test_save_transfer.sh`'s 64-bit half is the build the host compiler makes natively (the line it always ran) and its 32-bit half is the `-m32` build CI turns on with `MIDAS_SAVE_TEST_I686=1`, so without the variable a host that can build 64 bits prints `32-bit half skipped (set MIDAS_SAVE_TEST_I686=1)` and one that cannot (a 32-bit-only host) runs it: there the `-m32` build, with `-D_TIME_BITS=64`, now runs in place of the native build the old script always ran. (3) `scripts/port/test_harness_widths.sh` (new, in CI's tests step; 21 checks) tests the helper with a stand-in compiler first on `PATH`: an aarch64 one that rejects `-m32` gives `64`; one that accepts it on a 64-bit host `32` then `64`; on a 32-bit host `32`; both restrictions; a request that no width satisfies fails; an x86_64 or i686 one that rejects `-m32` fails naming the missing 32-bit toolchain and `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=64`, and gives `64` when restricted to it; an unknown width is refused; a failing macro probe fails and shows the compiler's message; the pending test; the flags; and a compiler whose macro list is long (see below). It was seen to fail first, on the missing helper. (4) `test_ads.c` and `test_wardrobe.c` declare the stub `uintptr_t osVirtualToPhysical(void *)` as `include/PR/os.h` does, where they had `u32` (the declarations disagreed, so neither compiled at 64 bits), and `test_knife_ads.c` builds its command words as `(u32)G_MTX << 24` and so on, where `G_MTX << 24` and `(u8)G_TRI1 << 24` were an `int` shifted into its sign bit, which sign-extends into a 64-bit word. (5) `HARNESS_PENDING` holds `test_wardrobe 64` only; Task 11 empties it. With the stubs corrected, `test_wardrobe` at 64 bits stops on `ASSERTION FAULT - paNativeFit(&nativeData.DisplayList,-200,items[i]==ITEM_FIST ? 50 : 0,portWardrobeCuff(variant),BOND_CONNERY,&fit) - scripts/port/test_wardrobe.c, line 246`, the 24-byte `Vertex` indexing 16-byte `Vtx` data, as the plan measured. `test_ads` first stopped at 64 bits on `scripts/port/test_tracers.c` line 158 (`core[2].v.ob[0] == 26`), which is not a pointer-width defect: `test_ads.sh` compiles its drivers with a plain `-m32` and without the shipped build's `-msse2 -mfpmath=sse` (`CMakeLists.txt:68`), so `0.9f * 30` truncated to `s16` was 26 in x87 extended precision and is 27 in the SSE or NEON arithmetic every shipped and planned build uses (the same compile of the driver with `-m32 -msse2 -mfpmath=sse` failed it too). The assertion pinned an artefact of the harness's own flags. A later commit ("Let the tracer strip test accept both float arithmetics") makes the scale-1 assertions accept both results as consistent pairs (26 with -26 and a far-corner depth of 2008, 27 with -27 and 2009, the same effect on `2000 + 0.9f * 10`), with the comment saying which arithmetic gives which; the next assertion, which allows 80 or 81, already allowed for it. No `test_ads.sh` flag and no `port/src` file changed. With that, `test_ads` passes at 64 bits (aarch64 and x86_64 containers) and at 32 bits (x86_64 and i686 containers), and `test_ads 64` is off the pending list. (6) A flaw the first version had, found by running it eight times: `harness_widths` piped the compiler's macro list into `grep -q`, and under `pipefail` the compiler's SIGPIPE (the pipe closed after the first match) now and then dropped the 64-bit half without a message. It reads the macros into a variable now, and the test has a stand-in compiler that prints 20,000 macros after the pointer size (seen to fail against the piped form). *What the containers print* (this Mac, Docker; the x86_64 and i686 containers are one image, and `harness_widths` prints `32` then `64` in both, since the compiler is a 64-bit GCC with multilib; the i686 container does not have 4-byte native pointers): in the x86_64 and i686 containers every harness prints both PASS lines, except `test_wardrobe` (32-bit PASS and the pending line for 64), `test_save_transfer` (64 only in the x86_64 container, both with `MIDAS_SAVE_TEST_I686=1`, which the i686 run set), and `test_start_input`, a known gap in the x86_64 and i686 containers: its 32-bit compile fails there because the 32-bit SDL headers are missing, as it did before this change, and it is not a line of CI's tests step; it fails in the container before this change as well (`SDL2/_real_SDL_config.h: No such file or directory`; it is not a CI line; its 64-bit half passes with `MIDAS_HARNESS_WIDTHS=64` in the x86_64 container and in the aarch64 container); in the aarch64 container (`-m32` rejected) every harness prints `PASS (64-bit)` only, with the same pending line for `test_wardrobe`. `test_buffers.sh` ran without `MIDAS_BUFFER_SANITIZE=1` (it hangs under i686 emulation here; CI runs it with the variable, which is unchanged); the 64-bit half is not run under the sanitizers here. The CI lines of the step are otherwise unchanged apart from the new `test_harness_widths.sh` line. *Task check:* step 1 in the x86_64 container (`329 files compiled, 0 failed` and `360 files compiled, 0 failed`); step 3, `compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`, exit 0 (`identical in loaded code and data`); step 4 in the x86_64 container, exit 0, with the counts unchanged (`OK: 112 narrowings in 19 files, all allowed` and `OK: 159 unprototyped calls in 75 files, all allowed`). Also run: `test_ci_dependencies.py` and `bun scripts/bright-builds-check.ts all` (0 findings). *Review fix (commit "Fail a harness when an x86 host cannot build its 32-bit half"):* the helper's x86 check, the `-dM` failure and the extra tests described above were added after the review; the first version dropped a rejected `-m32` silently on every host. The helper's widths were re-checked with two harnesses in each container (x86_64 and i686: `32 64`; aarch64: `64`). *Not run:* the sanitizer variant of `test_buffers.sh`, the `--web` variants (no emscripten here), anything in CI, the ROM, step 5 of the task check (it does not exist until Task 4).

*LP64-003 task 3, arenas above 4 GB, the host-pointer test and the startup check (2026-11-16, commit "Keep 64-bit game memory above 4 GB and check it at startup"):* (1) `port/include/port_hostptr.h`: at 64 bits `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR(v)` is `((((uintptr_t) (v)) >> 32) != 0)`, "any of the upper 32 bits set"; the 32-bit form and the `GE_XBOX` form are unchanged token for token (the 64-bit branch is an `#if IS_64_BIT` inside the existing non-Xbox `#else`, after an added `#include "platform_info.h"`), and the header comment states the rule and its condition, that no game data lives below 4 GB. The old test cast through `unsigned int`, so at 64 bits it called `0xFFFFFFFF` a host address and `0x0000AAAA03123456` (a host address whose low word looks like a segment-3 word) not one. (2) New `port/include/port_lp64.h` and `port/src/port_lp64.c` (175 lines): `portLp64RegionIsHigh(start, size)` is true when the region starts at or above `0x100000000` and does not wrap; `portLp64CheckRegion(name, start, size)` prints `ge: lp64: NAME at ADDRESS is below 4 GB; a 64-bit build needs every game address above 4 GB (scripts/port/native_64bit_plan.md, "Addresses")` and exits with status 4 for a low region, and otherwise remembers its name and start (16 entries for the report; a later name for the same start replaces the earlier, so the ROM's mapping is listed as `ROM image`, not `high allocation`; regions past 16 are still checked and counted as "and N more"); `portLp64CheckAddressSpace()` checks the main executable's loaded segments (the span of the `PT_LOAD` segments of the first object `dl_iterate_phdr` reports), a 64-byte `malloc` block and a stack address, then logs `ge: lp64: address space OK:` with each remembered region's name and start. The executable-image check is Linux-only (`#if defined(__linux__)`); a 64-bit build on any other system stops at an `#error` saying that platform's port must supply the main executable's loaded address range (the macOS project fills it in). At 32 bits the three are macros that generate no code (`1`, `((void) 0)`, `((void) 0)`), and `CMakeLists.txt` removes `port_lp64.c` from the source list unless `GE_POINTER_BITS` is 64: with the file in the 32-bit list, its empty object still grew the Windows executable's `.rdata` by 20 bytes (0xf526c to 0xf5280, at the end, where the objects' compiler idents sit) and changed 14 bytes of `.text` (`compare_win32.py` exit 1, with every change of this task except the `port_memp.c` message), and without it the comparison was identical. (3) `port/src/pcsched.c` at 64 bits: `portAllocHighRaw` calls `mmap` with no address hint (a new `#elif IS_64_BIT` branch; the hint argument is ignored) and unmaps and refuses a result `portLp64RegionIsHigh` rejects; a new static `portAllocHighOrExit(name, size)` maps one region, and when that fails logs `ge: NAME: could not map SIZE bytes above 4 GB` and exits with status 1 (no `NULL` return, no low fallback), and passes the region to `portLp64CheckRegion`; `portGetMempArena` maps the `memp arena` through it, `portAllocHighReserve` the `high arena`, and `portAllocHigh` (a request the 64 MB arena cannot hold) and `portAllocHighDedicated` (the ROM image) a `high allocation`; a request too large for their `u32` rounding is fatal at 64 bits too, with its own message (`ge: high allocation: a request of N bytes is too large to round up to the mapping size`, exit 1), instead of returning `NULL`. The 32-bit paths, the hint ladders (`0x20000000`, `0x30000000`, `0x50000000` and up), the Windows scan and the 32-bit messages are untouched; each 64-bit branch sits behind `IS_64_BIT`. No hint, fixed base or `-no-pie` link is added at 64 bits. (4) `port/src/romdata.c`: the "keeping the heap copy" fallback is inside `#if !IS_64_BIT` (at 64 bits `portAllocHighDedicated` stops the game instead of returning `NULL`), and `portLp64CheckRegion("ROM image", sRom, sRomSize)` runs once the image is copied. (5) `port/src/main.c` calls `portLp64CheckAddressSpace()` right after `romdataInit` returns, before `osInitialize` and `portAnimDataInit`: the arenas are reserved (`main.c:853`) and the ROM image is in place, and no ROM data is converted yet. (6) `port/src/port_memp.c`: the memory-bank exhaustion message names the bank as well as its number, at both widths: `Memory bank exhausted (bank %u "%s", request %u bytes)`, with the names of `enum MEMPOOL` (`total`, `mf`, `2`, `ml`, `stage`, `me`, `permanent`). This is the one change to the 32-bit program (below). (7) `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` includes `port_hostptr.h` and asserts `!PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR(0x0E000000u)` at both widths, and at 64 bits `!PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR(0xFFFFFFFFu)` and `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR(0x100000000ull)`. (8) `scripts/port/test_high_alloc.c` (run by `test_buffers.sh`) expects the 64-bit fatal exit for oversized requests (below). (9) New `scripts/port/test_lp64_address.sh` and `.c`, in CI's tests step after `test_abi_probe.sh`, using `harness_widths.sh`: the truth table of `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR` at each width (32 bits: `0x0E000000` and `0x0FFFFFFF` false, `0x10000000` true; 64 bits: `0x0E000000` and `0xFFFFFFFF` false, `0x100000000` and `0x0000AAAA03123456` true); at 64 bits `portLp64RegionIsHigh` for a region ending at 4 GB (low), one starting there (high) and a zero-size one there (high); at 32 bits that the check returns for a low address; and at 64 bits the driver's `portLp64CheckAddressSpace()` linked `-fPIE -pie`, which must print `ge: lp64: address space OK` and exit 0, and the same driver linked `-fno-pie -no-pie` (the one deliberate `-no-pie` link, in the test), which must exit 4 naming `executable image` (it prints `ge: lp64: executable image at 0x400000 is below 4 GB; ...`). It was seen to fail first: before `port_lp64.h` existed it did not compile (`fatal error: port_lp64.h: No such file or directory`). Against the old macro (the header from 4d90a65 placed first on the include path) the 64-bit truth table fails three cases, and against a weakened predicate (`start > 4 GB`) the two "at 4 GB is high" cases fail. It passes at 32 and 64 bits in the x86_64 container and at 64 bits in the aarch64 container. *The 64-bit executable* (`build/lp64/boot/IronSights`, Debug, headless, `GE_FRAMES=120`, `GE_ROM=/rom/baserom.u.z64`, run from a scratch folder under `build/lp64`): in the aarch64 container the log has `ge: memp arena: 64 MB at 0xffff9aa00000`, `ge: portAllocHigh: 64 MB arena at 0xffff96a00000` and `ge: lp64: address space OK: memp arena 0xffff9aa00000, high arena 0xffff96a00000, ROM image 0xffff95000000, executable image 0xaaaae47e0000, malloc block 0xaaab19ba1490, stack 0xffffc65b0c7c`; in the x86_64 container `0x7ffffb4bc000`, `0x7ffff74bc000` and `... ROM image 0x7ffff5cbb000, executable image 0x555555554000, malloc block 0x555556553490, stack 0x7ffffffc572c`. Both runs then end with signal 11 (exit 139) in `modelAnimReadRootMotionValue` (`src/game/model.c:941`) from `initResolveAnimGroups` in `bossInitMainthreadData` (`src/boss.c:284`), the crash the plan measured, which Task 4 turns into a named stop. The sanitizer build (`-DGE_SANITIZE=ON`, aarch64) passes the check too (its `malloc` block is at `0x506000000020`, still above 4 GB) and stops at its first report, `src/game/initanitable.c:241`, as measured. *The other pools' behaviour on exhaustion*, read from the code at this commit, for LP64-005 (none is resized or changed here):

| Pool | Where it is made | What happens when it is full |
|---|---|---|
| Memory banks (`stage`, `permanent` and the others) | `port/src/port_memp.c` `portMempAllocate`, in the 64 MB memp arena | Falls back to the `permanent` bank; when that is full too, `sysFatalError("Memory bank exhausted (bank N \"name\", request N bytes)")`. Named and fatal. Setup files, model slots, the graphics and frame buffers, the stage texture pool and the music heap are all carved from these banks, so their own allocation at stage load stops here. |
| Graphics buffer (the master display list, `g_GfxBuffers`) | `src/game/dyn.c` `dynInitMemory`, `-mgfx` KB per stage, doubled on PC, from the `stage` bank | Not checked: display-list writers run past the end into the next allocation. Only `GE_ROOM_AUDIT` notices, after the frame (`portDynAuditFrameEnd`: `roomaudit: *** DYN POOL OVERFLOW`). Silent otherwise. |
| Frame data (vertices, matrices, lights; `g_VtxBuffers`) | same place, `-mvtx` KB, doubled and sized by `portDynVertexCapacity` | `port/src/port_dyn.c` `portDynAllocate`: `sysFatalError("Frame data buffer exhausted (request ..., remaining ... bytes)")`. Named and fatal. |
| Room display lists and vertices | `src/game/bg.c` `bgLoadRoom`, one block per room from the `mema` heap (`-ma` KB, `src/mema.c` `memaAlloc`) | `memaAlloc` returns `NULL` after eight defragmentation passes and the room is not loaded, so it is not drawn; a block too small for the expanded display list makes the loader return -1 and the room is freed and not drawn. A message only with `GE_ROOM_AUDIT` (`roomaudit: *** MEMA ALLOC FAILED`). |
| Model slots (`g_ModelSlots`, `g_AnimModelSlots`) | `src/game/initunk_005520.c`, a fixed count from the `stage` bank | `modelmgrInstantiateModel` and `modelmgrInstantiateModelWithAnim` (`src/game/model.c`) return `NULL` to their caller, with no message. |
| Model display-list copies and the model texture pool | `src/game/objecthandler_2.c` through `portAllocHigh` (the 4 MB pool is `portModelTexPool`) | At 32 bits a `NULL` from `portAllocHigh` leaves the model node unconverted; at 64 bits, after this task, a request the high arena cannot hold gets its own mapping, and only a failed mapping stops the game (`ge: high allocation: could not map N bytes above 4 GB`). |
| Texture pools (the stage pool, `-mt` KB doubled, `src/game/initmttex.c`; the model pool above) | loaded by `texLoad` (`src/game/image.c`) | When fewer than `0x10CC` bytes (uncompressed) or `0xA28` (zlib) are free, the texture is pointed at the pool's start and draws as garbage; the PC build prints `ge: TEXOOM: texnum N cannot fit ...` for the first 12. The test is a fixed minimum, not the texture's size. Named, not fatal. |
| Music heap | `src/music.c`, `4 * 0x2E000` bytes from the `permanent` bank | `alHeapAlloc` (`src/libultra/audio/heapalloc.c`) returns `NULL` with no message (its `_DEBUG` report is compiled out), and `musicSeqPlayerInit` copies into the result unchecked, so the game crashes unnamed. (The comment in `music.c` says the allocator has no bounds check; it has one, and returns `NULL`.) |

*The 32-bit Windows comparison* (`compare_win32.py commits HEAD WORKTREE`, exit 1): `.text` (VirtualSize 0x335904 to 0x335914), `.rdata` (0xf526c to 0xf52ac), `.data`, `.reloc`, `.CRT`, the `/4` section and the BaseRelocation and TLS directories differ. Every object file of the two builds was compared: only `port_memp.c.obj` differs in its code or loaded data. `main.c.obj`, `pcsched.c.obj` and `romdata.c.obj` differ in debug sections only (same disassembly with relocations, same non-debug section contents), and every other object is byte-identical. In `port_memp.c.obj` `.text` grew from 0x200 to 0x210 bytes and `.rdata` from 0x98 to 0xdc: `_portMempAllocate`'s exhaustion call loads `names[bank]` and passes it as a third argument (`mov 0x...(,%esi,4),%eax`, the other two arguments moved one stack slot up), and `.rdata` gains the seven bank names, their pointer table and the longer format string. A per-function comparison of the two executables' disassembly, with addresses blanked, shows `_portMempAllocate` as the only changed function (the remaining entries it lists are the `.ctors` pointer tables, data disassembled as code, whose function addresses moved). Everything else that differs is those 0x10 bytes of code and 0x40 bytes of read-only data moving the code and data linked after them. *LP64-003 task 4, a named stop at each unconverted asset class, and the boot check (2026-11-16). Task 4 built: commit "Stop a 64-bit boot at the first asset class without a converter".* (1) `port/include/port_lp64.h` gains `enum PortLp64Asset` (`PORT_LP64_TEXT_BANKS`, `_FONTS`, `_TEXTURES`, `_ANIMATIONS`, `_MODELS`, `_COLLISION`, `_SETUPS`, `_BACKGROUNDS`, `_AUDIO_BANKS`, `_MUSIC`, `PORT_LP64_ASSET_COUNT`: the design's ten classes in the design's order), declared at both widths (an enum makes no code), and at 64 bits `portLp64AssetName` (`text banks`, `fonts`, `textures`, `animation tables`, `models`, `collision tiles`, `setup files`, `backgrounds`, `audio banks`, `music sequences`; `unknown asset class` outside the enum), `portLp64AssetConverted` and `portLp64RequireConverter`, which for an unconverted class logs `ge: lp64: stopping: asset class "NAME" has no 64-bit converter yet (LP64-004)` and exits with status 5. `port/src/port_lp64.c` (237 lines) holds the names and the converted table, all ten entries 0; LP64-004 sets a class's entry in the commit that lands its converter. At 32 bits `portLp64AssetConverted(asset)` is `1` and `portLp64RequireConverter(asset)` is `((void) 0)`, and `portLp64AssetName` does not exist; `port_lp64.c` stays out of the 32-bit source list. (2) The guards. A guard is the first statement of the code that reads or rewrites a class's ROM bytes (or the compiled-in copy) in place, after declarations whose initializers only look a segment up (`romdataSeg`). Where a class has a compiled-in path that the ROM path's guard does not cover, that path has its own guard. Line numbers are at this commit:

| Class | Guarded function | Place | Compiled-in path |
|---|---|---|---|
| text banks | `romdataTextPreprocess` (rewrites the bank's 4-byte offsets as 4-byte pointers) | `port/src/romdata.c:899` | None to guard: the compiled-in banks are C pointer arrays, used as they are, and at 64 bits they are not linked (`GE_ROMDATA_FALLBACK` is refused); this ROM serves every bank |
| fonts | `portFontBuildSegments` (fontchar tables and `fontdl` written as 4-byte words) | `port/src/segments.c:348` | Covered by the same guard: it precedes the choice between the ROM and the compiled-in composition; the fix-up in `load_font_tables` (`src/game/textrelated.c`) runs after it |
| textures | `texLoad` (writes a texture's data address into a 4-byte slot of a display list, a model file's `ModelFileTextures` record or an image table entry) | `src/game/image.c:2541` | Covered: every caller goes through `texLoad`, including the compiled-in global image bank (`texReset`, `assets/oddtextures.c`) and the room lists (`texLoadFromGdl` through `texLoadFromTextureNum`) |
| animation tables | `portAnimDataInit` (`ModelAnimation`'s 0x14-byte file header read through 8-byte address fields) | `port/src/animdata.c:248` | Covered by the same guard (before the ROM or compiled-in choice); `expand_ani_table_entries`' relocation (`boss.c:282`) runs after it |
| models | `romfileModelConvert` | `port/src/romfile_model.c:412` | Guarded: the compiled-in branch of `load_object_fill_header`, `src/game/objecthandler_2.c:372` (not linked at 64 bits; this ROM serves every model) |
| collision tiles | `romfileStanConvert` (4-byte room pointer slots) | `port/src/romfile_stan.c:65` | Guarded: `portStanPack`, `src/game/stan.c:603` (4-byte room slots), which builds every compiled-in stan; eight stans are missing from this ROM |
| setup files | `romfileSetupConvert` | `port/src/romfile_setup.c:501` | Guarded: the compiled-in setup's restore and word walk in `proplvreset2`, `src/game/prop.c:1979`, the first layout-dependent step on that path (the `SETUP_PROMOTE` before it passes the typed struct's own pointers through); not linked at 64 bits, and this ROM serves every setup |
| backgrounds | `romfileBgConvert` (4-byte offset words of the front matter) | `port/src/romfile_bg.c:68` | Guarded: a new `else` of the served test in `load_bg_file`, `src/game/bg.c:1098`, before the header is read as `s32` words; eleven bg files are missing from this ROM |
| audio banks | `alBnkfNew` (relocated in place through 8-byte pointer slots over 4-byte file offsets) | `port/src/audio_stubs.c:238` | None: the banks come only from the ROM segments, and it is the only bank conversion (`src/libultra/audio/bnkf.c` is not compiled) |
| music sequences | `musicSeqPlayerInit`, before the sequence table is read (`RareALSeqData`'s address slot over a 4-byte file offset) | `src/music.c:798` | None: the table comes only from the ROM segment |

The 19 files this ROM lacks, from the 32-bit smoke's log (`not in this ROM's directory - keeping the compiled-in copy`): the bg files of `sho`, `eld`, `imp`, `ash`, `lue`, `rit`, `ear`, `lee`, `lip`, `wax` and `pam`, and the stans of `ear`, `eld`, `lee`, `lip`, `lue`, `pam`, `rit` and `wax`. At 64 bits their compiled-in copies are not linked. A stage that needs one stops at the bg guard in `load_bg_file`, which runs before the stan is loaded; every missing stan belongs to a missing bg file. (A null stan on its own would be read in `stanDetermineEOF` before `portStanPack` is reached.)

The texture class needs no guard where its directory is installed. `romdataImageTableApply` (`port/src/romdata.c`, inside `romdataInit`, before the address line; the log line `romdata: texture table`) reads the ROM table with `be32` and stores each value into `g_Textures` by field name, and takes the image bank's base from the file table: nothing in it depends on pointer size. The pointer-sized work of the class is `texLoad`'s store into a 4-byte slot, so the guard is there, and it is reached only at the first texture load, after the animation guard. The guard covers `texLoad` as a whole, including `texLoadFromTextureNum` with a stack copy, because the pool record `struct tex` it builds is in the design's texture class too. Edits in upstream-owned files are one include and one call each: `src/game/image.c` (the call inside `#ifndef TARGET_N64`, like the include), `src/music.c`, `src/game/stan.c`, `src/game/objecthandler_2.c` and `src/game/prop.c`; `src/game/bg.c` also gains the two-line `else`. `stan.c` and `objecthandler_2.c` keep their CRLF line endings. It exits 0 only if every run exited with status 5, logged `ge: lp64: address space OK`, stopped at NAME, and logged no `ge: fatal signal` and no sanitizer line (`runtime error:`, `ERROR: AddressSanitizer`, `ERROR: LeakSanitizer`, `ERROR: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer`); it prints `OK: stopped at "NAME" (EXECUTABLE)` or `FAIL:` with every difference and the last 20 log lines. *LP64-003 task 6, host pointers told from numbers and segment words at full width (2026-11-16). Task 6 built: commit "Classify command words and texture slots at pointer width".* The game told a host pointer from a small number or an N64 segment word by looking at a 32-bit copy of the value; at 64 bits that drops the upper half, so a real pointer could pass as a texture number or a segment word. (1) `port/include/port_hostptr.h` gains three predicates beside `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR`, each with a 32-bit form that is the expression its sites had and a 64-bit form that reads the whole word: `PORT_WORD_IS_HOST(w)` is `((u32) (w) >= 0x10000000u)` at 32 bits (under `GE_XBOX` too, whose `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR` differs; the user supplies `u32`) and `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR(w)` at 64; `PORT_WORD_HAS_SEGMENT(w, seg)` is `(((uintptr_t) (w) & 0xFF000000) == ((uintptr_t) (seg) << 24))` at 32 bits and `(((uintptr_t) (w) >> 24) == (uintptr_t) (seg))` at 64; `PORT_WORD_IS_INDEX(w, limit)` is `((uintptr_t) (w) < (uintptr_t) (limit))` at both. The header now includes `platform_info.h` outside the `GE_XBOX` branch as well (a second, guarded include on the other branch); `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR` is unchanged, and `port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`, the strict-tier file that includes the header, uses none of the new names. (2) The sites (line numbers at this commit):

| Site | Before | Now | At 64 bits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `propobj.c:9168-9170` (`bgTestHitOnObj`, `G_VTX`) | `u32 vaddr = gdl->words.w1;` and `vaddr >= 0x10000000u` | `uintptr_t vaddr`, `PORT_WORD_IS_HOST(vaddr)` | a host vertex pointer is used whole; only a word with the upper 32 bits clear is resolved as segment-relative |
| `propobj.c:9293-9295` and `:9477-9479` (`G_TRI1`/`G_TRI2` texture lookups) | `u32 timg = tcmd->words.w1;` and `timg >= 0x10000000u && (timg >> 16) != 0xABCDu` | `uintptr_t timg`, `PORT_WORD_IS_HOST(timg) && (timg >> 16) != 0xABCDu` | the texture number is read at `timg - 8` from the whole pointer; the `0xABCD` IMAGESEG marker test keeps its tokens, so it reads the whole word: an IMAGESEG word (`0xABCD0000 \| id`) has its upper half clear and is already rejected by the host test, and a host pointer whose bits 16-31 are `0xABCD` still counts as a pointer |
| `bg.c:4517-4519` and `:4718-4720` (`bgTestRayIntersectionInRoom`) | as the `propobj.c` texture lookups | as the `propobj.c` texture lookups | as the `propobj.c` texture lookups |
| `lightfixture.c:296` (`lightFindVertexBaseForTri`) | `((uintptr_t) ret & 0xFF000000) == 0x0E000000` | `PORT_WORD_HAS_SEGMENT(ret, 0x0E)` | a host pointer whose bits 24-31 are `0x0E` is no longer rebased onto the room's vertices |
| `othermodemicrocode.c:363` | `(u32) tconfig->index < NUM_TEXTURES` | `PORT_WORD_IS_INDEX(tconfig->index, NUM_TEXTURES)` | a pixel pointer with a small low word is not taken for a texture number |
| `port_textures.c:83` (`texCrosshairNum`) | `(u32) crosshairimage->index < 0x1000u` | `PORT_WORD_IS_INDEX(crosshairimage->index, 0x1000u)` | as above, for the crosshair's slot |
| `port_textures.c:348` (`texLoadSlot`) | `t->entry.index = (u32) (uintptr_t) px;` | `t->entry.index = (uintptr_t) px;` | the external texture's slot holds the whole pixel address |

Each `src/game` file gains one `#include "port_hostptr.h"` (inside the existing `#ifndef TARGET_N64` include block in `propobj.c` and `bg.c`, beside the other includes in `lightfixture.c`, whose function is also compiled for the N64, and `othermodemicrocode.c`); the lines that rebuild the pointers (`(u8 *) (uintptr_t) vaddr`, `(u16 *) (uintptr_t) (timg - 8)`) are unchanged and now take the whole word. (3) The two refusals of external textures at 64 bits in `port/src/port_textures.c` are removed, as the design says (`native_64bit_plan.md`, "External textures stop being refused on 64-bit once their address slot is..."). Behind the first (`portTexExternal`) the slot loader reads a BMP through `stdio`, allocates the blob with `portAllocHigh` into a `u8 *`, writes the pixels through a `u16 *` and stores the address in `entry.index`, now whole; behind the second (`portTexReplaceRom`, called from `texLoad`) the code copies and re-encodes pool bytes through `u8 *` buffers and a `struct tex *`, keyed by the `s32` texture number. Neither path truncates a pointer or assumes 4-byte pointers once the slot is whole. At 64 bits `texLoad` itself is behind Task 4's `textures` guard, so the second path is not reached until LP64-004. `docs/port/abi-and-portability.md` no longer says the file truncates the slot and refuses external textures. (4) The slot loader can be driven ROM-free, so its first run is here rather than in LP64-005: new `scripts/port/test_lp64_textures.c` (173 lines) links `port_textures.c` with stubs (`portRootPath` into a scratch root, `portAllocHigh` from a static array, which is above 4 GB in a position-independent 64-bit executable, and empty stand-ins for the ROM-texture and crosshair paths), writes a 4x4 24-bit BMP it draws itself (no game data) as `Data/Textures/Base/option.bmp`, calls `portTexExternal("option")` and checks that `entry.index` equals the address of the pixels (16 bytes into the allocation); at 64 bits it first checks that the array is above 4 GB. `scripts/port/test_lp64_address.sh` builds and runs it at each width (`-Iinclude` puts the game's `string.h` first, as in the game build, so it adds `-Wno-builtin-declaration-mismatch`), and now passes `-D_LANGUAGE_C` so `test_lp64_address.c` can include `PR/ultratypes.h`. Seen to fail first: at 6def5b4 (in an ignored scratch directory) the driver printed `ge: textures: external textures need the 32-bit build` and `FAIL: the external texture's index is the whole address of its pixels`; with the refusals removed and `(u32) (uintptr_t) px` restored in a scratch edit (reverted) the 64-bit half printed the same `FAIL` line after `option.bmp 4x4 loaded`. (5) `scripts/port/test_lp64_address.c` gains one truth table per predicate. `PORT_WORD_IS_HOST`: `0x0E001234` false at both widths; at 32 bits `0x0FFFFFFF` false and `0x10000000` true (the non-Xbox `PORT_IS_HOST_ADDR` line); at 64 bits `0xFFFFFFFF` false and `0x0000AAAA0E001234` true. `PORT_WORD_HAS_SEGMENT(w, 0x0E)`: `0x0E001234` true and `0x0F001234` false at both; `0x0000AAAA0E001234` false at 64 bits. `PORT_WORD_IS_INDEX(w, 0x1000)`: `0xFFF` true and `0x1000` false at both; `0x0000AAAA00000123` false at 64 bits (the old `(u32)` test said true). Seen to fail first: before the predicates existed both containers stopped on `error: implicit declaration of function 'PORT_WORD_IS_HOST'` (and the other two names). With each 64-bit form replaced by its 32-bit form in a scratch edit (reverted), the 64-bit half printed four failures: `0xFFFFFFFF is not a host word at 64 bits`, `0x0000AAAA0E001234 is a host word although its low word looks like a segment-14 word`, `0x0000AAAA0E001234 is not a segment-14 word at 64 bits` and `0x0000AAAA00000123 is not an index below 0x1000 at 64 bits`. (6) `scripts/port/abi_probe/probe.c` asserts that `ModelFileTextures.TextureID`, `sImageTableEntry.index` and `Gfx.words.w1` are unsigned (`UNSIGNED_FIELD`, `(__typeof__(field)) -1 > 0`), beside the existing pointer-sized assertions, so the full-width sentinel comparisons that the check found correct (`gun.c`, `objecthandler_2.c`, `image.c`, `front.c` and the others in the plan's list) stay unsigned; those sites are not edited. The same macro on a signed `int` field fails to compile (checked in a scratch file). (7) Allowlists: `scripts/port/lp64_narrowing_allowed.txt` `src/game/bg.c` 9 to 7 and `src/game/propobj.c` 21 to 18 (the five `u32` copies), 112 to 107 places; `scripts/port/lp64_casts_allowed.txt` loses the `port/src/port_textures.c` line, 28 to 27 casts in 12 files. The two web-only traces in `texLoad` print the slot with `"%08" PRIxPTR` and the slot's address through `(void *)` (`<inttypes.h>` joins the file's `#ifndef TARGET_N64` include block). Task 4's `portLp64RequireConverter(PORT_LP64_TEXTURES)` stays `texLoad`'s first statement; its comment, which gave the 4-byte slot as the reason, now names what is still unconverted, the pool's `struct tex` records. The one other call, `texLoad((u32 *)((s32)bytes + 4), arg1)` in `texLoadFromDisplayList`, is inside `#ifdef TARGET_N64` (the N64 byte-walk; the PC branch is the `cmd->words` loop above), so it is not compiled on PC and its text is unchanged. ### FORK-088 — Faster frames: GL state answered from memory, arm switches read once

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-15 at the owner's request, as the first
optimizations from the profile in FORK-087. Built and measured for Windows and
the browser. The picture is unchanged (the review gallery regenerated with no
changed image). The owner play-tested the Windows build on 2026-11-15 and
reported that it works. Linux and Steam Deck builds were not built or run.

Inherited behaviour: upstream's renderer sets GL state and does not ask for it
back in a frame. The fork's added passes (Gun Glint and screen reflections,
FORK-058; Glass Reflections, FORK-066; bloom; Tone Mapping and HDR Output,
FORK-082) each save the state they change by querying the driver, about 120
query calls in `port/fast3d/*.inl`, and restore it afterwards.

**What changed:**

- **GL state shadow** ([gfx_gl_shadow.inl](port/fast3d/gfx_gl_shadow.inl)).
  After glad loads a context's functions, `gfx_gl_shadow_install` replaces 32
  of its function pointers with recorders. Calls that set state the passes
  later ask about (program, vertex array, array buffer, framebuffers,
  renderbuffer, active texture, the 2D texture and sampler of each unit, blend
  function, equation and colour, depth function and mask, colour mask, clear
  colour, viewport, scissor box, and the blend, scissor, depth, cull and
  stencil switches) are noted on their way to the driver, and `glGetIntegerv`,
  `glGetBooleanv`, `glGetFloatv` and `glIsEnabled` answer from the note. A
  value nobody has set is asked of the driver once and kept. Deleting an
  object forgets the bindings it could have held; a viewport or colour the
  driver might clamp is not kept. Anything untracked goes to the driver as
  before, so the passes themselves are unchanged. `GE_GLSHADOW=0` leaves
  glad's pointers alone (the old behaviour, and the "before" of a
  measurement); `GE_GLSHADOW_CHECK=1` also asks the driver every time and
  reports any difference.
- **Arm audit switches read once**
  ([port_native_arms.c](port/src/port_native_arms.c)).
  `portWardrobeRenderNode` runs for every hand node of every view each frame
  and called `getenv` three times a call (`GE_ARM_AUDIT_STOCK`,
  `GE_ADS_AUDIT`, `GE_ARM_AUDIT`). It now reads them on first use. The mesh it
  builds, and everything in the arm rendering contracts, is untouched.

**Measured** (2026-11-15, the development laptop; "before" is the last commit
`1e3df59` built by `stock.py --ref HEAD`, "after" this change):

Windows, `bench.py run --smoke` (three repeats, medians, 1920x1080, a quiet
machine: 27% median processor use, 1-5% between repeats), frames a second:

| Scenario | Preset | Stock 1.0.2b | Before | After | Render ms | Game ms |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cradle-fight | default | 898 | 320 | 518 (+62%) | 2.88 to 1.54 | 0.55 to 0.33 |
| dam-walk | default | 1411 | 559 | 815 (+46%) | 1.59 to 0.81 | 0.42 to 0.28 |
| temple-4p | default | 1123 | 421 | 604 (+43%) | 2.32 to 1.41 | 0.87 to 0.59 |
| cradle-fight | matched | 895 | 434 | 665 (+53%) | 2.08 to 1.34 | 0.54 to 0.33 |
| dam-walk | matched | 1400 | 799 | 1120 (+40%) | 1.07 to 0.72 | 0.41 to 0.27 |
| temple-4p | matched | 1112 | 769 | 775 (+1%) | 1.25 to 1.24 | 0.88 to 0.59 |

Browser (headless Chromium 157, ANGLE/Direct3D 11, 1280x960 canvas; one run
each with `GE_GLSHADOW=0` and without, same runtime), renderer milliseconds
per frame:

| Scenario | Default: before to after | Matched: before to after |
|---|---:|---:|
| cradle-fight | 11.64 to 3.08 (-74%) | 10.09 to 2.53 (-75%) |
| dam-walk | 9.87 to 1.83 (-81%) | 8.27 to 1.45 (-82%) |
| temple-4p | 6.35 to 3.45 (-46%) | 2.65 to 2.73 (within noise) |

- The state shadow accounts for the frame-rate gain: the same executable with
  `GE_GLSHADOW=0` against without gave +38% to +63% on Windows (four repeats)
  wherever a gun or a graphics pass is drawn, and no change in four-player
  Temple with settings matched, where neither is.
- The arm change accounts for the game-code time: down by a third in every
  scenario, including the one the shadow does not touch.
- A browser single-player frame now costs 2.0-3.7 ms of processor time
  (render plus game) against 8.8-12.3 ms, so a 120 Hz display is within
  reach there.
- FORK-087's reading of the Windows profile held: with the queries gone the
  driver's worker thread is busy again (1.53 ms a frame on Cradle, from 0.27)
  and the draw call no longer appears among the differences from stock.
- Against stock with settings matched the fork is now at 74-80% in single
  player (from 49-57%) and 70% in four-player. A profile of this build puts
  what remains in per-triangle setup (`gfx_sp_tri1`, +0.34 ms on Cradle), the
  arm mesh still rebuilt each frame (0.13 ms), and HUD rectangles (0.12 ms).

**Checks:** a run of six scenario and preset combinations with
`GE_GLSHADOW_CHECK=1` answered between 3,609 and 345,914 queries from memory
per run with no mismatch against the driver, asking the driver 2 to 6 times.
`python scripts/port/test_gl_queries.py` (new: every state the renderer
queries is tracked by the shadow or listed as asked once at start-up),
`test_bench.py` (37 tests) and `test_bench_profile.py` passed.
`test_wardrobe.sh` and `test_ads.sh` passed in the build container. The
Windows and browser builds passed; the gallery regenerated with zero changed
cells; the Bright Builds checks and the settings placement check passed.

**Limits:** the shadow keeps one record, for the one GL context the game
creates; a second context sharing glad's pointers would need its own. State
changed by code that does not go through glad (none today) would not be seen.
Both are what `GE_GLSHADOW_CHECK=1` exists to catch.

**Shared hooks for later merges:** [gfx_opengl.cpp](port/fast3d/gfx_opengl.cpp)
(inherited) gains the include, one call to `gfx_gl_shadow_install` after glad
loads in `gfx_opengl_init`, and one to `gfx_gl_shadow_frame` in
`gfx_opengl_start_frame`. A new pass that needs another piece of state adds it
to the shadow, setter and query together; `test_gl_queries.py` fails until it
does.

**Sources:** [gfx_gl_shadow.inl](port/fast3d/gfx_gl_shadow.inl),
[port_native_arms.c](port/src/port_native_arms.c),
[test_gl_queries.py](scripts/port/test_gl_queries.py), and the Render
performance rule in `AGENTS.md`.
