### FORK-087 — Profilers for the benchmark runs, and where the time goes

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-15 at the owner's request, as the second
step of performance work (FORK-085 measures; this finds the causes; nothing is
optimized yet). No game behaviour changes: the sampler runs only when
`GE_PROFILE` is set.

Inherited behaviour: upstream has no profiler. Its hitch log and title-bar
figures split a frame into render, swap and game time and stop there. The tree
is built with frame pointers for the crash handler's stack walk, which is what
makes a sampler possible without debug-info unwinding.

**What it does:**

- **Windows sampler** ([port_profile.c](port/src/port_profile.c)):
  `GE_PROFILE=<file>` starts a time-critical thread that wakes `GE_PROFILE_HZ`
  times a second (default 1000). For each other thread whose cycle count has
  moved by more than 20,000 since its last sample, it suspends the thread,
  records its program counter and frame-pointer chain (up to 48 frames, read
  only between the stack pointer and the end of its committed region) with the
  stage, game tick, wake-up number and a microsecond clock, resumes it, and
  reads the cycle count again so the suspension itself does not make it look
  busy. Nothing is allocated or printed while a thread is suspended. Samples
  sit in 48 MB reserved at start and are written once, with the loaded module
  list, by `portProfileWrite`, which `port_bench.c` calls before it leaves.
  The sampler starts from a constructor, so no other file calls it.
- **Report** ([bench_profile.py](scripts/port/bench/bench_profile.py)): names
  addresses with the container's `nm` (functions of the game) or the module
  they lie in, keeps the samples of the benchmark's tick window, and prints
  processor milliseconds per frame by function, self and inclusive, per busy
  thread; with two runs, the functions whose inclusive time differs most. A
  thread's samples over the sampler's wake-ups is its share of a processor.
  Samples under `portPumpEvents` are totalled and set aside: unpaced, the game
  thread spins there waiting for the renderer.
- **Browser** ([bench-audit.mjs](web/tools/bench-audit.mjs),
  `MIDAS_BENCH_PROFILE=1`): records a Chromium CPU profile of each run over the
  DevTools protocol, from player control to the end, with the frames it covers.
  [bench_profile_web.py](scripts/port/bench/bench_profile_web.py) prints the
  same tables for the page's main thread.
- `bench.py run --env NAME=VALUE` passes extra environment to the game, and
  `stock.py` now always copies this checkout's `port_bench.c` and
  `port_profile.c` into a reference build, so every build is measured by the
  same instrument.

**Findings** (2026-11-15, the development laptop, one profiled run of each;
processor milliseconds per frame; the Windows figures are stock 1.0.2b against
Iron Sights at `d56205e` with the `matched` preset on Cradle unless noted):

| Where | Stock | Fork | What it is |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Render thread, total | 1.16 | 2.49 | |
| `gfx_opengl_draw_triangles` (inside the GL driver) | 0.03 | 0.63 | The driver doing its work on the render thread |
| GL driver's own worker thread | 1.16 | 0.27 | The driver's threading, mostly idle in the fork |
| `gfx_sp_tri1`, self | 0.36 | 0.71 | Per-triangle setup |
| `gfx_draw_rectangle` | 0.03 | 0.26 | HUD rectangles (0.57 in four-player) |
| Game thread, outside the pump | 0.23 | 0.86 | |
| `portWardrobeRenderNode` | none | 0.33 | First-person arm mesh rebuilt every frame (0.56 in four-player) |
| `roc_env_cube`, default settings | none | 0.68 | The reflection cube |

1. **The fork queries GL state every frame, and that is the largest single
   cost on both platforms.** `gfx_opengl_glint_draw` (the weapon glint,
   `gfx_glint.inl`) saves the state it changes with one `glIsEnabled`, ten
   `glGetIntegerv` and one `glGetBooleanv`, on every call. The same
   save-by-query pattern is in the bloom, glass, grade, HDR and screen-space
   reflection passes (about 120 query calls in `port/fast3d/*.inl`).
   - In the browser a query crosses into JavaScript and waits on the GPU
     process: on Dam with settings matched, WebGL `getParameter` takes 6.50 ms
     of the 10.14 ms frame, all of it under the glint draw. Four-player Temple,
     where no gun is drawn, spends none and costs 4.76 ms.
   - On Windows the cost shows differently. In stock the NVIDIA driver hands
     draws to its own worker thread (1.16 ms a frame there, 0.03 ms in the
     draw call). In the fork's single-player runs that worker is mostly idle
     and the draw call itself takes 0.63 ms. In the fork's four-player run the
     worker is busy again. That the queries make the driver wait for its
     worker is my reading of this pattern, not something the profile shows
     directly; removing the queries will confirm or refute it. (It held:
     see FORK-088.)
2. **The first-person arm mesh is rebuilt every frame** on the game thread
   (`portWardrobeRenderNode`, `portArmMeshBuildJoinedSurface`, `armCopyPart`):
   0.33 ms a frame, 0.56 ms with four players, 0.21 ms of it inside C runtime
   calls made directly by `portWardrobeRenderNode`. It is the main reason the
   fork's game code costs three times stock's.
3. **HUD rectangles** cost 0.26 ms a frame against stock's 0.03 ms, and
   1.15 ms a frame in the browser's four-player run.
4. **Per-triangle setup** (`gfx_sp_tri1` itself) takes twice stock's time.
5. At default settings the reflection cube adds 0.68 ms and the retained
   draw (`gl_ret_draw`) 0.33 ms on the render thread.
6. A benchmark artifact, not a game cost: unpaced, the game thread polls input
   in a spin, and `videoGetPad` spends most of that in the C runtime. Paced
   play polls once a tick.

The profile reports and frame logs are local (`build_win/bench-results`,
ignored by Git); these figures are the record.

**Not done yet:** GPU time per render pass (the samplers see processor time
only), a profile of the browser at default settings, and Linux. The sampler is
Windows only; elsewhere `portProfileWrite` is an empty function.

**Shared hooks for later merges:** none in upstream files. `port_bench.c`
(FORK-085) calls `portProfileWrite`; `port_console_env.h` lists `GE_PROFILE`
and `GE_PROFILE_HZ`.

**Sources:** [port_profile.c](port/src/port_profile.c),
[bench_profile.py](scripts/port/bench/bench_profile.py),
[bench_profile_web.py](scripts/port/bench/bench_profile_web.py),
[bench-audit.mjs](web/tools/bench-audit.mjs),
[the guide](scripts/port/benchmarks.md#profiling).

**Checks:** `python scripts/port/test_bench_profile.py` (11 tests: sample
parsing, naming, the tick window, per-frame arithmetic, the pump's set-aside,
difference ranking, and the browser profile's tables) and
`python scripts/port/test_bench.py` (36 tests) passed. The Windows build and
the stock reference build passed and ran profiled: frame rates with the
sampler on matched unprofiled runs (Cradle, stock 889 and fork 298 frames a
second), and idle threads stopped appearing once the cycle count was re-read
after each resume. The browser runtime built, the site assembled, and two
profiled browser runs completed. The Bright Builds checks and the settings
placement check passed, and the review gallery regenerated with no changed
image. Linux and Steam Deck builds were not built or run for this change.

**Input idioms:** no menu, prompt or setting was added.

### FORK-086 — Room Seams: level seams no longer show the sky

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-15 after the owner reported thin blue
lines along floor edges, wall feet and the road's centre line in Dam. The
owner play-tested the first version (below) as
`build_win/IronSights-Seams.exe` and still saw the lines; this version
replaced it the same day, and the owner play-tested it the same way and
approved it. Built for Windows and the browser (`web_build.py video`).
Linux and Steam Deck builds were not run locally.

**Cause (inherited, made visible by FORK-082):** Rare's room meshes have
T-junctions whose middle vertex sits off the long edge it should lie on. At
one of the owner's spots (room 132, x 17151, z 19170) a floor triangle's
corner is 0.65 units from the barrier foot it should meet (eye-space units,
where Bond's eye is about 186 above the floor), so a thin wedge of the floor
plane belongs to no triangle and the sky drawn behind the room shows through.
The gap has a size in the world: close up it is several pixels wide (about 5
at 1920x1080 there), and further away it shrinks to a dashed sub-pixel
sliver. A build of `d9cd84f` (2026-11-01, before this month's rendering work)
shows the same lines at the owner's four spots and at the tunnel wall below,
so the gaps are not new. Tone Mapping (FORK-082, the same day) brightens
them from dark navy to vivid cyan: at the tunnel wall, against a surrounding
brightness of about 22, the crack went from 53 with Tone Mapping off to about
95 with it on (Clarity, Sharpen and Brightness each add a little, the tone
curve the rest). That is why it looked like a regression.

**What it does:** each opaque triangle of a room's display list also draws a
backing copy. The copy is the triangle grown, in its own plane, by 2 world
units along each edge that no other opaque triangle of the room has, and it is
drawn 16 units (eight times the grow) further back in depth. Every real
surface wins the depth test against it, so it only shows where nothing was
drawn: the seams. The real triangles are untouched.

- **Which edges grow:** a room's first draw learns its edges, keyed by the two
  corners' integer model positions (`gfx_seam_edge_key`), counting every
  opaque triangle of the list before culling. An edge two triangles share
  (a box's corner edges, a floor's inner diagonals) stays; an edge only one
  triangle has (the long side of a T-junction, a floor's edge at a wall foot,
  a room's border) grows. That first draw takes no copy. A different stage
  in the tag forgets every room.
- **The grow:** each corner goes to where its two (moved or unmoved) edge
  lines meet, capped at three times the grow from where it was so a needle
  corner does not spike (`gfx_seam_grow_plane`). Positions are camera-relative
  (modelview times the vertex), in world units; the copy's clip position is
  that point times the projection.
- **The depth:** only the copy's clip z changes, to the depth of the point 16
  units further along the view axis (`gfx_seam_push_depth`), so its screen
  shape, perspective and fog stay as grown. The copy is first clipped to the
  near plane itself (`gfx_seam_clip_near`, every float interpolated as the
  rasterizer would), so every corner is in front and takes the push; a
  quadrilateral is drawn as two triangles.
- **Which draws:** depth-tested, opaque, not decals and not cutouts. Dam's
  opaque lists use the one-minus-alpha blender with `ALPHA_CVG_SEL` and
  `A_IN`, whose alpha is pixel coverage, which the renderer draws opaque, so
  they count as opaque. Truly blended draws, `CVG_X_ALPHA` texture-edge and
  alpha-threshold cutouts (a copy behind a fence would double its pattern),
  decals (and so they do not mark a floor edge as shared), texture
  rectangles, the rooms' translucent lists, props, characters, guns and hands
  take no copy, so the first-person arm contracts are untouched.
- **What it costs in looks:** at an unshared edge whose background is more
  than 16 units behind it (a mesh border against the sky), the copy shows as
  a rim of up to 2 units. None was visible in the captures below.
- **Tuning:** `GE_SEAM_GROW=<world units>` (0 to 16, default 2) for
  diagnosis; 0 turns it off. No menu setting: it fixes a defect.
- **Not covered:** the room cache's replay paths (`room_cache = 1` or `2`,
  default 0 on PC, 2 on the Xbox) draw rooms without the interpreter's
  triangle path, so they keep the seams.

**Replaced the same day:** the first version grew every opaque room triangle
by half a pixel in clip space (a conservative-rasterization grow). It closed
the dashed sub-pixel crack at the tunnel wall but not the owner's lines,
which are gaps of a fixed world size and several pixels wide up close. A
grown copy at a small fixed depth offset was tried next: it closed the lines
but overhung convex corners (a barrier's top face in front of its side and
over the floor below), showing shards and spikes. Pushing the copy back
fixed the shards on faces but not over far backgrounds, and moving vertices
along their view rays misplaced triangles that cross the eye plane. Growing
only unshared edges, with the near clip and the z-only push, removed all of
those.

**Hooks:** `bg.c`'s `bgRenderRoomPrimary` brackets the room's opaque
`gSPDisplayList` with `portRoomSeamsTag(gdl, 1, room)` / `(gdl, 0, room)`
(inside `#ifndef TARGET_N64`). That is a G_NOOP tag 0x68 that
`port_room_seams.c` emits with the room (bits 1-10) and the stage's low byte
(bits 11-18, from `bossGetStageNum`). In `gfx_pc.cpp`:
- `gfx_run_dl` reads the tag and drives the room's learning state;
  `gfx_start_frame` closes the span;
- `gfx_sp_vertex` stores the camera-relative and model positions in the
  `LoadedVertex` (`seam_eye`, `seam_ob`; separate from the glint and glass
  `eye`);
- `gfx_sp_tri1` counts edges at entry while a room learns, prepares the grown
  corners before emission, and appends the clipped, pushed copy after the
  triangle is counted, flushing the batch as usual.

**Input:** none; it is a rendering fix with no row or binding.

**Sources:** [tag](port/src/port_room_seams.c) and its
[header](port/include/port_room_seams.h), the
[helpers](port/fast3d/gfx_seam_grow.h), the hooks in `src/game/bg.c` and
`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`, `GE_SEAM_GROW` in `port/src/port_console_env.h`,
and the [unit test](scripts/port/test_room_seams.c)
([runner](scripts/port/test_room_seams.sh)).

**Checks (2026-11-15):**
- `test_room_seams.sh` (ROM-free, in the `goldeneye` Docker image) passes:
  - every grown edge sits the grow outside its line, in the triangle's
    plane;
  - with one edge named, the opposite corner stays and the other two slide
    along their unmoved edges;
  - no edge, no area or no grow declines, and a needle corner is capped;
  - edge keys match in either order and differ for different edges;
  - the near clip keeps the part in front as a quad with interpolated floats,
    drops a triangle behind the eye and keeps one in front whole;
  - for a GL perspective, the pushed depth equals the depth of the point that
    far back, the near plane's w is found, and a corner behind the eye keeps
    its depth.
- **The owner's four spots** (`GE_SPAWNXYZ` with their coordinates and
  pitch, 1920x1080, their `[display]` settings without HDR Output, a pulsed B
  press to skip the intro). Strong-blue pixels in the left two thirds of the
  frame, baseline (`GE_SEAM_GROW=0`) then fix:

  | Spot | Before | After | Peak blue excess |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | room 132, x 17151, z 19170 | 5,829 | 22 | 98 → 23 |
  | room 132, x 16385, z 18690 | 2,073 | 1 | 86 → 16 |
  | room 132, x 15650, z 18810 | 3,798 | 0 | 102 → 7 |
  | room 126, x 14338, z 18198 | 3,587 | 274 | 90 → 18 |

  The pixels left at the last spot are dark (brightness 19, against the
  line's 137), not the line. Crops showed the lines gone and the barriers
  as in the baseline.
- **Tunnel wall:** `audit_graphics.ps1`, `GE_AUTOSTICK=0,70,700,3000` from
  Dam's start, Bond walks into the wall at room 132 (x 16524, z 17091). Crack
  pixels (blue more than 12 above red and green) went from about 200 to 0.
- **Elsewhere on Dam** (the start yard down the road and against the cliffs,
  the dark tunnel, the far tunnel by the dam), copy on and off side by side:
  the same apart from guards and the sky moving, and the cliff silhouettes
  against the sky are identical.
- **Performance:** 20,000 uncapped frames at the road spot took 99 and 109 s
  without the copy and 122 and 93 s with it (about 200 fps either way); the
  run-to-run noise on this machine is larger than any difference.
- The owner's play-test in Dam, from `build_win` with their own settings,
  found the lines gone.
- Not yet checked: other levels, the room cache paths, HDR Output, a browser
  device, and the cost on phones.

### FORK-085 — Benchmark suite: fixed-work frame timing against stock

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-15 at the owner's request, as the first step
of performance work (measure, then profile, then optimize). It covers the
Windows build and, with its own runner, the browser build. No game behaviour
changes: the frame log is off unless `GE_BENCH` is set.

Inherited behaviour: upstream has no benchmark. It does have the pieces one
needs, all present at the 1.0.2b baseline and reused here unchanged: the input
recorder and replayer (`GE_INPUTREC` / `GE_INPUTPLAY`, `port/src/inputrec.c`),
`GE_SEED`, `GE_STAGE`, `GE_MP`, `GE_FIXEDTICK`, `GE_NOSLEEP`, `GE_TICKHZ`, and
the hitch log's per-frame split of render, swap and game time
(`port/src/hitchlog.c`, called once per presented frame by `gfx_sdl2.cpp`).

**What it does:** `python scripts/port/bench/bench.py run` times builds on
fixed work and prints a comparison; [the benchmark guide](scripts/port/benchmarks.md)
is the reference. Each run plays one scenario in fixed tick, unpaced mode
(`GE_FIXEDTICK`, `GE_NOSLEEP`, `tickhz` 0, no vsync, no frame cap): every frame
advances the game one 60 Hz tick and draws as fast as it can, so a run draws
the same frames on any machine and in any build. The measured window is 3,600
ticks, starting 300 ticks into the mission. Runs are repeated (five by
default) with the builds interleaved, and the report gives medians and marks a
change as real only when it exceeds the runs' own slowest-to-fastest range.

- **Frame log** (`GE_BENCH=<file>`, [port_bench.c](port/src/port_bench.c)): one
  row per presented frame with the present-to-present interval, renderer time,
  swap, limiter, longest stretch of game code, audio, pacer sleep, draw
  batches, stage, game tick and the five timed load-event kinds. Rows are held
  in memory (60 bytes each, 200,000 by default, `GE_BENCH_MAX`) and written
  once. `GE_BENCH_END=<tick>[,<stage>]` writes the file and leaves the process
  when the mission reaches that tick (`_Exit`, after flushing every stream;
  the browser build writes the file and stays up). The one hook is a call from
  `portHitchFrame`, which already holds every value.
- **Scenarios** ([scenarios.json](scripts/port/bench/scenarios.json)): Dam,
  Streets, Depot, Jungle and Cradle, and four-player Temple. A one-off survey
  of 19 missions with the same route picked the heaviest (Cradle, Streets,
  Depot, Jungle); Dam is kept as the familiar opening.
- **Routes** are generated from a description (walk forward, turn the camera by
  a fixed list of angles between straight legs, fire in bursts) into
  `GE_INPUTPLAY` pad and mouse-look records, so the input is a function of the
  game tick and identical for every build. In the four-player scenario player
  1 follows the route and the others stand at their spawns.
- **Presets**: `default` runs each build as it ships; `matched` sets the
  settings both builds share to stock's defaults (`msaa`, `anisotropy`,
  `filter_2d`, `filtering`) and turns off `shiny_weapons`, `glass_reflections`,
  `tone_mapping` and `baked_lighting`.
- **Reference builds** ([stock.py](scripts/port/bench/stock.py)): exports a
  commit (by default the inherited baseline) into `build_win/bench-<name>`,
  copies this checkout's ignored generated assets, and builds it in the project
  container with the same flags. It adds this checkout's `port_bench.c` (and
  the profiler, FORK-087), the `hitchlog.c` call
  and, for stock, an early return in `waitForNextFrame` so `GE_FIXEDTICK` does
  not wait on the clock (the fork has had that since the 2026-11-06 gallery
  speed-up, FORK-022); a commit that already has one keeps its own. The same
  script builds a "before" executable from any commit, so no old executable is
  kept as a backup.
- **Host guard**: before each run the runner waits for other game processes to
  exit, repeats a run one overlapped (up to three times) and reports how many
  stayed overlapped, with processor use across the machine during the runs.
  Each run uses its own folder, `midas.ini` and executable copy under
  `build_win/bench-run-*`, deleted when measured; the player's game, settings
  and saves are not touched. Runs use SDL's dummy audio driver.

- **Browser runner**: `bench_web.py plan` writes the same runs as data (the
  environment, `midas.ini`, generated route and tick window of each);
  [bench-audit.mjs](web/tools/bench-audit.mjs) (`bun run audit:bench`) plays
  them in one Playwright browser profile, reloading the page per run, and saves
  each frame log; `bench_web.py collect` turns one or more such folders into
  the same results file and report. In the browser the renderer shares the
  game's thread, so the metrics take its time off the game's stretch, and the
  results add `work_ms` (render plus game). An unpaced browser run hands the
  browser its event loop at the top of every pump; `pcsched.c` now counts that
  wait as pacer sleep (browser build only), or it was charged to the game code
  before it.

- **Smoke check and switches** (added with FORK-088): `bench.py run --smoke`
  is three scenarios, every preset and three repeats, the check `AGENTS.md`
  now asks of any change to what is drawn or computed every frame. A build
  can carry environment of its own (`label=path@NAME=VALUE,...`), so one
  executable can be measured against itself with a switch flipped, and
  `bench_web.py plan --env` does the same for a browser session.

**Findings while building it** (they shape how the numbers must be read):

- A hidden window ran about 30% slower than a visible one on the development
  machine (296 against 418 frames a second on the same Dam run), so measured
  runs show their window.
- The game's scripted drivers (`GE_DRIVE`, `GE_MPDRIVE`) count controller
  polls. Unpaced, the pump polls tens of thousands of times a second, so those
  scripts gave different input on every run (the four-player scenario's draw
  counts diverged from tick 115 with them, and matched tick for tick without
  them). They are not used. `GE_DRIVE=1` also walks Bond into the first wall
  and leaves him there, so it was no use as a route either.
- Replay matches by tick, so a generated route puts the fork and stock at the
  same position and view on the same tick (checked by screenshots at tick 1,400
  and 2,800 in Facility).
- Fixed tick makes every frame do a whole 60 Hz game tick; in normal uncapped
  play most frames are sub-ticks, so the in-game counter reads higher. The
  suite compares cost per frame of full work.

**Baseline, stock 1.0.2b against Iron Sights at `21ccff3`** (2026-11-15; the
development laptop, an i7-10870H with an RTX 3070 Laptop GPU; 1920x1080
visible window; five repeats, medians; 120 runs):

| Scenario | Stock fps (default / matched) | Fork fps, default | Fork fps, matched | Stock render / game ms, matched | Fork render / game ms, matched |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| dam-walk | 1168 / 1230 | 481 (-59%) | 788 (-36%) | 0.53 / 0.16 | 1.05 / 0.44 |
| streets-fight | 917 / 1068 | 329 (-64%) | 562 (-47%) | 0.66 / 0.13 | 1.52 / 0.44 |
| depot-fight | 979 / 1181 | 367 (-62%) | 645 (-45%) | 0.56 / 0.12 | 1.28 / 0.42 |
| jungle-fight | 912 / 1033 | 402 (-56%) | 563 (-46%) | 0.75 / 0.20 | 1.51 / 0.58 |
| cradle-fight | 718 / 834 | 294 (-59%) | 449 (-46%) | 0.95 / 0.16 | 1.97 / 0.57 |
| temple-4p | 907 / 1065 | 306 (-66%) | 764 (-28%) | 0.70 / 0.15 | 1.24 / 0.89 |

- At default settings the fork draws 34-44% of stock's frames a second on
  every scenario. Its 1% lows fall the same way (91-174 against 205-439).
- With settings matched and the fork's graphics features off it draws 53-72%.
  The renderer then takes about twice stock's time per frame and the game code
  about three times (six times in four-player split screen). That gap remains
  with those settings off, so it comes from fork work the preset does not
  switch off; profiling has to say which.
- The fork's default-on graphics (2x MSAA, anisotropy, Tone Mapping, Baked
  Lighting, the reflections) take a further 29-60% of its own frame rate.
- Stage loads were 17-48% longer at default settings (54-128 ms against
  36-109 ms) and equal with settings matched.
- The fork still drew 294-481 frames a second at its defaults on this machine;
  the cost matters on weaker hardware and for headroom.

Read the default-preset numbers as approximate. Two other sessions were
building and running game audits on the machine: processor use across it was
41% in the median run and peaked at 94%, and average fps ranged by up to 64%
between repeats of one build. The matched preset ran in a quieter spell
(median 34%, ranges of 8-22%). Twenty runs were repeated because another game
process overlapped them; none stayed overlapped. The ratios agree across
scenarios and both presets, so the direction and rough size hold; the
individual figures need a rerun on an idle machine. The results file is local
(`build_win/bench-results/baseline.json`, ignored by Git) and is not needed
later: before and after are always measured together.

**Browser baseline, Iron Sights at `bf052df`** (2026-11-15; the same laptop;
Chromium 157 headless on ANGLE/Direct3D 11, 1280x960 canvas; two repeats,
medians; 24 runs; processor time per frame in milliseconds):

| Scenario | Browser render / game, default | Browser render / game, matched | Windows fork render / game, matched |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| dam-walk | 10.06 / 0.67 | 8.48 / 0.59 | 1.05 / 0.44 |
| streets-fight | 11.83 / 0.76 | 9.78 / 0.62 | 1.52 / 0.44 |
| depot-fight | 11.12 / 0.74 | 9.49 / 0.60 | 1.28 / 0.42 |
| jungle-fight | 11.64 / 0.86 | 10.05 / 0.74 | 1.51 / 0.58 |
| cradle-fight | 12.20 / 0.76 | 10.44 / 0.67 | 1.97 / 0.57 |
| temple-4p | 6.58 / 0.96 | 2.69 / 0.80 | 1.24 / 0.89 |

- A single-player frame costs the browser 10.7-13.0 ms of processor time at
  default settings (render plus game), against the 16.7 ms a 60 Hz display
  allows, and 9.1-11.1 ms with settings matched. A 120 Hz display is out of
  reach.
- Nearly all of it is the renderer: 8.5-10.4 ms with the graphics features
  off, five to eight times the Windows build's figure for the same frames.
  The game code is close to the Windows build's (0.6-1.0 ms).
- The graphics features add 1.6-2.1 ms a frame in single player and 3.9 ms in
  four-player split screen.
- Four-player split screen is the cheapest scenario in the browser (2.69 ms
  of renderer with settings matched) although it draws four views. Something
  the single-player scenarios draw and it does not is expensive there; the
  profiling step starts with that.
- These are far steadier than the Windows numbers: render time ranged by 0-4%
  between repeats. Average fps (44-58 at defaults) is not comparable with
  Windows: the unpaced browser run waits on the event loop twice a frame,
  about 4.8 ms each, and the window sizes differ.

**Not done yet:** a paced mode for frame-time consistency at a fixed rate,
hand-played routes (a scenario takes one as `route_file`), Linux, and a guard
against other programs in the browser runner. Only headless Chromium was
measured; Firefox, Safari and phones were not. Stock's repeats of the fight
scenarios vary by a few draw batches on some ticks, well inside the report's
tolerance.

**Shared hooks for later merges:** [hitchlog.c](port/src/hitchlog.c) (inherited)
gains one call to `portBenchFrame` after it takes its counters; keep it there
if upstream changes that function, and keep `stock.py`'s anchor text in step
(`test_bench.py` checks both). `port_console_env.h` lists the three new
`GE_BENCH*` names. [pcsched.c](port/src/pcsched.c) times the unpaced browser
yield at the top of `portPumpEvents` (inside its existing `__EMSCRIPTEN__`
block). No upstream file changes otherwise.

**Sources:** [port_bench.c](port/src/port_bench.c),
[bench.py](scripts/port/bench/bench.py) (runner),
[bench_plan.py](scripts/port/bench/bench_plan.py) (settings, environment,
routes, host checks), [bench_metrics.py](scripts/port/bench/bench_metrics.py)
(numbers), [bench_report.py](scripts/port/bench/bench_report.py) (Markdown),
[stock.py](scripts/port/bench/stock.py),
[bench_web.py](scripts/port/bench/bench_web.py) and
[bench-audit.mjs](web/tools/bench-audit.mjs) (browser),
[scenarios.json](scripts/port/bench/scenarios.json),
[the guide](scripts/port/benchmarks.md) and `AGENTS.md`'s repo-local guidance.

**Checks:** `python scripts/port/test_bench.py` (36 tests: metrics, run planning
for Windows and the browser, route generation, host checks, report, stock
patching, and that the fork's
hook and the inventory's baseline match what `stock.py` uses) passed. The
Windows build passed and the frame log was exercised by every run above: a
1,500-tick Dam run replayed twice gave identical draw counts on every tick; the
four-player scenario did the same in both builds; mean draws per frame agreed
to two decimals across all five repeats of every build and scenario. Stock
1.0.2b built from the export with the three harness additions and ran every
scenario. The browser runtime built (`web_build.py video`), the site
assembled, and the browser runner completed all 24 runs with no page errors.
The Bright Builds checks and the settings placement check passed, and the
review gallery regenerated with no changed image. Linux and Steam Deck builds
were not built or run for this change.

**Input idioms:** no menu, prompt or setting was added; the suite is a
development tool run from a shell.

### FORK-084 — Debug Position: the position readout as an in-game setting

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-15 at the owner's request. Built for
Windows (an isolated build directory) and the browser
(`web_build.py video`). Not yet play-tested by the owner. Linux and Steam
Deck builds were not run locally.

Inherited behaviour: the decompiled game keeps Rare's "testing man pos"
readout (`sub_GAME_7F08AAE8`, `bondview2.c`): a dark strip across the top of
the view with the room id, x / y / z, and the heading. It shows while
`get_debug_testingmanpos_flag()` (`debugmenu_handler.c`) is set; the Debug Pos
cheat sets that flag. Earlier fork work added the pitch (`P`) and dropped the
compass prefix from the heading (`H`) so a spot can be copied into
`GE_SPAWNXYZ`, and `GE_DEBUGPOS=1` set the flag once as each stage loaded
(`portDebugPosApply`, `lv.c`), so it only took effect at launch.

**What it does:** **Gameplay > Iron Sights > System > Debug Position**
(`[display] show_debug_pos`, default 0) shows or hides the readout from the
next frame, in a running mission too. The row is in the System subsection
of both the Options folder and the watch, and the console's `cl_debugpos`
(an alias of `cl_show_debug_pos`) sets it too. `GE_DEBUGPOS` still overrides the
setting either way: unset leaves it to the setting, `0` hides the readout, and
any other value shows it (as before, anything not starting with `0` turns it on).
The override is read once; the setting keeps its saved value under it. The
Debug Pos cheat keeps its own flag, and the readout shows while either is on.
Turning the cheat off while the setting is on leaves the readout up. The
readout's look in native builds is unchanged.

**Browser:** the readout and the `show_input` row under it start no nearer
the window edge than the safe-area inset (`portWebSafeAreaTopLeft`, FORK-025)
reaches. Only the left/top starting point is clamped. The FPS counter, by
contrast, is moved in by the whole inset. Vertically the rows also start below
the top-left corner's FPS counter, mission clock and NOCLIP label
(`portHudDebugRowsTop`, FORK-015), keeping the same safe-area floor. In a wide frame the readout already
starts inside the 4:3 area, past an iPhone notch, so it stays put. Adding the
whole inset there would push the line right for nothing, and in a stretched
4:3 frame it would push `P` off the right edge. The full-width strip behind
the text still runs under the notch, which hides nothing. Native builds are
unchanged.

**Hooks:** `get_debug_testingmanpos_flag` returns TRUE when
`portDebugPosShown()` does (inside `#ifndef TARGET_N64`), so the three
`bondview2.c` reads and the cheat's checks see the setting with no other
upstream change. `lv.c`'s `portDebugPosApply` was removed. The readout's six
`viGetViewLeft()` x positions take a local `debug_left` and its y a
`debug_top` (`portDebugRowsClearSafeArea`). The option is registered in
`joy_port.c`'s dispatch, `port_options.c` (after Fog, display category), the
folder's System rows (`front.c`) and the watch's (`port_watchpages.c`), with
help in `port_option_help.c` (also named in the System page description),
`tools/midas_ini_help.txt`, the default midas.ini writer (`video.c`), the
console alias and help line (`port_console.c`) and README.md. `GE_DEBUGPOS`
stays in `port_console_env.h`, and the launcher's "Testing man pos"
checkbox (`tools/GELauncher.cs`) still sets it, as the override.

**Input:** an ordinary option row. Keyboard, mouse, gamepad and browser touch
already confirm and adjust it as they do every toggle. The readout itself
takes no input.

**Sources:** [header](port/include/port_debug_pos.h),
[setting](port/src/port_debug_pos.c) and the
[ROM-free test](scripts/port/test_debug_pos.c) (included by `test_noclip.c`,
run by `test_ads.sh`): off by default, a toggle row, shown and hidden live,
`GE_DEBUGPOS=1` and `=0` overriding a setting of off and on.

**Checks:** `test_ads.sh`, `test_states.sh`, `test_hud.sh` and
`test_web_menu_pointer.sh` pass (`test_web_touch.sh` needs `emcc` on the path
and `test_start_input.sh` needs SDL headers; neither ran).
`settings_placement.py` and `bun scripts/bright-builds-check.ts all` pass.
The Windows build and `web_build.py video` compile cleanly. ROM captures on
Dam with the isolated Windows exe: `GE_CONCMD="cl_debugpos 1"` set from
the title screen over `show_debug_pos=0` shows the readout as before
(`ROOM135  X 20198  Y 60  Z 16902  H 90  P -4`). `show_debug_pos=1` with
`GE_DEBUGPOS=0` hides it, and the default hides it. Harness runs never write
midas.ini (`GE_WINDOW`), so saving was not captured. It uses the same
`portIniWriteStrs` path as Fog. A scripted mid-mission run toggled it from the
watch (`GE_INPUTPLAY` Start presses, `GE_WATCHPAGE=3,13,13,1,1,1` on the System
page's row): with `show_debug_pos=0` the readout appeared the frame the row
read ON, over the open watch, and stayed after the watch closed. With
`show_debug_pos=1` it disappeared the same way. Not yet play-tested by hand.
The browser safe-area clamp has not been seen on an iPhone. The hand gallery was regenerated with the isolated exe,
because `src/` and `port/` C files are its render inputs.

### FORK-083 — Headshots Only: a mission modifier with its own records

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-15 at the owner's request and committed to
`main` with the owner's approval after six rounds of review of the
difficulty page (see the review history below). Built for Windows into the
main `build_win/IronSights.exe`. After the push the owner reported playing
several Headshots Only missions with the Windows build and that the mode
works. Linux, Steam Deck and browser builds were not run locally.

Inherited behaviour: `handles_shot_actors` (`chraction.c`) scales a hit's damage
by body part (head x4, chest x2, limbs x1, hat and held gun x0) and every hit
part hurts. The save keeps one best time per mission and difficulty (Agent to
00 Agent; 007 is never recorded), only for runs without cheats, and the
difficulty page marks completed difficulties with a red checkmark.

**What it does:** **Headshots Only** (off by default) makes the player's hits
on a guard do damage only on the head. Any other part (feet to chest, and
the crouched melee's general hit) leaves the guard's health alone: the guard
still flinches (`chrSetHiddenToRandom`, as an invincible character does) and
notices (`CHRFLAG_WAS_HIT` is set before the check), the hit still counts in
the shot register and the debrief hit map, and the confirmed hit sound
(FORK-043) still plays, but no hit marker shows, no hurt yelp plays and the
guard is not staggered into its argh animation. The function returns TRUE, so
a bullet still leaves its blood decal and a thrown knife still stops. Hat and
held-gun hits keep stock handling (no damage either way, the hat still
knocked off, the steel helmet still ricochets; a moonraker helmet already
counts as the head). Thrown knives report a real hit part, so a knife to the
head counts.

**Headshots Melee** (`headshots_only_melee`, **Allowed** by default) covers
melee, which never reports a head hit (`chraiFistAttackHandler` hits the
chest): Allowed keeps stock damage for `ITEM_FIST` and `ITEM_KNIFE`, so missions
that start unarmed (Bunker 2's cell, Archives' interrogation) stay playable, as
the owner asked; Blocked makes melee do nothing too.

**Deliberately unaffected:** explosions (`chrlvExplosionDamage` cannot tell the
player's grenade from a guard's, so blocking it would make guards immune to
their own; this includes Explosive Rounds' splash, FORK-078), guard-on-guard
fire and scripted AI damage (`isPlayer` false), and players in multiplayer
(`PROP_TYPE_VIEWER`).

**When it applies:** `lv.c` latches the setting as a non-title stage loads,
only for solo play (`gamemode == GAMEMODE_SOLO`, one player) outside demo
playback (`get_is_ramrom_flag`). A change made from the pause watch applies to
the next mission, so a run is either all Headshots Only or not. The front end
is not a stage load, so the latch still describes the mission just played on
its debrief. Headshots Melee is read live: it only relaxes the rule.

**Records:** `file.c`'s `end_of_mission_briefing` records a headshot completion
right after the stock save does, under the stock rule (not 007, no cheats
active), so a big-head cheat cannot earn one. Records live in
`Data/Saves/headshots.ini` (`[headshots_only]`, `version=1`, one
`fN_mNN_dD=seconds` line per folder, mission and difficulty; 1023 marks an
untimed completion, as in the stock save), because the N64 save has no room.
Only a faster run replaces a record. `file2.c` clears a folder's records when
the folder is erased and copies them with **Copy** to the folder it fills.
The difficulty page shows a record only where the save has its own completion
of that difficulty, so a replaced, imported or reset `eeprom.bin` never shows a
stale time. Harness runs (`GE_NOINISAVE` or `GE_WINDOW`) read the file but never
write it. In the browser the file is in the persisted set and save backups
(`web/src/backup.ts`, `web/src/persistent-files.ts`).

**Where it shows:**
- Each mission's difficulty page: a **Headshots Only: ON/OFF** row on the
  Reinforcements line, from the page's left margin. The label is black and the
  value is printed after it separately: **ON** in the dossier's emphasis red
  (`0xA00000FF`, as the cheat badges), **OFF** black. The Reinforcements row
  does the same for a level above Original (FORK-081). Pointing at it
  highlights it with the difficulty rows' box and the confirm press flips it
  (A, Start or Z on a pad, Enter, a mouse click, a browser tap), with the
  options' click sound; it calls the options table's `portOptStep`, so it saves
  `midas.ini`. Browser touch sends cursor motion and A, all it needs, so it
  has no native touch context. Both bottom rows moved up from y 300 to 295
  (FORK-081) so the highlight clears the FORK-016 cheat footer below them.
- Two best-time columns, always shown whatever the setting: the stock records
  under a red checkmark heading (the stock checkmark texture in place of
  FORK-032's **Best Time** text, placed so its bottom point is over the
  column's centre: the texture's centre sits 4.2 units right of it), then the
  Headshots Only records under the crosshair-and-head mark. The mark is a ring
  around a head and shoulders with four straight ticks that cross the ring,
  each showing as much of itself inside the ring as outside it (0.28 of the
  ring's radius each way, clear of the head), with a stroke 0.17 of the
  radius. The head is centred on the ring's centre and the shoulders below it
  meet the ring's inner edge. On the heading the
  ring's radius is 6.6 native units and the ticks reach about 9, so the mark
  spans about the 18-unit square around the checkmark heading (measured: the
  checkmark 16.5 x 17.9, the mark 18.5 x 18.5). Both are drawn in the
  checkmark's red with the overlay ellipse and rectangle primitives. With
  the row checkmarks gone, the stock column moved left into the freed space
  (centres at x 300 and 362; the difficulty names and cheat-target badges end
  near x 238). 007 reads `--:--` in both.
- The port no longer draws the stock checkmark on each completed difficulty
  row (`front.c` keeps it for N64): the times say the same. To keep that true,
  a time at the save's 1023-second cap, which FORK-032 showed as `--:--`, now
  reads `17:03+` in either column, as the Mission Timer's BEST does.
- Owner review history: the first draft put a crosshair mark beside each
  completed row's checkmark and swapped the one Best Time column to the
  Headshots Only records while the mode was on. The first review asked for
  both columns with icon headings and a smaller ring and figure with longer
  ticks; the second removed the row checkmarks and marks as redundant with the
  times, enlarged the heading's mark, ran its ticks inside the ring, and
  centred the checkmark's point on its column; the third moved the stock
  column left (from x 314) and made the ticks equal inside and outside the
  ring, keeping the ring and figure's size; the fourth sized the heading's mark
  to the checkmark's square, thinned its stroke (from 0.24 of the radius),
  lowered the figure so the head is about central (it was 0.2 of the radius
  above), widened the row highlight over the times and hid the cheat footer
  where the row badge already shows the cheat; the fifth extended the
  highlight over the cheat badge and lowered the figure one more screen pixel
  (0.05 of the radius at 1280x960) to centre the head exactly; the sixth
  turned both bottom rows' values red when not the default.
- A highlighted difficulty row's box runs past both time columns to x 386
  (`PORT_MISSION_TIMES_ROW_RIGHT`; the stock box ended at x 240, after the
  difficulty name), and on the cheat's row it runs 8 units lower (to row y +
  203, from + 195) to take in the **CHEAT TARGET** / **CHEAT UNLOCKED** badge
  drawn under the name, at the owner's request after the fourth review. The
  rows were already selected across the page's whole width (the stock hit
  test reads only the cursor's height), so only the box changed.
- The FORK-016 cheat footer (`CHEAT TO UNLOCK` and the required difficulty and
  time) shows on the difficulty page only when the cheat's difficulty is still
  locked, so its row and the row's **CHEAT TARGET** badge are hidden; otherwise
  the badge says the same. The mission grid keeps the footer.
- The debrief: the mark and **HEADSHOTS ONLY** in the dossier's emphasis red
  after **STATISTICS** when the mission just played ran the mode.
- **Gameplay > Iron Sights > Enemies** (both the Options folder and the watch):
  **Headshots Only** and **Headshots Melee** after Reinforcements.

**Shared hooks in upstream files** (all `#ifndef TARGET_N64`): `chraction.c`
`handles_shot_actors` (the check, after the body-part multipliers), `lv.c` (the
stage latch, beside the MP stats reset), `file.c` `end_of_mission_briefing`
(the record), `file2.c` `fileDeleteSaveForFolder` and
`fileCopyFolderToFirstFree` (erase and copy), and `front.c` (the difficulty
page's hit test, confirm and draw calls, the stock row checkmarks limited to
N64, the highlight box's right edge, the cheat footer's condition, the Enemies
sheet rows and the debrief badge).

**Sources:** rules in [port_headshots_only.h](port/include/port_headshots_only.h),
settings and latch in [port_headshots_only.c](port/src/port_headshots_only.c),
records in [port_headshots_records.c](port/src/port_headshots_records.c), the
difficulty-page row, marks and debrief badge in
[port_headshots_menu.c](port/src/port_headshots_menu.c), the two best-time columns in
[port_mission_times.c](port/src/port_mission_times.c), plus
[port_options.c](port/src/port_options.c), [joy_port.c](port/src/joy_port.c),
[port_watchpages.c](port/src/port_watchpages.c),
[help](port/src/port_option_help.c), [default ini](port/src/video.c),
[settings reference](tools/midas_ini_help.txt) and [README](README.md).
`ge: headshots:` lines on stderr log each recorded completion.

**Checks:**
- [test_headshots_only.c](scripts/port/test_headshots_only.c), run by
  [test_ads.sh](scripts/port/test_ads.sh) through `test_tracers.c`: defaults,
  option rows and value texts, the difficulty page's wrapping step, the solo
  and demo latch, every body part blocked for bullets and thrown knives, head,
  hat and gun untouched, guards' hits untouched, and melee under both melee
  settings.
- [test_headshots_records.c](scripts/port/test_headshots_records.c), run by
  [test_mission_times.sh](scripts/port/test_mission_times.sh) with the real save
  codec in both Unlock All variants: no record without the latch, only faster
  runs replace one, the untimed clamp, 007 and out-of-range rejection, the stock
  completion gate, the column text, the file round trip with unknown lines
  ignored, and folder erase and copy. (The `file2.c` call sites write the
  eeprom, so they are checked in game rather than there.)
- `web/src/backup.test.ts` allows `Data/Saves/headshots.ini`; 37 tests pass.
- The settings placement check and Bright Builds checks pass; the Windows build
  succeeded with no implicit declarations. The hand gallery regenerated from
  that build with 0 of 108 image cells changed (only its source fingerprint).
- In game, [audit_hitmap.ps1](scripts/port/audit_hitmap.ps1) (new
  `-HeadshotsOnly` and `-BlockMelee` switches) fired 120 probe bullets at Dam's
  guards: with the mode on, 113 body and limb hits did no damage and killed no
  one, and head hits killed 2; with it off, body hits damaged 8 guards and

- [audit_mission_cheats.ps1](scripts/port/audit_mission_cheats.ps1) (new

  at 1280x960 and 960x540 with records for Agent and Secret Agent: the row
  plain and highlighted, and both bottom rows clear of the cheat footer. After
  each review it captured both sizes again, with the mode off and on: the
  final capture shows both icon headings and no row icons, both columns of
  times inside the paper (`17:03+`, the widest, ends about 5 units short of the
  paper's edge), the stock column clear of the highlighted row's box, and the
  checkmark's lowest red pixels measured at x 299.9 for the column's 300.
  After the fourth review: the highlight box spanning both columns at
  1280x960 and 960x540, no cheat footer with Dam's and Facility's target rows
  shown, and the resized mark with its head on the horizontal ticks' line.
  After the fifth: the box around Dam's Secret Agent row taking in its
  **CHEAT TARGET** badge at 1280x960 and its earned **CHEAT UNLOCKED** badge at
  960x540, clear of the next row, and the 00 Agent row's box at its stock

- The owner played several Headshots Only missions on Windows after the push

### FORK-082 — Graphics: Tone Mapping, HDR Output and ray-traced Baked Lighting

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15 at the owner's request.
- **Built:** for Windows in an isolated worktree build.
- **Play-tested:** by the owner as `build_win/IronSights-Graphics.exe`, beside
  the main executable (which then held FORK-081's play-test build).
- **Committed and pushed:** to `main` on 2026-11-15 as `08af4e2`, after
  rebasing onto FORK-080 and FORK-081; first drafted as FORK-080 and
  renumbered when those two landed.
- **Browser (2026-11-15, at the owner's request):** ported, on by default in
  desktop browsers, and checked with private real-ROM captures in headless
  Chrome on this machine's GPU. See **Browser** below.
- **Not yet seen running:** Linux and Steam Deck (CI builds and packages
  them), Safari, Firefox and phones.
- **HDR Output** was not seen on an HDR display: this machine's monitor
  reports Windows HDR off.

Inherited behaviour: the renderer replays the N64 display lists through
OpenGL into an 8-bit target and presents with `SDL_GL_SwapWindow`. Room
lighting is the vertex colours in the level files; characters, props and guns
use the N64's directional lights. There was no grading, no HDR path and no
light baking.

**Defaults (2026-11-15, the owner's choice):**
- **On by default:** the Windows, Linux and browser builds start with Tone
  Mapping and Baked Lighting on and the Vibrant Look (its values are the
  slider defaults and the fresh midas.ini's), Gun and Hands on, HDR Output
  off.
- **HDR Output stays opt-in:** it only runs while Windows HDR is on, and its
  presenter has not yet been seen on an HDR display.
- **Touch devices in the browser** start with Tone Mapping and Baked
  Lighting off (`browserTouchGraphicsDefaults`): phones and tablets render at
  their full pixel density on weaker GPUs, and no phone has been measured.
  Both rows stay on the Graphics page.
- **Xbox:** both stay off, untested.
- **Capture runs:** every run with `GE_WINDOW` set (audits, the review gallery,
  weapon icon export) starts with both off (`portGraphicsCaptureDefaults`,
  called by `videoLoadConfig` before the ini is read), so captures stay
  comparable with stock unless their own midas.ini turns them on.
- **Existing midas.ini files keep their saved values.** Earlier in the day all
  of these defaulted to off.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > Graphics**, a new subsection in both the Options
folder (`PORT_SHEET_IS_GRAPHICS`, `GE_MENU=zgraphics`) and the watch
(`PORTWATCH_IS_GRAPHICS`, appended after the System pages so earlier watch
page numbers stay put; the Control tab's `GE_WATCHPAGE` numbers move up by one). All keys are `[display]`:

- **Tone Mapping** (`tone_mapping`, default 1 on Windows, Linux and desktop browsers) with seven sliders (all
  0-100% unless noted; 2026-11-15 after the owner found the first version
  darker than stock and asked for more pop and control):
  - **Brightness** (`tone_brightness`, 50-200%, default 150, the Vibrant value; 100 = stock): an exposure gain.
  - **Contrast** (`tone_contrast`, 50-200%, default 90): a power of 0.75-1.5
    around mid grey.
  - **Intensity** (`tone_intensity`, default 50): the share of the filmic
    highlight roll-off.
  - **Vibrance** (`vibrance`, default 80): more saturation for the
    less saturated colours.
  - **Clarity** (`tone_clarity`, default 60): local contrast - luminance
    against an edge-aware local mean, x1.3, limited to +-0.25 and faded
    toward black and white. The mean (`clarityMean`) takes 16 taps of the
    4x4 mip on rings of 8 and 18 px, each weighted by its likeness to the
    pixel (Gaussian range kernel, sigma 0.12 in gamma luminance).
    - **Halo fix (2026-11-15):** the owner saw an uncanny halo around the
      gun and hands. Captures traced it to Clarity, not Glow: its plain
      16x16 mip average included the dark gun, so the wall beside it read as
      brighter than its surroundings and was brightened further.
    - **Before:** with Glow off, Clarity brightened the band within 6 px of
      the gun, relative to the wall 20-40 px away, by about 10 levels of 255
      on Facility and 4 on Caverns. Glow alone added nothing there.
    - **After:** the pale band along the Facility barrel is gone; Caverns
      keeps a residual of about 3 levels.
    - **Texture detail:** the x1.3 gain keeps the boost away from the gun at
      82-123% of the old one (mean absolute difference from a 6 px box blur;
      Facility, Surface and Caverns).
    - **Browser:** the shader compiles and grades there too (headless Chrome
      on Facility, no WebGL errors).
  - **Sharpen** (`tone_sharpen`, default 50): contrast-adaptive sharpening of
    the 4 neighbours after AMD's CAS, strongest on flat mid-tone texture and
    backing off near clipping, so no halos.
  - **Glow** (`tone_glow`, default 100): a half-size bright pass (linear light
    above 0.4 luminance), mipmapped and sampled at four levels, added before
    the curve, so lamps, sky and flashes bleed a soft halo.

  The game emits G_NOOP 0x66 (`portGraphicsGradeTag`) in
  `maybe_mp_interface` (`bondview2.c`), after the first-person guns and
  before the watch, HUD and fades, and at the start of the cutscene branch.
  The renderer (`gfx_grade.inl`) copies the bound target into a mipmapped
  texture and draws the current viewport (one per player in split screen)
  back graded: the N64 image as gamma 2.2, sharpened, glow added, brightness
  and contrast applied, then the filmic curve mixed in by Intensity. The curve
  is an ACES fit on a highlight range recovered by an inverse Reinhard on
  luminance (white to 2.5x), exposure 0.53 so mid grey stays put, normalised
  to keep white. Below a luminance of 0.1-0.3 the curve gives way to the
  image (the brighter of the two), so shadows never sink. The first version
  used the plain curve at 50%, which darkened a quarter-bright pixel by about
  20%; GoldenEye's scenes sit mostly in that range. Vibrance and Clarity
  follow. In a Facility capture the mean brightness with the Natural values is
  115.6 against stock 115.7 (the first version was visibly darker). Menus,
  title screens and the watch are never graded.
- **Looks and colour grading** (2026-11-15, at the owner's request for
  presets with different feelings). Seven more grading sliders, applied after
  the curve:
  - **Saturation** (`tone_saturation`, 0-200%, default 100; 0 = black and
    white) and **Temperature** (`tone_temperature`, -100 cool to 100 warm,
    default 0), both in linear light. Temperature is white-balance gains of
    (1 + 0.25t, 1 + 0.04t, 1 - 0.3t) scaled to luminance 1.
  - **Split Tone** (`tone_split`, default 0) with **Split Colours**
    (`tone_split_colours`: teal / orange, green / gold, blue / amber, sepia):
    shadows toward one tint, highlights toward the other, brightness kept.
  - **Fade** (`tone_fade`): blacks lifted to 0.12 and white lowered 5%.
  - **Vignette** (`tone_vignette`): corners darkened up to 60%, by the view's
    own rect.
  - **Film Grain** (`tone_grain`): a hash per pixel and frame, strongest in
    mid tones.

- **Auto Exposure and highlight detail** (2026-11-15, after the owner found
  the snow on Surface washed out under Vibrant: Brightness 150 put it on the
  flat top of the curve, Glow 100 hazed it and Clarity faded out near white):
  - **Auto Exposure** (`tone_auto_exposure`, 0-100%, default 60) and
    **Adaptation Speed** (`tone_adapt_speed`, 25-400%, default 100), in
    `gfx_exposure.inl`.
  - **Metering:** the view is drawn into a 64x64 float buffer as luminance x
    weight (centre 1.5, edges 0.5), and its 1x1 mip gives the mean. The plain
    mean, not the log mean: measured on stock captures, the log mean put Dam
    at -5.6 stops and Surface at -1.9, letting dark textures dominate.
  - **Adaptation:** a 1x1 float per player view (ping-ponged, up to 4 in
    split screen) moves the adapted log2 luminance toward the meter at 2.5/s
    toward brighter scenes and 0.6/s toward darker ones, times the speed. A
    gap over a second resets it. Nothing is read back to the CPU.
  - **Exposure shift:** (key - adapted) stops, clamped to -2 .. +0.25 and
    scaled by the strength, multiplies Brightness. The key, log2 0.125, sits
    between the measured centre-weighted means of Dam, Bunker and Caverns
    (-4.1 .. -4.7) and Surface's snow (-1.5).
  - **Clarity in highlights:** it now fades only halfway toward white, so
    bright surfaces keep their texture.
  - **Glow ignores wide bright areas:** the bright pass needs a pixel above
    1.25x its 32x32 mip surroundings as well as above 0.4, so a whole
    snowfield no longer glows while lamps and sky edges still do.
  - **Measured on isolated captures:** mean frame brightness, stock /
    Vibrant without Auto Exposure / Vibrant with it:
    - Surface: 139.0 / 161.8 / 122.6, the snow's shading and tracks visible
      again;
    - Bunker 1: 49.8 / 61.9 / 64.6;
    - Facility's first wall: 115.7 / 138.0 / 125.5.
  - **In the Looks:** both are part of every Look. Auto Exposure is 60 in
    Vibrant, 50 in Natural, Cinematic and Cold War, 40 in Noir, Muted and
    Warm Retro, and 25 in Dark; speed 100 in all.

  **Look** (`graphics_look`, default Vibrant; `port_graphics_looks.c`) sets
  all sixteen grading sliders at once:

  | Look | Brightness | Contrast | Intensity | Vibrance | Clarity | Sharpen | Glow | Saturation | Temp | Split | Colours | Fade | Vignette | Grain | Auto Exp. |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Natural | 100 | 100 | 50 | 50 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 100 | 0 | 0 | teal/orange | 0 | 0 | 0 | 50 |
  | Vibrant (the owner's settings) | 150 | 90 | 50 | 80 | 60 | 50 | 100 | 100 | 0 | 0 | teal/orange | 0 | 0 | 0 | 60 |
  | Cinematic | 105 | 115 | 70 | 40 | 35 | 30 | 40 | 100 | 0 | 40 | teal/orange | 0 | 30 | 0 | 50 |
  | Noir | 100 | 130 | 60 | 0 | 50 | 40 | 30 | 0 | 0 | 0 | teal/orange | 10 | 50 | 35 | 40 |
  | Muted | 100 | 85 | 40 | 0 | 15 | 20 | 0 | 70 | 0 | 0 | teal/orange | 25 | 10 | 0 | 40 |
  | Cold War | 95 | 105 | 50 | 20 | 35 | 30 | 20 | 80 | -40 | 40 | green/gold | 10 | 20 | 10 | 50 |
  | Warm Retro | 105 | 95 | 60 | 30 | 20 | 20 | 45 | 90 | 60 | 40 | sepia | 30 | 25 | 30 | 40 |
  | Dark | 75 | 120 | 60 | 30 | 40 | 30 | 30 | 90 | -10 | 0 | teal/orange | 0 | 50 | 10 | 25 |

  - **Tuning from captures:** the values were tuned from contact sheets of
    every Look on Facility and Dam. Warm Retro first read cool (its blue /
    amber shadows outweighed a weak Temperature), then olive with green /
    gold, which is why Temperature was strengthened and the Sepia pair added.
    Dark was deepened from brightness 85.
  - **Custom:** changing any grading slider (menu, hotkey or midas.ini) keeps
    the values and makes the Look Custom; values that match a Look again read
    as that Look, so the owner's existing settings load as Vibrant.
  - **Saving:** midas.ini writes `graphics_look` before the sliders.
  - **Tone Mapping:** the Look row and midas.ini leave Tone Mapping alone; the
    Insert hotkey also turns it on.
  - **Not in a Look:** HDR calibration and Baked Lighting.
- **HDR Output** (`hdr_output`, default 0; **HDR Peak Brightness**
  `hdr_peak`, 400-2000 nits, default 1000; **HDR Paper White**
  `hdr_paper_white`, 80-480 nits, default 200), Windows only (the rows and
  keys are compiled out elsewhere and on the Xbox).
  - **Display:** while the window's monitor is in Windows HDR mode (checked
    every 2 s through DXGI), a DXGI flip-model R16G16B16A16_FLOAT swap chain
    (scRGB) presents the window instead of GL (`gfx_hdr_dxgi.cpp`; d3d11 and
    dxgi load at run time). GL draws its final frame into a shared D3D11
    texture through `WGL_NV_DX_interop2`.
  - **Float targets:** framebuffer 0 becomes an RGBA16F texture (its fbo
    stands in for GL's window in `framebuffers[0]`), and every other target,
    the MSAA resolve copies and the N64 AA textures allocate RGBA16F.
  - **Grade:** on a float target it skips the curve, so highlights go above
    paper white with a soft shoulder into the peak. The HUD, drawn afterwards
    at up to 1.0, sits at paper white.
  - **Present:** `gfx_hdr.inl` converts the gamma-encoded, paper-relative
    values to linear scRGB (x paper / 80) at swap.
  - **Fallback:** with Windows HDR off, or if the presenter fails, GL keeps
    presenting and a console message says why. `GE_HDR_FORCE=1` runs the
    presenter on an SDR monitor for audits.
- **Baked Lighting** (`baked_lighting`, default 1 on Windows, Linux and desktop browsers; **Lighting Strength**
  `baked_lighting_strength`, 25-200%, default 100):
  - **Capture:** `load_bg_file` already loads every room once at stage start
    (`bgRoomCalcBB`). `portBakeCaptureRoom` copies each room's vertices
    (room-bounds space, the file colours) and walks its opaque and translucent
    lists (G_VTX slot cache, G_TRI1, G_TRI4). Opaque triangles become
    occluders; both kinds feed area-weighted vertex normals, whose winding was
    confirmed to face out (flipped, about 1,000 vertices on Dam and Facility
    came out almost black).
  - **Bake:** `port_baked_trace.c` builds a BVH and casts 64 cosine-weighted
    rays per vertex up to 220 world units (scaled by the level scale) on SDL
    worker threads (CPU count - 2, at most 8). Where threads are unavailable
    it runs 4 ms slices per frame.
  - **Result:** occlusion (weight 1 - t / radius, strength 0.85) darkens; the
    gathered colour of nearby surfaces tints but adds no brightness. Adding
    gathered light was tried first and brightened Facility by 54% on average,
    because the file colours already contain the level's light.
  - **Timing and apply:** a bake takes about 0.4 s on Dam and Facility here
    (21,722 and 25,493 vertices). Until it finishes the level keeps its own
    colours; then loaded rooms are rewritten, and rooms streaming in take the
    result in `bgLoadRoomModelData` (before the shot-light redarken, so a
    shot-out light still darkens on top).
  - **Strength and off:** strength blends file colour to bake in linear
    light, so changing it needs no new bake. Off writes the file colours back.
    Each rewrite reapplies the room's shot-out lights and drops the room
    cache's copy.
  - **Tuning env vars:** `GE_BAKE_RADIUS`, `GE_BAKE_RAYS`, `GE_BAKE_AO`,
    `GE_BAKE_BOUNCE` and `GE_BAKE_THREADS`. `GE_BAKE_DEBUG=1` shows the
    occlusion and tint on white. `stderr` logs one `bake:` line with the
    vertex and triangle counts, radius, mean brightness ratio and time.
- **Gun and Hands** (`graphics_viewmodel`, default 1). On: the grade runs
  after the guns, hands and arms, and Baked Lighting sends a probe (G_NOOP
  0x67, `portGraphicsViewmodelTag`). The probe is 64 rays from the eye
  against the bake, giving the surroundings' baked/original ratio, a little
  occlusion and their tint. The renderer multiplies the computed vertex
  colour of every draw in the `portHudViewmodelTag` span by it. Off: the
  grade runs before the guns and no probe is sent.

**Hotkeys:** ten appended bind actions (`PORTACT_TOGGLE_TONE_MAPPING` ..
`PORTACT_GRAPHICS_LOOK_NEXT`, `PM_PORT_LAST` +43):

| Action | Key |
| --- | --- |
| `toggle_tone_mapping` | F3 |
| `toggle_baked_lighting` | F4 |
| `toggle_hdr_output` | F2 |
| `toggle_graphics_viewmodel` | F7 |
| `graphics_compare` | F11 (F8 in the browser) |
| `graphics_slider_next` / `graphics_slider_prev` | Home / End |
| `graphics_slider_up` / `graphics_slider_down` | Page Up / Page Down |
| `graphics_look_next` | Insert |

The four slider keys (added 2026-11-15 at the owner's request, so every slider
can be tuned at run time) pick one of the page's sliders - the sixteen Tone
Mapping and grading sliders, Lighting Strength, and on Windows HDR Peak Brightness and HDR Paper
White - and step it by its menu step, clamped rather than wrapped. Each press
shows the slider's name and value, noting when its feature is off or a limit is
reached; a change saves. Home, End, Page Up and Page Down were free outside the
console. Pads ship unbound. They are taken every frame, menus included, in
`portStateInput`. Each toggle saves like its menu row and shows a console
message (`portConPrintf`). Compare splits the graded view (left stock, right
graded) and is not saved. They are listed in Controls (`sBindsAllExtra`).

**Arm rendering contract:** the owner asked for these features to reach the
gun, hands and arms. `scripts/port/arm_rendering.md` records the exception:
final colour only (the full-view grade, and one multiplier on the computed
shade inside the viewmodel span); vertices, UVs, alpha, triangles, materials,
depth and the native render setup are unchanged, and with the features off
(their default) the viewmodel draws as before.

**Hooks in upstream-owned files:**
- `bg.c`: `portBakeLevelBegin` / `portBakeLevelLoaded` around the
  `bgRoomCalcBB` loop, `portBakeCaptureRoom` in `bgRoomCalcBB`,
  `portBakeApplyRoom` after the room's vertices load, and
  `portBakeLevelUnload` in `cleanup_rooms`.
- `bondview2.c`: the grade and viewmodel tags around
  `gunRenderFirstPersonGunModels`, and the grade tag in the cutscene branch.
- `gfx_pc.cpp`: decodes 0x66 / 0x67 and scales the viewmodel's vertex shade;
  before grading it applies the game's pending viewport and scissor
  (`gfx_sync_viewport_scissor`, extracted from the per-draw state code), so
  the grade covers the player's view whatever GL was left on.
- `gfx_opengl.cpp`:
  - the float colour format, `framebuffers[0]` swap and HDR sync;
  - the grade entry in `gfx_opengl_api` and `gfx_rendering_api.h`;
  - a fix: `resolve_msaa_color_buffer` rebinds the current target's fbo; it
    used to bind its index, which only worked while that was 0.
- `gfx_sdl2.cpp`: skips `SDL_GL_SwapWindow` while DXGI presents.
- `port/web/state.c`: the browser's `portStateFrame` calls
  `portGraphicsFrame` (hotkeys and Baked Lighting's slice).
- `web/src/browser-settings.ts`: touch defaults and the one-time desktop
  migration (browser build only).
- `CMakeLists.txt`: the `ge_hdr_dxgi` object library, built without the
  game's include directories, which collide with the Windows SDK headers.
- `front.c`, `port_watchpages.c/.h`, `port_options.c`, `joy_port.c`,
  `input_pc.c`, `video.c` (default ini), `port_option_help.c`,
  `tools/midas_ini_help.txt`, README.md and AGENTS.md (the subsection list).

**Pitfall found:** in files compiled with the game's include directories,
`powf` is not the hosted one (`powf(1, 2.2)` returned 16481, which turned
baked rooms black). The bake's float maths therefore lives in the SDL-only
`port_baked_trace.c` (`portBakeLinTable`, `portBakeEncode`, `portBakeSqrt`).

**Seams (2026-11-15):** the grade turned the level's inherited seams
(T-junction gaps that show the sky behind a room) from dark navy into bright
cyan lines that the owner took for a regression. FORK-086 closes the seams
themselves; the grade is unchanged.

**Input:** the eight rows are ordinary option rows, so every supported input
(keyboard, mouse, gamepad, browser touch) changes them. The hotkeys are
keyboard by default and bindable to a controller; browser touch has no way to
press them and gets no overlay control. This is deliberate: they are a review
aid, and every setting they flip is a menu row touch can reach.

**Fix: the Dam ending darkened all but a square (2026-11-15, reported by the
owner).**
- **Symptom:** during Dam's bungee fall and outro, at 1920x1080, the whole
  view lost the grade (read as darker under Vibrant) except one square near
  the bottom left.
- **Cause:** the grade took the player's view from GL's current viewport.
  Richer Reflections' level cube (FORK-066, `gfx_envcube.inl`) renders its
  six 128x128 faces in a 3x2 atlas mid-frame. It marks the game's viewport
  to be re-applied by the next draw but leaves GL on its last cell (256, 128,
  128x128). In play the gun and hands draw before the grade and restore it;
  the Dam outro hides the weapons, so nothing drew in between and only that
  cell was graded. It happens wherever the cube renders and no draw follows
  before the grade.
- **Evidence:** a temporary log in an isolated outro capture (spawned in the
  bungee room, reflections on, 1920x1080, 60 and 120 Hz) showed the grade
  receiving viewport 256 128 128 128 of 1920 x 1080 on every logged outro
  frame, the reported square's position; in normal play it never happened.
  With the fix, the same run logged no small viewport.
- **Fix:** the 0x66 handler applies the game's pending viewport and scissor
  before grading.

**Browser (2026-11-15, at the owner's request to bring Graphics to the web
build).** The first browser build compiled the Graphics code with it off by
default and never ran it; bringing it up found four gaps:
- **No per-frame work:** the hotkeys, `portGraphicsTick` and Baked Lighting's
  slice ran from `portStateInput`, which only the native suspend-point frame
  (`portStateFrame`) calls; the browser's `port/web/state.c` stubs that
  frame out. The three now live in `portGraphicsFrame` (`joy_port.c`), called
  from `portStateInput` natively and from the browser's `portStateFrame`, so
  in the browser the bake never started and no hotkey worked before.
- **Black grade under MSAA:** the grade copied the target into an RGBA8
  texture. Desktop GL converts the RGB8 MSAA buffer while resolving; GLES and
  WebGL resolve only between identical formats (`GL_INVALID_OPERATION`, a
  black scene). The copy now takes the target's format: RGB8, or RGBA16F
  under HDR Output.
- **Bake time:** the browser has no threads, so the bake runs in 4 ms slices
  per frame: 4.1 s wall on Surface (14,697 vertices), 6.2-7.0 s on Dam
  (21,722) and 7.1 s on Facility (25,493), finished before control in every
  capture. The `bake:` line's time is wall time in this mode (it read 0 ms
  before).
- **Keys:** the browser keeps F11 (fullscreen) and F2 (the launcher's
  Controls), so Compare defaults to F8 there; `undo_load`, F8 natively, is
  unbound in the browser, which has no suspend points. The other hotkeys
  work as on Windows. The Graphics page help names F8 in the browser.
- **Weapon icons:** the first-launch icon stage (FORK-019) renders guns in
  Dam and reads them back. Its pixels are drawn after the grade, so they were
  never graded, but the grade, the viewmodel probe and the bake all ran
  during it. While the export runs (`portWeaponExportEnabled`, also the
  native icon helper) no grade or probe tag is sent and the bake does not
  start.
- **Defaults and migration:** `PORT_GRAPHICS_ON_DEFAULT` is now 1 in the
  browser. The launcher (`web/src/browser-settings.ts`) starts touch devices
  with both off. Browsers that ran the first build saved `tone_mapping=0` and
  `baked_lighting=0` with every other setting; on desktop the launcher drops
  that pair once (`browserGraphicsDefaultMigration`, remembered in
  `localStorage` as `midas-graphics-default-v1` after the save flush), so the
  new default applies. A later choice is kept. HDR Output does not exist in
  the browser.
- **Captures** (`bun run audit:graphics <rom> <out> [origin] [cases]`,
  `web/tools/graphics-audit.mjs`; private, not committed): one Chrome profile
  prepares the weapon icons, then each case reloads the cartridge into Dam,

  - the game's GL submit time per frame rose by about 0.5-2 ms with Vibrant
