### FORK-081 — Reinforcements: more clones and a reinforcement director

**Status:** Clones and the difficulty-page row implemented on 2026-11-14 at
the owner's request; after their first play-test the owner asked for the
reinforcement director, added on 2026-11-15 together with a spawn clearance
check. Built in a separate CMake directory (another session was rebuilding
the main executable at the time) and copied into the main
`build_win/IronSights.exe` for the owner's play-test. The owner approved the
director build on 2026-11-15 and asked for it to be committed and pushed to
`main`, which was done the same day. Linux, Steam Deck and browser builds not
run locally.

Inherited behaviour: Rare's only general reinforcement is the clone. A guard
running the standard guard AI (`chraidata.c` `m_StandardGuard`) that hears Bond
before Bond has seen it jumps to `m_TryCloneSendOrRunToBond`: if its single
clone (chrnum + 10000) does not exist, `chr_try_spawning_clone` makes a copy of
it beside it, which runs to Bond while the original holds its post. Only guards
whose setup sets the clone flag (`GUARD_SETUP_FLAG_CHR_CLONE`) can do it: 7 in
Archives, 10 in Runway, 4 in Surface 1, 14 in Bunker 1 and 9 in Bunker 2, none
anywhere else. Every spawn (`chrSpawnAtCoord`) needs 3 free character slots, and
the pool (`alloc_init_GUARDdata_entries`) holds the level's placed guards plus 10,
with 30 spare plain and 10 spare animated model slots (`initunk_005520.c`). On
PC, running out of character slots stops the game with "Character pool
exhausted". Level scripts time their own reinforcements (`chr_try_spawning_at_pad`,
about 330 calls in 17 setups) with local timers and fixed guard IDs; this entry
leaves them alone.

**Reinforcements** (`[display] reinforcements`, default 0 = Original) sets how
many guards the level sends:

- **Original** (0): Rare's rule, unchanged. Every hook below is a no-op.
- **More** (1): any placed guard with a soldier's body (Jungle Commando, St
  Petersburg Guard, Russian Soldier and Infantry, Janus Special Forces and
  Marine, Russian Commandant, both Siberian guards and Special Forces, Naval
  Officer, Helicopter Pilot, Arctic Commando, both Moonraker Elite) may clone,
  as may Rare's flagged guards. Named characters, Bond's outfits, civilians,
  scientists, invincible characters, clones and guards spawned by scripts never
  do. Each keeps up to 2 living clones, the next at most every 8 seconds while
  it still hears gunfire, and the level gets 12 more character slots, 12 more
  animated and 24 more plain model slots.
- **Relentless** (2): up to 3 living clones per guard, one every 4 seconds, 24
  more slots (24 animated, 48 plain), and a guard Bond has already seen may call
  one more while it is off screen (`PROPFLAG_ONSCREEN` clear), so the clone never
  pops into view.

**The director (More and Relentless).** Clones need a guard that hears Bond
before Bond sees it, which open levels rarely give, so the director sends guards
of its own (`port_reinforcements_director.c`, called once a frame from `lv.c`
after `propsTick`). Bond counts as noticed while any guard saw him within Rare's
10-second memory (`chrSawTargetRecently`) or the alarm is on; the director keeps
sending for 20 seconds after. It sends one guard every 20 seconds while fewer
than 4 of its own are alive (More), or every 10 seconds up to 8 (Relentless),
searching at most once a second. The guard starts on a waypoint pad (so it is on
Rare's navigation network) 600 to 6000 units from Bond across the floor and
within 400 up or down, with a `waypointFindRoute` route of 2 to 14 steps to the
waypoint nearest Bond, off screen (`chrIsPosOffScreen`: its room not drawn, or
out of view) and clear of others; of up to ten shuffled candidates the shortest
route wins. It wears the body, guns (doubles kept) and hat of the nearest placed
soldier, copied while that soldier is alive and remembered after it falls, gets
Rare's clone AI (`GAILIST_STANDARD_CLONE`: run to Bond, then act as a standard
guard), never clones, and drops its gun when killed like any guard. Objectives
are untouched; the debrief counts its kills like any other.

**Spawn clearance.** Rare's `chrAdjustPosForSpawn` tests a 20-unit circle against
characters that are standing (dying and dead ones are not obstacles), so a spawn
can land touching another guard or inside a falling one. Every spawn this entry
adds, clone or director guard, now also needs no character, living or fallen,
within 60 units across the floor (and 200 up or down), and a director guard no
Bond within 300 (`portReinforcementsSpawnClear`, hooked into `chrSpawnAtCoord`).
Rare's own spawns, and every spawn at Original, skip it.

A clone Rare would not have made (any clone under More or Relentless except a
flagged, unseen guard's first), and every director guard, only spawns while 10
character slots stay free, the margin Rare's pool always had, so scripted
reinforcements keep their room and the pool-exhausted stop cannot be reached by
these spawns. Rare's own spawns keep
the 3-slot test, now inside a bigger pool. A guard at its limit or cooldown holds
its post as Rare's clone guards do; a seen guard falls back to Rare's run at
Bond. The level is read when a stage loads (the pools are sized then), so a
change applies from the next mission start. Multiplayer (no placed guards) and
demo playback (`get_is_ramrom_flag`) keep Original.

**Where it is set:** each mission's difficulty page shows a **Reinforcements:**
row under the best times (right of the cheat footer, at y 295, just short of a
difficulty pitch below the 007 row; FORK-083 moved it up from 300 and put its
Headshots Only row at the line's left end). Since FORK-083 the value prints
after the black label in the dossier's emphasis red (`0xA00000FF`) when it is
above Original, and black at Original. Pointing at it highlights it with the difficulty rows' box; the
page's confirm press steps to the next level and wraps (A, Start or Z on a
pad, Enter, a mouse click, a browser tap), with the options' click sound. It
calls the options table's `portOptStep`, so it saves `midas.ini` like any row.
Every supported input reaches it: browser touch sends cursor motion and A, which
is all it needs, so it has no native touch context. It was also the only row of a
new **Gameplay > Iron Sights > Enemies** subsection (FORK-083 added Headshots
Only and Headshots Melee after it), in both the Options folder
and the watch, between Combat Feedback and HUD Additions (no existing
subsection fits a setting about the guards). `GE_MENU=zguards` opens the folder
page.

**Shared hooks in upstream files** (all `#ifndef TARGET_N64`):
`initguards.c` adds the stage's slots; `initunk_005520.c` and `model.c` grow the
spare model slots and make the level-reset searches skip them; `chraction.c`
marks placed guards at setup, swaps `chrSpawnAtCoord`'s free-slot test and lets
`chrSpawnAtChr` clone a seen, off-screen guard during a Relentless clone, and
adds the clearance test to `chrSpawnAtCoord`; `lv.c` runs the director each
frame after `propsTick`;
`chr.c` clears a slot's record when it is freed; `chrai.c` hooks
`IFChrDoesNotExist(CHR_CLONE)` and `IFIveNotBeenSeen`, both only inside Rare's
clone list, and `TRYCloningChr` (eligibility and bookkeeping around the
spawn); `front.c` adds the Enemies page and the difficulty-page row.

**Sources:** rules in [port_reinforcements.h](port/include/port_reinforcements.h),
setting in [port_reinforcements.c](port/src/port_reinforcements.c), game hooks
and the per-slot side table in
[port_reinforcements_game.c](port/src/port_reinforcements_game.c), the
difficulty-page row in [port_reinforcements_menu.c](port/src/port_reinforcements_menu.c),
the director in [port_reinforcements_director.c](port/src/port_reinforcements_director.c)
with its rules in [port_reinforcements_director.h](port/include/port_reinforcements_director.h),
plus [port_options.c](port/src/port_options.c), [joy_port.c](port/src/joy_port.c),
[port_watchpages.c](port/src/port_watchpages.c),
[help](port/src/port_option_help.c), [default ini](port/src/video.c),
[settings reference](tools/midas_ini_help.txt), [README](README.md) and the
subsection list in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). `GE_REINFORCEMENTS_LOG=1` prints each
stage's level, every placed guard (body, position, clone flag, whether it may
clone), every clone with its game tick, living count, free slots and floor
distance to the nearest other character, and every director guard with its pad,
route steps, distance from Bond and the outfit and gun it copied.

**Checks:** [test_reinforcements.c](scripts/port/test_reinforcements.c), run by
[test_ads.sh](scripts/port/test_ads.sh), covers the setting, clamping and the
difficulty page's wrapping step, the pool sizes, the multiplayer and demo
gates, eligibility and soldier bodies, the per-guard limit and cooldown, the
free slots an added clone leaves, the director's timing, cap and noticed window,
its pad distance and route limits, and the spawn clearance. The four new sources
also compile with implicit declarations as errors: the director first called
`atan2f` without a prototype (this repository's `include/math.h` keeps its libc
declarations under `#if 0`), so its guards spawned with garbage headings and the
second one to aim crashed the game in `chrlvInitActAttack`; it now includes
`game/math_atan2f.h`. The settings placement check and Bright Builds
checks pass; the hand gallery regenerated with no changed image cells. In game
(isolated copies, `GE_SPAWNXYZ` beside Facility's guards 1, 3, 6 and 7 with dual
DD44s firing): Original made no clones; More made 2 per guard, the second about
8 seconds after the first (ticks 1557 and 2045); Relentless made 3 per guard
about 4 seconds apart and then stopped. A soak loaded 14 solo stages at
Relentless with the extra slots and no errors. The difficulty page was captured
with the row plain and highlighted. Not yet checked: what clones look like
arriving in a real fight (the audit spawn points were outside room geometry),
Relentless's after-seen clones, the clone rate in Rare's flagged levels, demo
playback, and the browser and Linux builds.

Director runs (isolated copies, Bond invulnerable with autofire): in Dam's
tunnel (`GE_SPAWNXYZ` 8194,-633,-1282) Relentless sent 9 guards in 90 seconds,
exactly 10 seconds apart, from pads 1200 to 2700 units away with 2 or 3 route
steps; More sent 4, 20 seconds apart. In Facility's bathroom Relentless sent 10,
from pads 700 to 1200 units away with 2 to 7 steps; most were killed by the
autofire and their slots reused, so they reached Bond. Original at the same Dam
spot ran without the director or a crash. Not yet checked: how the arrivals feel
and look in play (the audit camera faced a wall), stealth-heavy missions, and
long missions at the cap.

The owner's first play-test (Dam, Agent, Relentless, in the main executable)
found few extra guards, and some underground guards appearing inside each
other with confused behaviour. (A later `build_win/IronSights-Graphics.exe`
run, a separate graphics build sharing `midas.ini` and the log, overwrote
`Data/Logs/ge_direct.log`, so that session left no log.) Dam limits clones: 13 of its 36 guards run a
tower script (`ai_11`) that only rarely hands over to the standard guard AI,
and in a tunnel test (guards 16 to 21) every guard that reacted saw Bond first
and went straight to attacking, since Rare's standard guard checks sight before
hearing; none cloned. Open levels with long sightlines therefore gain little
from hearing-based clones, which is why the director above was added (it was
first recorded here as a follow-up). In the Facility runs each new clone landed
60 units (the spawn ring's spacing) from the nearest character; the overlapping
guards were not reproduced, and the spawn clearance above now rules out the
cases Rare's own test misses.

### FORK-080 — Touch Controls Opacity for browser touch

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-14 at the owner's request (default 50%,
80% while touched). Not yet tried on a physical phone or with the real ROM in
the browser.

Before this entry the touch overlay (FORK-028) had no overall strength: each
control's transparency was fixed in its colours in `web/src/touch.css`
(backgrounds 38-85%, borders 40-63%) and its labels and icons were fully
opaque. Upstream has no browser target.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > HUD Additions > Touch Controls Opacity**
(`[display] touch_controls_opacity`, 25 / 35 / 50 / 75 / 100, default 50):
- **At rest** during gameplay every touch button and the move stick show at
  the chosen percent of their designed look (labels and icons included, via
  CSS `opacity`), easing over 160 ms.
- **Touched** controls show at 80% or the setting, whichever is more, with no
  delay, so a pressed button or a dragged stick is always clear, and a 100%
  setting is never dimmed by a touch.
- **Menus, the watch and other touch screens** keep full strength; only the
  `game` touch context fades.
- An off-list value in `midas.ini` takes the nearest step.

**How.** `port/web/touch.c` stores the value next to Double-Tap Fire
(`portWebTouchOptionGet/Set`, `portWebTouchControlsOpacity`). The overlay
reads it each frame (`touch-controls.tsx`, through `createTouchFade` in
`web/src/touch-opacity.ts`) into a `--touch-rest-opacity` custom property on
the overlay root; the same module converts the percent and marks
the control each finger is on with `data-touching` until that finger lifts or
is cancelled (a delegated capture-phase `pointerdown` on the overlay and
window `pointerup`/`pointercancel`, so it does not rely on `:active`, which is
unreliable for multi-touch). The overlay's entry fade (`touch-hud-enter`) used
`fill-mode: both`, which held opacity at 1 after it ended and would have
overridden the stick's resting strength; it now uses `backwards`, and the
stick's entry ends at its resting strength (`--touch-enter-opacity`) so it
does not pop.

**Setting placement.** Browser-only like FORK-079: the option entry
(`port_options.c`), folder row (`front.c port_sheet_rows_is_hud`), watch row
(`port_watchpages.c sIsHud`) and the `joy_port.c` dispatch are inside
`#if defined(__EMSCRIPTEN__) && defined(GE_VIDEO)`. Desktop builds show no
row. Help text is in `port_option_help.c` (row and HUD Additions page
summary), `tools/midas_ini_help.txt` and the README touch paragraph.

**Input idioms.** An ordinary choice row, changed like any other by keyboard,
mouse, gamepad, the watch arrows and touch.

**Sources.** `web/src/touch-opacity.ts` and its test, `touch-controls.tsx`,
`touch.css`, `runtime-types.ts`, the fixture switch in
`web/tests/touch-driver.tsx`, `web/tools/touch-opacity-audit.mjs`,
`port/web/touch.c`/`.h`, `scripts/port/test_web_touch.c` and the rows above.
WEB-011 in `scripts/port/web_target_progress.md` records the milestone note.

**Validation.** `touch-opacity.test.ts` (6 tests: percent conversion,
default, multi-finger holds, finger moving between controls, clear, writing
the strength only on change) and all 262 web unit tests pass, as does TypeScript. The ROM-free touch UI audit
(`MIDAS_BROWSER=msedge`) passes with a new step: Fire and the stick rest at
0.5, a touched Fire or stick shows 0.8 while others stay 0.5, lifting or
cancelling returns to 0.5, a 100% setting shows 1 touched or not, and a menu
control stays at 1 with the setting at 25%. That step first found the stick
pinned at 1 by the entry fade's held frame (fixed above). `test_web_touch.sh`
in the pinned emsdk image passes with a new option check (default 50, steps,
nearest-step clamping). The web video target builds with the pinned SDK
(`web_build.py video`) and its wasm carries the key, the row label and the
`portWebTouchControlsOpacity` export. The Windows build compiles with the
rows guarded out. `settings_placement.py` and `bun scripts/bright-builds-check.ts
all` pass; the hand gallery regeneration changed 0 image cells. The ROM-backed
touch game audit was not run.

### FORK-079 — Double-Tap Fire for browser touch

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-14 at the owner's request; committed and
pushed to `main` on 2026-11-14 (`d31f229`) so GitHub Pages can deploy it for
phone testing. Not yet tried on a physical phone or with the real ROM
in the browser.

Inherited behaviour: upstream has no browser target. Before this entry the
fork's touch overlay (FORK-028) fired only from the Fire / Z buttons; a tap
on the free look area did nothing in gameplay.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > Aiming and Movement > Double-Tap Fire**
(`[display] touch_double_tap_fire`, default 1 = on) adds a fire gesture to
the look area in both touch layouts:

- **Gesture.** A first contact on the look area that lifts within 250 ms
  and never wanders more than 10 CSS pixels (the overlay's button tap slop)
  arms a pair. A second look contact that lands within 300 ms of that
  release and within 48 pixels of it holds Fire (`TOUCH_FIRE`, the N64 Z)
  from the moment it touches until that finger lifts, so automatic weapons
  keep firing and semi-automatic ones fire once, as when Z is held. The
  firing finger keeps looking as it drags, like a held Fire button.
- **Never by accident.** The first tap never fires. A look swipe is not a
  tap, so lifting and quickly re-touching to keep turning does not fire. The
  firing contact does not arm another pair, so three quick taps fire once.
  A cancelled contact, lost capture, context change, focus loss or layout
  change forgets an armed tap.
- **Scope.** Only the gameplay look surface (`.touch-look`); menus, the
  watch and cinematics keep their tap behaviour. Only one look finger is
  tracked at a time, as before.
- **Why a press, not a release.** Firing on the second touch rather than on
  its lift avoids adding delay, and lets the same finger hold and aim.

**Setting placement.** The row is browser-only: its option-table entry
(`port_options.c`), folder row (`front.c port_sheet_rows_is_aim`), watch row
(`port_watchpages.c sIsAim`) and `joy_port.c` dispatch are all inside
`#if defined(__EMSCRIPTEN__) && defined(GE_VIDEO)`, the guard front.c uses
for the other touch hooks, because `port/web/touch.c` (which stores the
value) is compiled only for non-headless web builds. Desktop builds show no
row and ignore the key. `settings_placement.py` reads the rows textually, so
the key needs no exception entry. Help text is in `port_option_help.c`, and
the Aiming and Movement page summary now mentions touch fire.

**Input idioms.** The setting is an ordinary toggle row, so keyboard, mouse,
gamepad and touch change it like any other. The gesture itself is
touch-only by nature; mouse, keyboard and gamepad already have Fire.

**Sources.** `web/src/touch-double-tap.ts` (pure timing rules),
`web/src/touch-controls.tsx` (look-surface hook: `maybeLook` now records its
start, farthest wander and whether it fires), `web/src/runtime-types.ts`,
`port/web/touch.c` / `touch.h` (`portWebTouchOptionGet/Set`,
`portWebTouchDoubleTapFire`), the rows above, `tools/midas_ini_help.txt` and
the README touch paragraph. WEB-011 in `scripts/port/web_target_progress.md`
records the milestone note.

**Validation.** `web/src/touch-double-tap.test.ts` (6 unit tests: tap and
second-tap limits, swipe, single use, slow touch, clear) and TypeScript
pass. The ROM-free touch UI audit (`bun run test:touch`, run with
`MIDAS_BROWSER=chrome`) passes with a new `touch-double-tap-audit.mjs` step
through the fixture's `doubleTapFire` switch: tap then touch holds Fire and
keeps aiming, lifting releases it, a third touch does not refire, and a
single tap, swipe and re-touch, far second touch, slow second touch and the
setting off never fire. Every earlier audit step still passes with the
gesture on. The Firefox audit browser failed to launch locally (Playwright
launch error), so only Chrome ran. `test_web_touch.sh` in the pinned emsdk
image passes with a new Double-Tap Fire option check. The web video target
builds with the pinned SDK (`web_build.py video`) and its wasm carries the
key, the row label and the `portWebTouchDoubleTapFire` export. All 256 web
unit tests, `settings_placement.py` and `bun scripts/bright-builds-check.ts
all` pass. The hand gallery was regenerated for the touched render inputs
with 0 changed image cells. The ROM-backed touch game audit was not run; the
gesture sends the same `TOUCH_FIRE` the Fire button does.

### FORK-078 — Explosive Rounds: a small blast where each bullet lands

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-14 at the owner's request and built into
the main Windows executable for play-testing. The owner's first play-test
found guards' rounds leaving large smoke plumes and asked for a quicker
blast; the shorter blast and short smoke below replaced the first version's.
The owner play-tested that revision and approved it; committed and pushed to
`main` on 2026-11-14 (`092f276`). Linux, Steam Deck and browser builds not
run locally.

Inherited behaviour: a bullet that reaches a wall or floor makes Rare's
impact spark, explosion type 1 (no damage, no sound, ten shrapnel bits and
smoke 7), plus a bullet hole and a `bullet_spark_create` puff
(`chraiDefaultWeaponFireHandler`, `chrprop.c`). A bullet that hits a guard,
object or door makes only that hit's puffs, blood or hole. A guard's bullet
makes a puff where it lands (`chraction.c`). Explosions take one of 6 slots
(100 with Unlimited Explosions), and every type but 1 and 16 starts the
screen shake.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > Combat Feedback > Explosive Rounds**
(`[display] explosive_rounds`, default 0 = Off) adds a small blast where each
bullet lands:

- **Visual** (1) is a fireball of size 12 (Rare's smallest damaging blast,
  type 2, is 30), 20 shrapnel bits, a brief pale puff and
  `EXPLOSION_1B_SFX`, with no damage: its damage range and damage are 0, as
  for the spark. The blast is quick: each flare sprite holds its 15 frames
  1.5 ticks apiece (3 in the first version), flares spawn for 24 ticks (21
  in the EU table) and the whole blast ends after about 48 ticks, under a
  second at 60 Hz (93 before). Its smoke is Rare's short smoke 9 (four light
  grey puffs that fade in about a second). The first version used smoke 7,
  as the bullet spark does, whose puffs keep growing and rising for 6 to 10
  seconds; the owner found that guards' rounds piled them into large
  plumes.
- **Explosive** (2) is the same blast with splash damage over a radius
  growing from 30 to 50 units: 0.165 per damage pass, three passes over the
  blast's life (any explosion applies damage every quarter of its life from
  age 8), matching type 2's four passes of 0.125. It damages
  characters, Bond included (so shooting a wall at point-blank range hurts),
  and objects, so rounds can set off barrels and other explosive props. The
  shooting player is credited, as the native stray-shot damage is.
- Placement: a wall or floor hit uses the native spark's point, 26 units off
  the surface. A bullet stopped by a guard, object or door blasts at its
  farthest hit, which is where it stopped, pulled 26 units towards the
  camera (the view-space point `chrHandleBulletHit` computes). A shotgun
  blast makes one blast, at the first pellet that lands. A guard's bullet
  blasts where its native puff appears, including on another guard it hits.
  A guard's shot that hits Bond makes no blast, so no explosion fills the
  screen.

**Whose Rounds** (`[display] explosive_rounds_guards`, default 1 =
Everyone) chooses whose bullets explode: Everyone, guards included, or
Players (0). In multiplayer every player's rounds follow the shared
setting. The row was first labelled Explosive Rounds For, with values
Players Only and Everyone; the owner saw that label run into its value in
the Options folder (both fonts, 1080p captures), and it nearly touched the
value on the watch, where Players Only also overhung the value column. The
shorter label and value replaced them; the midas.ini key is unchanged.

The fork appends three rows to `g_ExplosionTypes` (both the NTSC and the EU
tables, after Rare's 22; not on N64): 22 Visual, 23 Bond's Explosive and 24 a
guard's Explosive. Rows 23 and 24 are identical, except that damage from a
guard's round never shows Bond's hit marker. Rounds never start the screen
shake. A round is skipped unless more than two explosion slots are free
under the cap, so grenades, mines and props still explode with Unlimited
Explosions off. Demo playback (`get_is_ramrom_flag`) keeps the native
impacts, since recorded input expects them. The native spark and puffs are
unchanged and still appear under the blast. `GE_ROUNDS_LOG=1` prints each
blast's type, position and room, and each one held back for the slots.

**Hooks** (all inside `#ifndef TARGET_N64`): `chrprop.c` calls
`portExplosiveRoundsPlayerWall` beside the wall spark's `bullet_spark_create`
when the shot reached a surface, `portExplosiveRoundsPlayerHits` at the end
of `chraiDefaultWeaponFireHandler` when it did not, and
`portExplosiveRoundsShotBegin` / `ShotEnd` around the shotgun's pellet loop
in `chraiCheckUseHeldItem`. `chraction.c` calls
`portExplosiveRoundsGuardImpact` beside a guard shot's
`bullet_spark_create`. `explosion.c` appends the rows, routes `explosionCreate`'s
shake test (US and EU/JP copies) through `portExplosionStartsShake`, which
keeps Rare's exemptions, and adds `portExplosionShowsHitMarker` to
`explosionInflictDamage`'s `portHudHit` call. The options register in
`joy_port.c`'s dispatch, `port_options.c` (after Decorative Pellets), the
folder's Combat Feedback rows (`front.c`) and the watch's
(`port_watchpages.c`), with help in `port_option_help.c` (which also names
tracers and explosive rounds in the page description),
`tools/midas_ini_help.txt`, the default midas.ini writer (`video.c`) and
README.md.

**Input:** two ordinary option rows, so every supported input already
adjusts them as it does the other Combat Feedback rows.

**Sources:** [header with the pure rules](port/include/port_explosive_rounds.h),
[settings](port/src/port_explosive_rounds.c),
[game hooks](port/src/port_explosive_rounds_game.c) and the
[ROM-free test](scripts/port/test_explosive_rounds.c) (included by
`test_tracers.c`, in `test_ads.sh`).

**Checks:** in the `goldeneye` Docker image, `test_ads.sh` passes with the new
test: the defaults and menu entries; midas.ini clamping; which shooter,
mode and demo state make which row; the row indices after Rare's 22; the
two-slot reserve; Rare's shake exemptions kept and rounds added; the guard
row's hidden hit marker; and the one-blast-per-shotgun-shot queue.
`test_hud.sh`, `test_states.sh`, `test_upstream_merge.sh`,
`test_wardrobe.sh`, `settings_placement.py` and `bright-builds-check.ts all`
pass. The Windows build succeeds. Two isolated 60-second Dam runs
(invulnerable, holding fire in one-second bursts, `GE_ROUNDS_LOG=1`) exited
cleanly: Explosive with Unlimited Explosions off made 48 type-23 blasts with
none held back, and Visual made 48 type-22 blasts. Two 90-second Explosive
runs where guards attack the invulnerable player also exited cleanly:
Runway made 79 type-23 and 238 type-24 (guard) blasts, and Archives made 107
guard blasts. Those runs used the first version's rows; with the quicker
rows, a repeat Runway run with Unlimited Explosions off exited cleanly with
64 type-23 and 118 type-24 blasts, the slot reserve holding back 114 more
under the guards' fire. The hand gallery was regenerated
for the source change with no changed image cells, and
`hand_gallery.py verify` passes. The owner's play-test covered the revised
blast's look. Not separately checked: its size and loudness (the sound has not been recorded and measured), damage
balance for Bond and guards, shotguns, explosive props, multiplayer and
raised tick rates. For the Whose Rounds rename, isolated 1920x1080 captures
(`GE_MENU=zfeedback` and `GE_WATCHPAGE=3,11,8`) in the Original and Iron
Sights fonts showed both rows clear of their values in the Options folder
and on the watch, Players inside the watch's value column, and both help
lines fitting their box; `test_ads.sh` and `settings_placement.py` pass.

### FORK-077 — Level decals keep the one-sided depth test

**Status:** Fixed on 2026-11-14 after the owner saw Statue's ground flip
between textures while walking near the start. The owner's play-tests of the
first two attempts each turned up another spot; this entry describes the
design that replaced them. Not yet play-tested by the owner in its final form.

Statue's ground near the start is two layers: a base grass and, over it, a
clover-patterned grass decal (`ZMODE_DEC`, texture `20154810`, from the model
texture pool). The decal's triangles are much larger than the ground's, share
only some of its corners, and so sit tens of units off the ground in places;
several reach from behind the camera hundreds of units out. Walking or turning
a degree or two cut bands, wedges and triangles out of the decal, showing the
darker base ground, and they came back as the view moved. The original
textures did the same, less visibly.

The cause is inherited decal emulation (present at the 1.0.2b baseline in
`gfx_opengl_draw_triangles`): to emulate the RDP's two-sided decal depth window
and trim a bullet hole where its wall ends, a marking pass pushes a copy of each
decal corner `GE_DEC_TOL` (8) world units away and draws the decal only where
the stored surface is no farther. Applied to Statue's terrain decals it failed
three ways, each found at one of the owner's positions (`GE_DEBUGPOS`):
- X -15196, Y 1029, Z 2284, pitch -24, heading 270 against 272: a corner at
  `w` 0.7 (or -0.6) was skipped by the push (`w - pull <= 1`), collapsing the
  window beside it.
- X -15060, Y 962, Z 2391, heading 241 pitch -13 against 243 pitch -26: a
  corner 10 units behind the eye pushed the visible part of the copy past the
  far plane; a GPU readback showed the marking pass left the stencil clear
  there even with its depth test forced to pass, despite depth clamp.
- X -15090, Y 1017, Z 2824, heading 170 pitch -28: every corner was well in
  front of the eye, yet the decal sat more than 8 units off the ground. A
  slope-scaled window (GL polygon offset, like the RDP's) needed a factor near
  64 to stop cutting it, which no longer trims anything.

So the window now applies only to the decals it exists for. `explosion.c`
brackets the bullet-hole and scorch draws with a `G_NOOP` tag (`0x65`, through
`portDecalWindowTag` in `port_bullet_rooms.c`); the renderer keeps
`gfx_ge_dec_window` while inside it, the translucent sort records it per state
(`DXluState.dec_window`), and the backend takes the two-sided path only for
those draws. Level and prop decals keep fast3d's one-sided `LEQUAL` with the
pull, as with `GE_DEC_CLIP=0`. Within the window path, a triangle with a corner
within `max(GE_DEC_TOL, 4 * pull)` of the eye, or behind it, also takes the
one-sided test (a large scorch mark under Bond's feet could have one), and no
pushed corner goes past the far plane. Corners in front keep the original
push. Two earlier attempts the same day (pushing near-eye corners with
`b*tol/(w + tol)`, then capping at the far plane) are superseded; the cap
remains inside the window path.

**Sources:** the decal path in [GL backend](port/fast3d/gfx_opengl.cpp)
(`gfx_opengl_draw_triangles`); the tag handler, `gfx_ge_dec_window` and the
`DXluState` field in [renderer](port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp); the tag helper in
[hole rooms](port/src/port_bullet_rooms.c) and its
[header](port/include/port_bullet_rooms.h); four `#ifndef TARGET_N64` tag calls
in [explosion.c](src/game/explosion.c) (`explosionRenderScorchBuffer`,
`explosionRenderBulletImpactOnProp`).

**Upstream hooks:** the `0x65` `G_NOOP` case and the `dec_window` capture and
replay in `gfx_pc.cpp`; the window condition and near-eye split in
`gfx_opengl.cpp`; the tag calls in `explosion.c`. A future upstream change to
decal emulation should keep level decals one-sided.

**Checks:** isolated copies spawned at each position (`GE_SPAWNXYZ`) reproduced
the cuts with the HD pack and with original textures, and showed none with
`GE_DEC_CLIP=0`. Room lists, texture and palette traces were the same at the
flipping headings. Temporary diagnostics (a per-pixel triangle probe, a
depth/stencil/colour readback inside the decal passes, and env switches for
depth clamp and the marking depth test) were used and removed. After the
change, captures with the owner's settings (3-point, MSAA 2x, tickhz 120,
render thread on) at headings 270 and 272, 241/-13 and 243/-26, 170/-28,
174/-28 and 166/-20, and at X -15116 Z 2652 show the decal whole. Shots into
Statue's ground drew the impact with the window on as with it off. Windows
build only; not checked: bullet holes trimmed at a wall edge, other levels'
decals, the browser build, Linux.

### FORK-076 — Silent audit runs

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-11 at the owner's request, after background
ADS audits played the game's sound while they were working.

Before this change, the hand gallery (FORK-022) already ran its game processes
on SDL's `dummy` audio driver, but the PowerShell audits did not: each launched
an isolated game copy that played music and effects through the real sound
device. All twelve `scripts/port/audit_*.ps1` launchers now add
`SDL_AUDIODRIVER='dummy'` to the environment table they already set before
`Start-Process` and restore afterwards. `audio_pc.c` opens that driver first
and it plays nothing. Each audit's game copy is silent. The caller's shell and
the user's own game keep their audio settings.

`GE_AUDIO_CAPTURE` records the mixed output before it reaches the device, so
`audit_hit_sound.ps1` still measures real audio.

**Sources:** the `$auditEnv` / `$testEnv` table in each of
`scripts/port/audit_{ads,fonts,hit_sound,hitmap,hud,mission_cheats,mission_hints,noclip,projectile_arc,sights,state_effects,states}.ps1`.

**Checks:**
- A KF7 `audit_ads.ps1 -Item 8 -Stage runway` run logged its device opening on driver `dummy` and verified its capture.
- `audit_hit_sound.ps1` with its default distances logged the `dummy` device and recorded a nonzero capture, and its level checks passed.
- A run limited to `-Metres '5,20'` failed the 10% check. It omits the 1 m point-blank reference the check compares against.

### FORK-075 — Hip-Fire Arms: the long guns' ADS arms at the hip

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-11 for
[issue #7](https://github.com/pRizz/Iron-Sights/issues/7) at the owner's
request and built for Windows (`build_win`). The owner's first play-test asked
for better hip grips, a bent rocket elbow and larger non-pistol hands; the
second asked for further grip changes and reported the rocket launcher's
lettering flickering; the third asked for the KF7 fingers out of the gun,
larger arms again and the sniper hand further back, and raised the dual-wield
switch, for which they then chose the lowering support arm (below), the
fifth revision. Temporary renders of an open
KF7 support hand (palm up under the wood, or flat along its side) did not
improve on the closed hand, which the owner kept. Further renders moved the
closed hand lower, out, back or forward, or flattened its finger curl; the
owner found the fingers glitched in all of them. On 2026-11-12 they chose,
from a third round of renders, the KF7 support hand drawn behind the gun and
raised against the wood (below), and approved that sixth revision in
play-test the same day. They then asked for the AR33's support thumb to point
up the hand guard instead of along the barrel, and chose, from four renders,
the hand tilted, raised and out to the guard's side (below). Their play-test
of that seventh revision found it mostly good but asked for the index finger
out of sight, then for the hand closer to the gun and a fuller arm, and gave a
reference photo of their own hand holding a bottle; from the renders that
followed they chose the hand tucked under the guard with a light roll and a
1.3 times fuller forearm (below). Their play-test of that eighth revision
found it mostly good but the wrist too small; on 2026-11-14 they chose, from
four renders, a wrist 1.5 times thicker from palm to back and 1.25 times wider
(below). Their play-test of that ninth revision found it mostly good but
thought a finger might be clipping through the gun, and asked for the hand
slightly lower; it now sits 0.5 lower (below). They then asked why the thumb
tip looked pointy, declined reshaping the model for now, and chose, from
renders of the hand moved left in small steps, 0.25 left (below). They
approved that eleventh revision in play-test the same day. Linux, Steam Deck
and browser builds not run locally.

Inherited behaviour: GoldenEye's rifles, SMGs, shotguns, sniper rifle, laser
and launchers have no first-person hands; the guns float at the hip. FORK-004
adds generated hands and wardrobe forearms to those 14 guns, but only while
aiming: they fade in with the ADS blend (alpha `blend*255`) and their elbows
rise 18 units as they do, so at the hip (blend 0) nothing draws. Players asked
to keep those arms on all the time.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > Aiming and Movement > Hip-Fire Arms** (`[display]
hip_arms`, default 0) keeps them at the hip, opaque. The arm keeps its settled
ADS shape relative to the gun: `adsSettledGun` rebuilds the settled ADS gun
matrix (view-facing basis, ADS pitch and roll, muzzle-derived sight pose, as
the gallery fixture builds it in `gunfire.c`) and `adsGunCarried` carries the
camera-space ADS elbow onto the current gun matrix, so the arm rides rigidly
with the gun through hip fire, bob, raises, lowers, reloads and switches.
Aiming lerps that carried elbow onto the camera-space ADS target; at a settled
ADS the original pose path runs, so ADS pixels are the same with the setting
on or off, and with it off the fade is unchanged. Hands, wrists, scale,
wardrobe meshes, watch and the RC-P90's support-only grip are FORK-004's. Dual
wielding keeps the right gun's trigger hand and slides the support arm away
(below). Off by default because the
stock game has no hip hands and FORK-004's ADS-only arms are the established
look.

The hip camera sees the support hand from above and beside the gun. In the
first play-test the ADS palm-up cradle left fingers floating beside the Klobb,
ZMG, D5K, RC-P90 and shotgun, sank into the assault rifle, held the sniper by
its muzzle, and the rocket launcher's carried arm ran straight to the lower
left corner. A per-gun hip fit (`sAdsHipGrips`) adjusts only the support hand,
fading out linearly as the gun rises: a weapon-local grip offset, extra outward
roll and a carried-elbow offset. After the second play-test (the Klobb's hand
clipped, the KF7's floated, the D5K, AR33, RC-P90 and shotgun hands stood
upright beside the gun, the Phantom's sat too near the muzzle and the sniper's
clipped): the Klobb and ZMG wrap the fore-end's side, rolled out; both D5Ks,
the AR33, RC-P90 and shotgun hold the gun from underneath, palm up; the
Phantom's hand sits 6 units back; the rocket's elbow moves down and towards the
body, bent under the tube. After the third, the KF7's hand sat below its wood
(offset y -1.2), which the behind-the-gun hand below replaced. The automatic
shotgun (approved as is), laser and grenade launcher keep the plain carried
grip. Values came from captured hip frames of three or four candidates per
gun, compared side by side. The trigger hand and settled ADS are unchanged.
The sniper's support grip itself moved in `sAdsGrips`, from the muzzle
(1.7,6,35) to the wooden fore-end (0.1,1,19): as a fading hip fit it slid back
onto the muzzle during the raise, where it clipped (a 4:3 capture showed the old
grip on the muzzle; the new one sits below the screen edge at the hip). The
scope hides both hands once raised, so no settled view changes.
The owner asked twice for larger hands and arms on the non-pistol guns:
FORK-004's base grip scale rises from 0.052 to 0.058 and then 0.065 (about 25%
in all), in ADS and at the hip alike, so the hands keep one size through a
raise.

An open hand for the KF7's support grip was asked for and tried: `GfistZ`'s
flat chop hand loads through the grip-source path, but its native orientation
does not match the grip basis (a blade at the hip and in ADS), so the
experiment was reverted. The pause-watch hand (open, used by these arms before
the closed PP7 hand) remains a possible source; swapping hands between the hip
and ADS would pop during a raise, so it would replace that gun's ADS hand too.
The owner kept the closed hand.

The KF7's glitched fingers: a zoomed hip capture showed the closed hand's
finger tips passing through the fore-end and showing on its near side as pale
shards, and as a white sliver when the raise starts. Moving the hand (lower 1
and 2, out 1, back 3, forward 3) or squashing its finger curl (70% and 55%)
left them, and pressing the vertices onto the wood's underside left shards and
added a spike. What removed them was order: `AdsHipGrip` gains `behind`, and
below a settled ADS such a support hand draws alone before the gun
(`portAdsDrawHandsBehindGun`), so the painter's-order gun covers whatever
overlaps it; the pass after the gun draws only the trigger hand
(`adsHandInPass`). Of three heights rendered, the owner chose the hand raised
1.2 against the wood, so the KF7's fit is offset (0.2, 0, 0), roll 0.2,
behind. Only the KF7 sets it. The cost: no finger shows on the gun's near
side, only the back and heel of the hand beside and below the wood. A settled
ADS is unchanged, and the raise showed no pop at 56%, 78% and 100%.

The AR33's thumb: the closed hand is rigid and its thumb lies along the hand's
axis, which ran from the elbow to the wrist, so under the hand guard the thumb
pointed along the barrel. Rolling the hand out or moving the carried elbow
under it (six renders) barely changed that. `AdsHipGrip` gains `tilt`:
`adsArmPose` leans the support hand's axis towards the gun's up by that much
before building the hand basis, so the hand, wrist seam, cuff and watch turn
together as one rigid piece about the palm, the thumb runs up the guard's left
face, and the generated forearm behind the protected cuff still ends at the
same elbow. Like the rest of a hip fit it fades out linearly with the raise.
Of twelve further renders, more tilt or height (tilt 1.5 and above, or the
hand raised 2.5) pushed finger tips through the guard. The owner chose, from
the current hand and three tilted ones, the hand raised 1.0, out 0.75 to the
guard's left, rolled out 0.5 and tilted 1.0: the AR33's fit is offset
(0.75, -1.5, 0), roll 0.2, tilt 1.0 (was (0, -2.5, 0), roll -0.3, untilted).
Only the AR33 sets it. Tilting lowers the cuff, so more wrist skin shows
between the guard and the sleeve than before.

The AR33's index finger and arm (eighth revision): with the thumb up, the
index finger lay on the guard's lower edge beside it. Rolling the wrist the
other way pushed finger tips through the guard; the behind-the-gun pass hid
the finger but also keeps the thumb off the guard's face; a hard roll (3.0)
hid it, and the owner found that closest, but the hand floated beside the gun
and the arm looked thin. Two causes of the thin arm were found. The wrist and
cuff, one rigid piece with the hand, are flatter than wide, and the roll
turned their narrow edge to the camera (the cuff measured about 32 px across
before and 22 px rolled). And the forearm's cross-section was built in the
hand's frame all the way to the elbow, so the roll and the tilt squeezed the
sleeve (about 75 px to 55 px at the screen's lower edge). For the second,
a tilted hand's forearm now eases from the hand's frame at the cuff to the
plain palm-up frame of the untilted forearm (`adsElbowFrame`, reached by
mid-forearm, `ADS_UNTWIST_RATE`), as an arm's twist fades towards the elbow.
`AdsHipGrip` also gains `girth`, a multiplier on the generated forearm behind
the protected cuff that fades out with the raise. The owner's photo showed a
broad forearm, a thumb gripping the near side and fingers curled round the far
side. The closed fist is rigid and cannot open round the guard, so no finger
shows on the far side; the pose takes the rest. Of the renders (rolls 0.5 to
3.0, the hand 0.5 to 1.0 nearer the gun and up to 0.75 higher, girths 1.3 and
1.6), the owner chose the light roll: offset (0, -0.75, 0), roll 0.7, tilt
1.0, girth 1.3. The hand sits under the guard, which hides the index finger by
depth; the thumb rests on the guard's edge and the wrist keeps its broad side
to the camera. Not done: reshaping the fist's fingers to wrap the guard, which
was offered as a larger experiment.

The AR33's wrist (ninth revision): beside the fuller forearm the owner found
the wrist far too small. Measured in the arm mesh, the wrist and cuff are
about 40 source units from palm to back and 62 across, against a fist of about
80 by 105 or more: half the hand's size, and thinnest from palm to back. Until
now the wrist seam, cuff and watch were fixed with the hand, so nothing could
widen them. `AdsHipGrip` gains `wristDepth` and `wristWidth`, and
`adsWristPoint` scales hand, cuff and watch points about the arm's centre line
before the rigid grip transform, easing in along the last 45 source units of
the hand's heel (`sAdsArmProfile.wristRamp`) and whole from the wrist seam
through the protected band; the generated forearm leaves the cuff at that
scale and blends to its own bulk and girth, so the elbow is unchanged. The
fingers, thumb and palm anchor keep their size, the watch grows with its
wrist, and the scale fades out with the raise, so the aimed view is as before.
Of the renders (current; 1.3 by 1.15; 1.5 by 1.25; 1.7 by 1.35; also 1.5 by
1.5 and 2.0 by 1.4, not shown), the owner chose 1.5 from palm to back and 1.25
across. Only the AR33's hip support hand has a wrist scale; every other gun,
the trigger hand, native pistols and ADS use exactly 1 and take the old path.
This is a deliberate, owner-requested exception to the arm contract's fixed
wrist, cuff and watch, recorded in `scripts/port/arm_rendering.md`.

The AR33's fingertip (tenth revision): the owner thought a finger might be
clipping through the gun. Zoomed Runway captures (960x540) found one: with
the hand 0.75 below the grip point, a fingertip of the tilted hand showed as
a speck about three pixels wide on top of the hand guard at the hip, and as a
longer streak along the guard's front edge while the gun rose. Renders with
the hand 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 and 1.5 lower all cleared the speck at the
hip, and the 0.5 and 1.0 renders, the two zoomed through the raise, also
cleared its first frame; the fit's offset is now (0, -1.25, 0), 0.5 lower,
for margin over the 0.25 that just cleared the hip. The thumb still rests
on the guard's edge and the index finger stays hidden. Still present: about a
third to a half of the way through the raise, a shorter streak of fingertip
shows along the guard's front edge, because the tilt and the offset fade out
together; lowering the hand up to 1.5 shortened it but did not remove it.
Changing how the tilt fades was not attempted.

The AR33's thumb (eleventh revision): the owner asked why the thumb tip
looked pointy. Two causes were found. The closed fist is the game's original
low-polygon hand, whose thumb narrows to a single vertex at its tip; a render
with the hand moved clear of the gun showed the same point. And the hand guard
hides the inner half of the thumb, so only a sliver cut diagonally by the
guard's edge shows. Reshaping the thumb's tip was offered and declined for
now. The owner asked instead for renders of the hand moved left in small
steps, to show more thumb with less clipping. Of 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 and 1.5
left: 0.25 and 0.5 showed slightly more thumb with nothing new through the
guard; at 0.75 an index fingertip showed as a streak on the guard at the hip,
at 1.0 the finger cut through the guard's edge, and at 1.5 the thumb and
index finger both showed, mostly beside the guard. The owner chose 0.25, so
the fit's offset is (0.25, -1.25, 0). The thumb tip is still pointed, and the
mid-raise streak above is unchanged.

Deferred, 2026-11-14: the AR33's thumb-up grip for the KF7. The owner asked
about it, saw six renders and put it off. What the renders showed, for
whoever resumes it:

- It needs only values in the KF7's `sAdsHipGrips` row; the tilt, girth and
  wrist scale already work for any gun.
- Clean: tilt 1.0 at the current fit (offset (0.2, 0, 0), roll 0.2), with the
  hand still drawn behind the gun. The thumb shows as a strip along the wood's
  left edge, not on its face, because the gun covers what it overlaps.
  Adding girth 1.3 and wrist 1.5 by 1.25 visibly broadens the wrist; that
  combination was the suggested pick. The hand 0.5 further left, 0.5 higher
  or lower, roll 0.7 and tilt 0.6 looked much the same.
- Not clean: the hand in front of the gun (AR33's offset (0.25, -1.25, 0),
  roll 0.7, or the KF7's own offset). The thumb and index finger show
  clearly, but the index finger crosses the wood's edge at the hip and
  through the raise; the KF7's fore-end is too narrow to hide it.
- Building it in also means: the checks in `test_hip_arms.c` that only the
  AR33 sets a tilt, girth or wrist scale; the tilted-hand and wrist-scale
  paragraphs in `scripts/port/arm_rendering.md`; and regenerating the
  gallery, whose KF7 Hip-Fire Arms views will change in all six wardrobes.

The renders were Runway stills in the blue wardrobe from a temporary tuning
build; they are not in the repository.

Dual wielding: the first version hid both arms the moment a left gun was
equipped, so with the All Guns cheat picking a 2x gun popped the support hand
away in one frame (and back on return). Of the options offered (fade, lower the
support arm, lower it and keep the trigger hand), the owner chose the last:
`sAdsSupportHold` per player eases over 300 ms towards 0 while a left gun is
equipped and back to 1 after, and `adsSupportLowered` moves the whole support
arm rigidly down, a little left and towards the eye by a smoothstep of that
hold, out of view before the second gun rises from the lower left. The right
gun keeps its trigger hand; the left gun has none (it is a mirrored model and
would need its own grip). The RC-P90, support hand only, shows no arms while
lowered. `portAdsHandsTick` runs at the top of `portAdsTick`, which returns
early when dual wielding. `GE_HIP_DUAL_AUDIT=<item>` (`joy_port.c`) takes up
and puts away the second gun, capturing every 4 ticks; a Klobb run showed the
hand leave in about four frames and return after the left gun lowered.

The rocket launcher's lettering flicker came from this feature. The stock gun
draws without depth testing, in its authored painter's order, so its coplanar
lettering and arrow, drawn after the tube, always show. Hip-Fire Arms put the
gun into the compressed first-person depth layer at the hip, where that
overlay, fractionally under the curved tube, lost the depth test and flickered
or vanished as the gun moved (switching the decal pull and clip off changed
nothing; `LEQUAL` alone fixed only part of it). Now, whenever a long gun has
generated arms and the ADS blend is below 1, its own draw keeps painter's order
with depth writes, and the arms draw after it, testing against that depth. A
settled ADS keeps the depth-tested gun with opaque arms drawn first, as before,
because from behind the gun the authored order paints a sliver of the Klobb's
grip and the rocket's lettering over nearer parts.

**Hooks:** `gunfire.c`'s first-person loop gates the arms on
`portAdsHandAlpha(item)` instead of `portAdsBlend()`, and `gunPainter` (arms
and blend below 1) brackets the gun's draw with `portAdsGunPainterTag` and
draws the arms after it, with one `portAdsDrawHandsBehindGun` call before the
opening tag for a hip support hand the gun is to cover; a settled ADS keeps the
old order (inside
`#ifndef TARGET_N64`; the unused grip locals there are removed). The renderer
(`gfx_pc.cpp`) decodes G_NOOP `0x64` into `s_GeGunPainter`, which clears the
depth compare (so `GL_ALWAYS`, writes kept) while set, beside FORK-058's
`0x5E`-`0x63` viewmodel tags; it applies to every backend through the shared
depth state. In
`ads_hands.c`, `adsNativePose` now wraps `adsArmPose` with `adsElbow` (the
same elbow expressions) and `adsArmPose` takes the support hand's added roll
and tilt (both 0 in ADS; `adsBackTerm` holds the shared back-vector seed and
`AdsArmPose` carries the girth, wrist scale and elbow frame for
`adsGripPoint`, 1 and unused in ADS, with `adsWristPoint` applying the wrist
scale ahead of the rigid branch); `adsHipPose`, `sAdsHipGrips`, the option and `portAdsHandAlpha`
are new, `sAdsArmProfile`'s hand scale is 0.065, the sniper's `sAdsGrips`
support point moved, and `portAdsDrawHands` builds
both grips in one loop (now in `adsDrawHands`, shared with the behind-the-gun
pass). The option
registers in `joy_port.c`'s dispatch, `port_options.c`, the folder (`front.c`)
and watch (`port_watchpages.c`) Aiming and Movement rows after Knife ADS, help
(`port_option_help.c`, which also names it in the page description),
`tools/midas_ini_help.txt`, the default midas.ini writer (`video.c`) and
README.md. `audit_ads.ps1` gains `-HipArms` (its blend-0 transition frames are
the hip poses). The hand gallery (FORK-022) gains 36 hip-arms cells.

**Input:** an ordinary toggle row; keyboard, mouse, gamepad and touch adjust
it like any other.

**Sources:** [arms](port/src/ads_hands.c), [declarations and the opacity
rule](port/include/port_ads.h), the [renderer tag](port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp)
(`s_GeGunPainter`), [contract](scripts/port/arm_rendering.md) and
the [ROM-free test](scripts/port/test_hip_arms.c) (included by `test_ads.c`).

**Checks:** `test_ads.sh` (with the new Hip-Fire Arms checks for all 14 grip
pairs, the hip fits, the painter's-order tag, the dual-wield slide and the
0.065 scale) and
`test_wardrobe.sh` passed in the `goldeneye` container; `settings_placement.py`,
`test_hand_gallery.py` and the Bright Builds checks passed. The Windows build
succeeded; the renderer change is not built for the browser locally. Runway
audits with `-HipArms -Transitions` (blue wardrobe) captured all 23 ADS guns
and 253 transition frames each round; the 14 long guns' hip frames (zoomed on
the support hands), the settled ADS contact sheet, the KF7 raise and the
mid-transition overview were reviewed, and the pistols matched the setting-off
run. Rocket captures with the setting off and on, and after each fix, showed
the lettering missing at the hip before the fix and complete after it. The
regenerated gallery verified all 108 views and 38 icons in both passes. Of the
original 72 images, exactly the 12 KF7/Klobb ADS fork views changed (the larger
hands); the rest, including every stock cell, are byte-identical. Of the 36 new
cells, only the KF7 and Klobb fork cells show arms.

For the KF7's behind-the-gun hand (2026-11-12): `test_ads.sh` (now also
checking that only the KF7's fit is behind and which hands each pass draws) and
`test_wardrobe.sh` passed, and the Windows build succeeded. A Runway KF7 audit
of the built exe (`-HipArms -Transitions`, blue) matched the chosen render in
all 11 transition frames, apart from one to three scattered scenery pixels in
four of them; a tuxedo run also captured. The regenerated gallery changed
exactly the six KF7 hip-arms fork cells and verified all 108 views and 38
icons. The owner's play-test approved it; the browser build is not run
locally.

For the AR33's tilted hand (2026-11-12): `test_ads.sh` (now also checking that
only the AR33's fit tilts, that the tilt leans the support hand's axis towards
the gun's up without moving its palm or elbow, leaves the trigger hand alone
and is gone at a settled ADS) and `test_wardrobe.sh` passed, and the Windows
build succeeded. Runway AR33 audits of the built exe (`-HipArms -Transitions`,
blue and tuxedo) were compared by eye with the chosen render at the hip and at
two raise frames and matched; captures taken under different load land on
different frames, so they were not compared pixel for pixel. The gallery has no
