### FORK-074 — Fog: turn the levels' distance fog off

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-10 at the owner's request, built for
Windows (isolated `build_win/hd-prototype` build) and play-tested by the
owner; committed and pushed to `main` on 2026-11-11. Linux, Steam Deck and
browser builds not run locally.

Inherited behaviour: `fogLoadCurrentEnvironment` (`bgfog.c`) loads a fogged
level's environment: the z range, the fog colour ramp, the sky fog, the
character / prop distance fade (`g_NearFogValuesP`) and the fog radius guards
see within (`g_ScaledFarFogIntensity`, `chraction.c`). Its `GE_NOFOG`
diagnostic already loaded a fogged level as fogless.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > System > Fog** (`[display] fog`, default 1) turns
it off: with Fog off the load takes that fogless path (no fog colour, sky fog
or distance fade). The z range and `g_ScaledFarFogIntensity` are derived
before it, so how far you can see and how far guards see you stay the same;
on Dam the fog only starts at 99.5% of the far distance, so the view barely
lengthens (Noclip View Distance, FORK-072, is what does). Changing the setting
reloads the level's environment on the next `MoveBond` tick through the shared
`portFogReapply` (renamed from FORK-072's `portFogNoclipReapply`), whose
check in `portNoclipTick` now also compares the Fog setting with the state the
level was loaded with. Levels without fog are unaffected. Fog is visual only,
so demo playback follows the setting.

**Hooks:** `fogLoadCurrentEnvironment` records the state with `portFogApply`
and adds `|| !port_fog_on` to the `GE_NOFOG` test (inside
`#ifndef TARGET_N64`). The option registers in `joy_port.c`'s dispatch,
`port_options.c` (beside Glass Reflections, display category), the folder's
System rows (`front.c`) and the watch's (`port_watchpages.c`), with help in
`port_option_help.c` (which also names fog in the System page description),
`tools/midas_ini_help.txt`, the default midas.ini writer (`video.c`) and
README.md.

**Input:** an ordinary option row; every supported input already toggles it.

**Sources:** [header](port/include/port_fog.h), [setting](port/src/port_fog.c)
and the [ROM-free test](scripts/port/test_fog.c) (included by
`test_noclip.c`).

**Checks:** see FORK-073; they were run together.

### FORK-073 — Leaning: Lean Left / Lean Right controls for the stock lean

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-10 for
[issue #8](https://github.com/pRizz/Iron-Sights/issues/8) at the owner's
request, built for Windows (isolated `build_win/hd-prototype` build) and
play-tested by the owner; committed and pushed to `main` on 2026-11-11.
Lean Tilt was added afterwards, play-tested by the owner, and committed and
pushed to `main` on 2026-11-11. Linux, Steam Deck and browser builds not run locally.

Inherited behaviour: the game leans. While `moveData.rLeanLeft` /
`rLeanRight` is set, `bondviewProcessInput` calls
`currentPlayerSetSwayTarget` (-1 / +1, 75 units) and `MoveBond` eases Bond's
body that far to the side, stopped by walls; the camera does not roll. Only
the strafe input in red-reticle aim mode (the port's Move input and the
keyboard's A / D on an N64 slot) and the N64 C buttons set them, so in ADS or
at the hip the Move keys strafe and there was no way to lean.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > Aiming and Movement > Leaning** (`[display]
leaning`, default 1) lets two new held controls set them too, in any stance:
**Lean Left** (`[input] lean_left`, keyboard default Z) and **Lean Right**
(`lean_right`, C), rebindable in Controls on the watch and in the Options
folder. Left wins when both are held, as in the stock code; the stock
aim-mode lean keeps working either way. Not while noclip flies (FORK-072) or
the controls are not live; the lean code itself is skipped in the tank.
The first version added no camera tilt, at the owner's request, because the
stock lean has none; they then asked for it as an option, default off:
**Lean Tilt** (`[display] lean_tilt`: Off 0 by default, Subtle 6, Strong 12
degrees; any whole number up to 20 in midas.ini) rolls the camera around its
line of sight in proportion to how far the body has actually moved (the sway
offset along Bond's right over the full 75 units), so it eases with the lean,
stops where a wall stops it, and follows every lean source. The look
direction, and so the aim and crosshair, is unchanged; the first-person gun is
drawn with its own matrix and stays upright. Not in demo playback or while
noclip flies; each split-screen player rolls with their own lean. Z and C were free on the shipped layout; the Q / E convention of other
shooters was declined because Q is Next Gadget and E is Use, and because
`videoPortBindNewDefaults` leaves a new control unbound when its default key
is already taken in a player's saved binds.

**Hooks:** `bondviewProcessInput` ORs `portLeanInput` into
`rLeanLeft` / `rLeanRight` just before the stock sway-target code (inside
`#ifndef TARGET_N64`). The actions are appended as `PORTACT_LEAN_LEFT` (31)
and `PORTACT_LEAN_RIGHT` (32) in `joy_port.c`, with `portJoyPortLeanHeld`,
the pad-map names in `input_pc.c` (`PM_PORT_LAST` + 32) and Controls rows in
`port_watchpages.c`'s shared `sBindsAllExtra`; the stale "Lean has no action"
comment there is updated. `bondviewMoveAnimationTick` calls `portLeanTilt`,
which turns `headup` around `headlook` (Rodrigues), after the No Head Roll
block so both apply. `video.c`'s `PORT_BIND_MAX` rises from 32 to 64:
`portJoyPortPoll` reads `PORTACT_COUNT` entries from its `pdown[PORT_BIND_MAX]`
arrays, so at 33 actions the 33rd (Lean Right) read a stray stack byte and
pressed at random, which also made the hand gallery's repeated poses differ. The option registers in `joy_port.c`'s dispatch,
`port_options.c`, the folder (`front.c`) and watch Aiming and Movement rows,
help (`port_option_help.c`, which also names leaning in the page
description), `tools/midas_ini_help.txt`, the default midas.ini writer
(`video.c`) and README.md.

**Input:** keyboard (Z, C), mouse (bind buttons) and gamepads (bind
`padN_lean_left`, `padN_lean_right`) can lean; the stock aim-mode lean stays
on every device. Browser touch has no lean controls: as with Noclip, a held
button needs a native touch context, overlay control and fixture audits, so
it is deliberately left for later. A browser keyboard's Z and C work.

**Sources:** [header with the pure rule](port/include/port_lean.h),
[setting and input](port/src/port_lean.c) and the
[ROM-free test](scripts/port/test_lean.c) (included by `test_noclip.c`,
which keeps `test_ads.c` within its line baseline).

**Checks:** in the `goldeneye` Docker image, `test_ads.sh` passes with the
new tests: the lean rule (left, right, left winning, setting off, controls
not live, flying), the default, toggle row, bind slots 31 / 32 and defaults Z
/ C, held controls reaching the game side and releasing; Fog on by default,
one environment reload when it changes and none while unchanged.
`test_hud.sh`, `test_states.sh`, `test_upstream_merge.sh`,
`test_wardrobe.sh`, `settings_placement.py` and `bright-builds-check.ts all`
pass, and the test asserts `PORTACT_COUNT` stays within the 64-entry bind
table. In game (isolated `hd-prototype` build on Dam, a scratch audit with
its own midas.ini): sixteen one-poll Lean Left and Lean Right presses at the
hip, not in aim mode, drove the stock sway (`GE_LEANDBG`) to +63 and -63 of
its 75 units, and an idle run logged no lean;
with `fog=0` the distant canyon walls lost their blue haze (a third of
sampled pixels changed) and the far distance was unchanged. Not checked in
game: holding the keys for a full lean, ADS and moving while leaning,
toggling Fog live from the menus, gamepads, split-screen and other stages.
Lean Tilt: the ROM-free test checks the default, the three choices, the angle
rule (full, partial and clamped leans, off, demo playback, flying) and that
the roll turns up by the setting's angle around an unchanged look; captures
with Strong showed the far barriers sloping down to the right while leaning
left, level with no lean, and up to the right while leaning right.
The hand gallery was regenerated from the isolated build for the
`bondview2.c` and `bgfog.c` input changes with no changed image cells.

### FORK-072 — Noclip: Quake-style flight through walls

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-10 at the owner's request. They play-tested
the first Windows build and asked for rise / fall controls and faster flight,
then play-tested the revised build; committed and pushed to `main` on
2026-11-10. Flying around Dam they saw much of the map vanish slightly too
high or low, so the view distance below was added; they play-tested it and it
was committed and pushed to `main` on 2026-11-10. The room-matrix range fix
for the stray polygons it caused at Dam's spawn was committed and pushed on
2026-11-11 after the owner reviewed it. Linux, Steam Deck and browser builds not
run locally.

Inherited behaviour: Bond always stands on a stan floor tile. `MoveBond`
(`bondview2.c`) turns the head animation's step into a move offset and
`bondviewCalcUpdatePlayerCollision` tests it against the tile edges (walls),
objects, doors and characters; `bondviewUpdatePlayerY` then sets his height
from the tile and applies gravity. The tile also gives his room, which
drives room registration, the rooms drawn and room objectives. The game's
own debug "collisions" switch (`obj_collision_flag`) only drops object,
door and character collision; walls stay.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > Aiming and Movement > Allow Noclip**
(`[display] allow_noclip`, default 0) lets the new **Noclip** control
(`[input] noclip`, keyboard default N, pads unbound, rebindable in Controls
on the watch and in the Options folder) toggle flight for the player whose
control pressed it:

- While flying, the walk step has its forward part tilted along the view's
  pitch (`portNoclipFlyStep`): looking up climbs, looking down dives,
  sideways stays level. It is then scaled to 3x (`PORT_NOCLIP_SPEED`), or 12x
  while Walk / Sprint is held (`PORT_NOCLIP_SPRINT_SPEED`), at the owner's
  request after play-testing the first version. `portJoyPortMoveScale` returns 1 while flying, so the
  walk animation (and its head bob) keeps its normal speed and Sprint,
  Ludicrous Sprint and ADS slowdowns do not apply. Bond moves there with no
  wall, object, door or character test and no gravity.
- Held **Noclip Up** (`[input] noclip_up`, keyboard default Space) rises and
  **Noclip Down** (`noclip_down`, unbound) or Crouch Hold (Left Ctrl) falls,
  at 10 units a field times the same 3x / 12x (`PORT_NOCLIP_CLIMB`,
  `portNoclipClimbFor`); both together cancel. While flying, the crouch step
  (`portJoyPortCrouchStep`) keeps Bond standing instead of crouching, and a
  crouch toggle press is dropped.
- Each tick the highest floor tile below his feet
  (`stanFindTileBelowPos`) becomes his tile, with
  `bondviewUpdatePlayerRoom` and `objectivestatusCheckRoomEntered`, so his
  room, the drawn rooms and room objectives follow him. Above no floor (under
  the level or outside it) he keeps the last tile and room.
- Pressing it again drops him onto the floor below through the normal
  gravity, or, with none below, puts him back where he last flew over one.
- A **NOCLIP** label shows at the top right of his view while flying; a
  press when Allow Noclip is off pops up where to turn it on.
- Never in demo playback, in the tank or once dead (each of those lands him);
  turning the setting off lands every flier; each stage starts on foot
  (`initBONDdataforPlayer`). Tank entry is unavailable while flying.
- **View distance while flying.** Inherited, the rooms drawn come from a
  portal walk from the camera's room (`bg.c`): portals behind the camera's
  side, outside the parent's screen box or past 0.9 of the far distance are
  dropped, and the walk stops at 16 hops. A flier's room is the floor's below
  him, so above the walls or under the floor whole rooms dropped out, and
  Dam's far distance (15,000, fog from 99.5% of it) cut off the rest. Now,
  while any player flies, every room is appended to the drawn set with a
  full-screen box after the walk (`portNoclipAllRooms`, beside the inherited
  `GE_FORCEROOM` diagnostic; at most 150 rooms, inside the 204-entry table),
  and **Noclip View Distance** (`[display] noclip_view`, Normal 1 / Far 4,
  default / Maximum 10) multiplies the level's far distance in
  `fogLoadCurrentEnvironment` before its fog, room cull radius and character
  fade are derived, so they stretch together; fogless levels scale their
  fixed 15-10,000 range. The fog reloads (`portFogReapply`) when
  flight starts or ends or the setting changes. The fog is shared, so in
  split-screen one flier stretches it for everyone.
  The owner then saw the screen fill with stray polygons when flying started
  at Dam's spawn. A room's matrix stores its offset from the camera anchor as
  16.16 fixed point (`setupRoomTransformationMatrix`), so a room more than
  32,767 units away on any axis wraps and draws at the camera; the stock far
  cull never reaches such rooms, but the raised far distance did. While flying,
  rooms outside +-32,000 on any axis (`portNoclipMatrixOffsetFits`) are now
  dropped from the drawn set, whether the walk or the append added them (121
  of Dam's 136 rooms remain at its spawn).
- Mission records and unlocks are unaffected, as with the game's own cheats,
  which do not block saving either.

**Hooks:** `MoveBond` calls `portNoclipTick` after `bondviewProcessInput`;
the on-foot branch calls `portNoclipMove` and jumps past the collision and
step-height code (`port_noclip_moved`) while flying; `bondviewUpdatePlayerY`
is skipped while flying; `initBONDdataforPlayer` (`player.c`) resets the
player; `portHudDraw` draws the label; `bg.c`'s visible-room pass appends
every room while flying; `fogLoadCurrentEnvironment` (`bgfog.c`) loads with
the view multiplier and keeps the unscaled record for `portFogReapply`,
defined beside it. All game-side hooks are inside
`#ifndef TARGET_N64`. The actions are appended as `PORTACT_NOCLIP` (28), `PORTACT_NOCLIP_UP`
(29) and `PORTACT_NOCLIP_DOWN` (30) in `joy_port.c`, with
`portJoyPortNoclipPressed` and `portJoyPortNoclipControls`, the pad-map names in
`input_pc.c` (`PM_PORT_LAST` + 30) and Controls rows in
`port_watchpages.c`'s shared `sBindsAllExtra`. The option registers in
`port_options.c`, the folder (`front.c`) and watch rows, help
(`port_option_help.c`, which also names noclip in the page description),
`tools/midas_ini_help.txt`, the default midas.ini writer (`video.c`) and
README.md.

**Input:** keyboard (N, Space, Left Ctrl), mouse (bind buttons) and gamepads
(bind `padN_noclip`, `padN_noclip_up`, `padN_noclip_down`) can toggle it and
rise or fall; a pad's crouch hold also falls. Browser touch has no Noclip control: the
touch overlay sends only the controls it draws, and adding a button needs a
native touch context, overlay control and fixture audits; deliberately left
for later. A browser keyboard's N works. The launcher's bind list
(`tools/GELauncher.cs`) does not list it, as it does not list the suspend
point actions either.

**Sources:** [header with the pure rules](port/include/port_noclip.h),
[setting, flight and hooks](port/src/port_noclip.c), the
[ROM-free test](scripts/port/test_noclip.c) (included by `test_ads.c`) and
the [in-game audit](scripts/port/audit_noclip.ps1). `GE_NOCLIPDBG=1` logs
flight starts, landings and positions; `GE_NOCLIPDBG_PITCH=deg[,ticks,deg2]` holds the
view pitch while flying (switching after that many ticks), for the audit only;
the audit's `-View` and `-MaxFps` set the view distance and frame cap,
`-UserIni` copies `build_win\midas.ini` and links its HD texture pack (the
junction is removed when the run ends), `-Intro` plays the mission intro and
`-Set` overrides midas.ini keys.

**Checks:** in the `goldeneye` Docker image, `test_ads.sh` passes with the
new test: the fly step (level, climbing, diving, sideways and turned
facings); the gates; the default, toggle row, bind slot 28 and default N; a
press while not allowed only pops the hint; flight follows the floor below
and keeps the last tile above none; landing with no floor restores the last
footing and with one leaves him to fall; 3x flight and 12x with Walk /
Sprint, with the native move scale held at 1; Space rises, Crouch Hold or
Noclip Down falls, both cancel, and Crouch Hold does not crouch while flying;
binds 29 and 30 default to Space and unbound; demo playback, the tank,
turning the setting off and a stage reset land him. `test_hud.sh`,
`test_states.sh`, `test_upstream_merge.sh`, `test_wardrobe.sh`,
`settings_placement.py` and `bright-builds-check.ts all` pass. In game
(isolated Windows build, `audit_noclip.ps1` on Dam; the first version, at
1x, unless noted): walking at a point
about 3,200 units away, noclip went straight through to it while the same
walk without it (press refused) stopped against a wall at x 17,410; held at
+30 and -30 degrees, Bond climbed and dived about 272 units over 502 along
the ground; turning it off in the air dropped him back to the floor (feet
-107), and turning it off under the terrain put him back at his last
footing. With the 3x speed, an unheld flight covered about 1,760 units a
second where the first version covered about 590, and ten one-poll Noclip Up
presses raised his feet 300 units (30 a tick). A capture showed the NOCLIP label and the level drawn around him
high on the cliff. The hand gallery was regenerated for the `bondview2.c`
and `port_hud.c` input changes with no changed image cells, and
`hand_gallery.py verify` passes. View distance (ROM-free): every room while flying, the
multiplier's clamp and default, fog reloads at 4 on take-off, at 10 and 1 as
the setting changes and at 1 on landing. In game, climbing at 25 degrees and
then diving at -35 over Dam: the stock build drew only fog-blue sky where
this one draws the cliffs and terrain; `GE_ROOMLIST` showed 2-10 rooms
before and all 136 of Dam's while flying, `GE_FOG_AUDIT` the far distance
reloaded at 150,000 for Maximum, and no fatal or table errors. At the spawn
point (60 FPS cap, `GE_HITCHMS=1`) GL time per frame went from 6.5 ms on
foot (about 370 draws) to 12.4 ms flying at Maximum (about 656). Not checked:
split-screen, other stages, guards' reactions, rooms far outside the level,
and slower GPUs. Stray polygons at the spawn: reproduced with the owner's
settings (HD pack, MSAA, reflections, 120 Hz, render thread) by skipping the
intro and flying at once, and also with defaults, but not at Normal view;
unaffected by reflections, the HD pack or 16 times the room memory; drawing
only rooms near the camera removed it. With the range check, the same runs at
Far and Maximum draw cleanly and the dive over Dam still shows the cliffs.
The hand gallery was regenerated for the `bg.c` and
`bgfog.c` input changes with no changed image cells.

### FORK-071 — Reload Speed: faster player reloads, up to instant

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-10 at the owner's request, built for
Windows and play-tested by the owner, then committed and pushed to `main` on
2026-11-10. Linux, Steam Deck and browser builds not run locally.

Inherited behaviour: a player reload is four first-person hand states in
`gunfire.c`. RELOAD_START checks the magazine is not full and spare ammo
exists, RELOAD_LOWER tilts the gun down (16 fields at NTSC), RELOAD_SWAP plays
the cock sound (17 fields and at least two ticks) and RELOAD_RAISE refills the
magazine on its first tick and brings the gun back up (23 fields). That is 56
fields, about 0.93 s, and the gun cannot fire until RAISE ends. Each state's
pose is computed from its field timer (`field_890`), which advances by
`g_ClockTimer` per tick.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > Aiming and Movement > Reload Speed**
(`[display] reload_speed`, default 1 = Original) offers 2x, 3x, 5x, 10x and
Instant:

- A multiplier advances the timer of RELOAD_LOWER, RELOAD_SWAP and
  RELOAD_RAISE by that many times the tick's fields, so the same motion plays
  faster. SWAP's two-tick minimum stays. Counted from the state thresholds
  (not timed in game), a 60 Hz reload takes 29 ticks at 2x, 20 at 3x, 13 at
  5x and 7 (about 0.12 s) at 10x.
- Instant (midas.ini `reload_speed=0`) ends LOWER, SWAP and RAISE on the tick
  they start, so the whole reload completes on the tick it begins, through
  the native refill (`sub_GAME_7F0649D8`, which also creates the rocket and
  sets the shotgun's visible shells), cock sound and trigger handling. The
  gun never dips, and with the native automatic reload on an empty magazine
  it keeps firing until the spare ammo runs out.
- midas.ini accepts any whole number from 0 to 10 (the menu snaps an
  unlisted one to the nearest choice); larger values read as 10 and negative
  ones as 1.
- Only the player's reload changes: guards reload through their own
  animations, and weapon switches, the watch and firing keep their timing.
  Demo playback (`get_is_ramrom_flag`) keeps the native reload, since
  recorded input expects it. Multiplayer players share the global setting.

**Hooks** (`gunfire.c`, inside `#ifndef TARGET_N64`, with the N64 build
keeping the inherited code): the `field_890` advance calls
`portReloadSpeedFields`, and `RELOAD_INSTANT()` (`portReloadInstant`; 0 on
N64) is added to the end conditions of RELOAD_LOWER, RELOAD_SWAP and
RELOAD_RAISE. The option registers through `joy_port.c`'s option dispatch,
`port_options.c` (ENUM after Weapon Kick), the folder's Aiming and Movement
rows (`front.c`) and the watch's (`port_watchpages.c`), with help in
`port_option_help.c` (which also names reloads in the page description),
`tools/midas_ini_help.txt`, the default midas.ini writer (`video.c`) and
README.md.

**Input:** an ordinary option row, so every supported input already
adjusts it the way it adjusts Weapon Kick.

**Sources:** [header with the pure rules](port/include/port_reload_speed.h),
[setting and hooks](port/src/port_reload_speed.c) and the
[ROM-free test](scripts/port/test_reload_speed.c) (included by `test_ads.c`).

**Checks:** in the `goldeneye` Docker image, `test_ads.sh` passes with the new
test: the default and menu entry; midas.ini clamping; only the three reload
states are scaled, and START, switch, watch and fire states keep their
fields; Instant applies outside demo playback only; and the menu's first and
last choices set Original and Instant. `test_upstream_merge.sh`,
`test_hud.sh`, `test_wardrobe.sh`, `test_states.sh`,
`settings_placement.py` and `bright-builds-check.ts all` pass. The hand
gallery was regenerated for the `gunfire.c` input change with no changed
image cells (only its input hashes moved), and `hand_gallery.py verify`
passes. Not yet checked in game: how each speed looks and sounds, dual-wield, the rocket
launcher and shotguns at Instant, and raised tick rates.

### FORK-070 — Thrown grenades slide the same at any tick rate

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-10 at the owner's request, after they saw
hand grenades slide well past the Projectile Arc's ring (FORK-069) on Runway
at their raised tick rate. Built for Windows (isolated worktree build) and
play-tested with the Projectile Arc; committed and pushed to `main` with it
on 2026-11-10. Linux, Steam Deck and browser builds
not run locally.

Inherited behaviour (the PC port's raised tick rates): once a thrown object
stops bouncing, `objSettle` (`propobj.c`) sets how fast it turns flat from
how far it spun over the last tick divided by `g_GlobalTimerDelta`, and
`objectTick` slides it a whole field per pass of a `g_ClockTimer` loop with
friction `unk94 * g_GlobalTimerDelta`. The spin (`sub_GAME_7F057DF8`) and the
slide only advance on whole-field ticks. At 60 Hz the step is one field and
a hand grenade loses 0.133 units of speed a field; above 60 Hz the tick's
fraction made the friction too weak (0.056 a field at 144 Hz, so it slid
about 2.4 times as far after turning), and a grenade settling on an
in-between tick measured no spin, so it took the slowest turn the game
allows (about 15 friction-free fields instead of the usual 5). Traced at
144 Hz on Dam, a grenade that stops in the open at 60 Hz slid on about
1,800 units and into a barrier, still moving at 10 units a field.

Now, above 60 Hz only (`portTickHz() != 60`; 60 Hz, demos recorded at it
and the N64 build keep the inherited code):

- each slide pass applies one field of friction (`SLIDE_FRICTION_STEP`,
  `portSettleFrictionStep`);
- `objSettle` measures the spin over the last whole field: each airborne
  tick that spins the object records the axis it spins from and the fields
  it covers (`portSettleSpinNote`, one record per `g_Projectiles` slot), and
  `objSettle` uses that axis and divides by those fields
  (`portSettleSpinPrevious`), so an in-between tick sees what a 60 Hz tick
  would.

This applies to every settling projectile with friction (`unk94`), which in
the game are hand grenades thrown by the player and by guards
(`chraction.c`); objects without it keep the per-field 0.9 factor, which
was already tick-rate independent. No setting: it restores the 60 Hz
behaviour. The Projectile Arc's prediction (FORK-069) follows it.

**Hooks** (inside `#ifndef TARGET_N64`, `propobj.c`): the
`SLIDE_FRICTION_STEP` macro beside `MONITOR_TIMER_DELTA` and its use in the
slide's friction, `portSettleSpinNote` after `objectTick` reads the axis
before the spin, and `portSettleSpinPrevious` plus the divisor in
`objSettle`.

**Sources:** [header with the pure rules](port/include/port_settle_ticks.h),
[game side](port/src/port_settle_ticks.c) and the
[ROM-free test](scripts/port/test_settle_ticks.c) (included by `test_ads.c`).

**Checks:** `test_ads.sh` passes with the new test: the friction step is the
tick's at 60 Hz (2 for a frame of two fields) and one field above it; above
60 Hz a settle on an in-between tick uses the axis from before the last
whole-field spin, over its fields, and before any spin the current axis over
one field; at 60 Hz the game's axis and step pass through. With the isolated
Windows build and `audit_projectile_arc.ps1` on Dam at 144 Hz (`-MaxFps
144`), grenades thrown at -25 degrees came to rest at 18,465-18,526 along x,
in the range 60 Hz throws reach (18,450-18,622 in these runs), where before the change
they slid on to the barrier at about 18,240; a per-tick trace (temporary,
removed) showed 0.133 units of friction a field at 144 Hz and turn rates at
settle spread as at 60 Hz (six of eight at the 0.15 cap). Not checked:
guards' grenades, uncapped and hardware-paced tick rates, and rates other
than 144 Hz.

### FORK-069 — Projectile Arc: predicted grenade, rocket, tank shell, hand grenade, knife and mine paths

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-09 at the owner's request and built for
Windows (isolated worktree build); committed and pushed to `main` on
2026-11-10 after the owner's play-test, numbered FORK-069 (and the slide fix
FORK-070) because FORK-068 had gone to the wall bullet holes on `main`
meanwhile. The owner play-tested the first version
the same day and asked for four changes, made the same day: arcs whenever
the weapon is held (not only while aiming), the rocket launcher too, a
single arc that includes the player's motion (two had shown while moving),
and a tighter ring. On 2026-11-10 the owner asked for hand grenades too,
with their whole path (bounces, roll and fuse), and for the impact burst
to go, keeping the ring; both done the same day (the burst was first
removed in place of the ring by mistake, then swapped). Later that day:
throwing knives and remote, timed and proximity mines; tank shells carried
on foot (the All Guns cheat); and one arc per hand when dual wielding. The second and third rounds are not yet
play-tested. Not yet committed or pushed. Linux, Steam Deck and browser
builds not run locally. The render review gallery has not been regenerated
for these source changes yet; the arc is off by default and skipped while
the gallery captures, so its images are not expected to change.

Inherited behaviour: nothing shows where a grenade round, rocket, tank shell
or hand grenade will go. A grenade round (`gunSpawnGLGrenade` in `gun.c`) and
a tank shell (`gunFireTankShell` in `gunfire.c`) are unpowered and fall at
`PROP_PROJECTILE_GRAVITY_MODIFIER` (0.2778 units per field²). A grenade round
leaves at 33.3 units per field plus the player's motion, bounces off walls,
ceilings and characters with restitution 0.3, and explodes when it lands on a
floor (`objectTick`'s airborne branch in `propobj.c`). A tank shell leaves the
turret's muzzle at 66.7 units per field and explodes on the first wall, floor,
object or character, so it lands short of the crosshair at range. A rocket
(also `gunFireTankShell`) leaves at three fields of its thrust plus the
player's motion and flies under thrust, described under Prediction. A hand
grenade (`generate_player_thrown_grenade` in `gun.c`) leaves the hand at
16.7 units per field along the aim plus 5 upwards and the player's motion,
bounces, rolls to a stop and explodes when its fuse runs out: 240 fields
(`THROWN_ITEM_TIMER_DEFAULT`, US) less the fields the trigger was held, so
holding the trigger cooks it.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > HUD Additions > Arc Impact Crosshair**
(`[display] arc_crosshair`: 0 Off, 1 On; default 0, 2026-11-10, owner's
request; it shipped on by default in `efa5f7a` and the owner turned the
default off the same day), after Projectile Arc in the Options folder and on the watch; a
plain toggle, so every supported input handles it. While the always-on
crosshair is drawn (Always Crosshair, or ADS Crosshair in ADS, or the
multiplayer key with two or more players) and the player holds a weapon
with a Projectile Arc, the cross marks the predicted impact instead of the
aim point: where the round or rocket explodes, the hand grenade bursts, the
knife strikes or comes to rest, the mine sticks or rests. One per hand's
arc. It eases there over about a twentieth of a second (exponential, the
same at any frame rate) so a jumping impact glides; an impact outside the
view keeps it at the edge on the line from the centre towards it; with no
impact (a shot past the prediction's reach) or one behind the camera it
stays at the aim point. Where the level, an object or a door stands between
the eye and the impact (2026-11-10, owner's request), the cross is drawn at
two thirds of its opacity with its arms in dashes marching outward (4 native
units a second), so a grenade lobbed over a wall still shows where it lands
and that it lands out of sight. It also shrinks with the impact's distance
from the eye (2026-11-10, owner's request), as an object there would look:
full size (Always Crosshair Size) up to 350 units, then 350/distance of it,
never under 40% so a far impact stays visible (`portArcCursorScale`,
`PORT_ARC_CURSOR_NEAR`, `PORT_ARC_CURSOR_MIN_SCALE`); the size glides with
the position. The scale multiplies Always Crosshair Size, so the floor is
40% of the player's own size: at 15% a far impact draws a 6% cross, at the
10% minimum 4%, little more than a dot (the stroke stays at least a pixel
wide). That is deliberate: offered an absolute floor that would leave small
crosses unshrunk, the owner kept this as a feature (2026-11-10). Characters do not count, so a guard in
front of the impact, or the one a shot hits, leaves it solid. The prediction
tests the line from the eye (`bondviewGetCurrentPlayersPosition`) to 8 units
short of the impact against the level (`bgTestBulletHitBackground` over the
rooms along it and the visible rooms) and against objects and doors
(`projectileFindCollidingProp` with `CDTYPE_OBJS | CDTYPE_DOORS`), with the
player's own collision off, and records it in `PortArcPath.endHidden`; it
refreshes with the path (at least every 10 ticks). The dashed cross is a new
renderer vector shape, 8 (`port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp`, `G_HUD_VECTOR_EXT`):
shape 1's arms from 1.75 to 7 units out as 1.5-unit dashes with 1.1-unit
gaps, shifted outward by the phase in its `start` parameter, drawn through
`portHudReticleDashed` (`port_hud.c`). It works with Projectile Arc off: the arcs are then
predicted for it but not drawn (`portProjectileArcWanted`). Upstream's
Always Crosshair is unchanged with this off, and the aiming ring (aim mode)
and the scoped Sniper Rifle's mark keep the aim point. The impact is
projected as the game projects its aim (`camGetWorldToScreenMtxf`,
`transform3Dto2DCoords`, then `bondviewAimPinX` into the crosshair's pinned
coordinates), and `port_sight.c` draws the cross there through the same
wide-aim conversion as the aim point (`port_projectile_arc_cursor.c`).
The first build of it hid the gun: `include/math.h` keeps `expf` inside
`#if 0`, so the easing's call was taken as returning `int` and left its
float on the x87 stack each frame until it overflowed and the gun's pose
came out NaN (the launch log showed NaN positions); `port_projectile_arc.c`
now declares `expf` itself, and the arc files compile with no implicit
declarations under `-Werror=implicit-function-declaration`.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > HUD Additions > Projectile Arc**
(`[display] projectile_arc`: 0 Off, 1 On; default 0), after ADS Crosshair in
the Options folder and on the watch. A plain toggle, so every supported input
handles it like the rows around it. One setting for every player; each
player sees only their own prediction. When on:

- **Grenade launcher and rocket launcher, whenever held** in either hand,
  from the hip or aiming. (Until the per-hand slots below, a second
  launcher in the left hand got no arc.)
  (The first version showed the grenade launcher's only while aiming; the
  owner asked for it always.)
- **One arc per hand.** Each player has two slots, the right hand (or the
  tank) and the left hand, each with its own launch, cached path and ring,
  so dual-wielded launchers, knives or mines each show theirs. Both hands
  aim at the crosshair, so two launchers' rings land close together.
- **Throwing knives and remote, timed and proximity mines, whenever held**
  (`generate_player_thrown_knife`, `generate_player_thrown_object`): from
  the hand as drawn, along the crosshair at 25 units a field (knife) or
  16.7 (mine), plus 5 upwards and the player's motion. A knife has no ring,
  as it does not explode; a mine has its ring where it will stick or rest.
  Where a knife will strike a character (2026-11-10, owner's request), a
  see-through orange knife (alpha 170, blade lighter than the grip, 30
  units long but never under 6% of the view's height) sticks out of them at
  the arc's end, its tip a fifth of the way in so the body hides it, flat to
  the camera. It leans at least 50 degrees off the line of sight, turned
  towards the knife's own sideways and downward drift (else straight down),
  since a knife thrown from the eye flies nearly along that line and would
  show end-on as a dot; the real knife spins, so how it sticks is not known
  anyway (`portArcKnifeAxis`). The path records the strike
  (`PortArcPath.endChr`) and the knife's direction (`endDir`).
- **A blast on a character** (2026-11-10, owner's request): where a tank
  shell or rocket will explode on a character (both do on contact,
  `objectTick`), or a grenade-launcher round comes down on one (it only
  turns off a character it meets otherwise, as the game's does), a small
  orange explosion stands at the hit in place of the ring's fence: a star of
  ten spikes, long and short, around a lighter core, flat to the camera,
  lifted towards it out of the body, 24 units across its long spikes but
  never under 4.5% of the view's height, turning and swelling slowly. The
  ring then lies on the floor under the character
  (`port_projectile_arc_world.c` sets `PortArcPath.ringCentre` and
  `ringNormal`; elsewhere they are the impact and its surface), not upright
  through them along the hit's normal. The models record the character hit
  in `endChr`.
- **Tank shells carried on foot** (the All Guns cheat): `gunFireTankShell`
  with no running tank, from the player along the crosshair.
- **Hand grenades, whenever held**, through the throw until the grenade
  leaves the hand (`portProjectileArcGrenadeThrown`), then again for the
  next one. While the trigger is held the fuse shortens with it, so the arc
  shows where a cooked grenade will burst, in the air if need be.
- **Tank, while driving it with the shells selected**, aimed or not.
- **One arc, the trajectory the round will fly, including the player's
  motion.** The game adds the player's motion to a round's launch speed,
  measured as the move over the last tick, and measures it only on frames
  where a tick ran (`g_ClockTimer > 0`). When frames are drawn faster than the
  60 Hz tick (tick rate following a higher `maxfps`), the first version
  dropped the motion on the frames without a tick, so it alternated between
  two arcs while moving; the owner saw both in the tank and walking with the
  grenade launcher. Each player's last measured motion now carries over
  (`arcAddMotion`). Real launches always fall on whole-field ticks, since
  input and the weapon state run at 60 Hz, so a real round always gets the
  motion: at 144 fps while walking, 16 of 16 grenade-launcher and rocket
  launches did, though 58% of frames were in-between ticks. A change that
  let launches on in-between ticks keep the motion (eight hooks in `gun.c`
  and `gunfire.c`) was built on 2026-11-10 and removed again the same day at
  the owner's agreement, because it never changed a launch.
- **The path:** marching orange dashes (36 units on, 24 off), drawn with the
  native tracer's texture and cloud render mode but depth-tested, so walls in
  front of the path hide it. It fades in over its first 240 units so it does
  not start as a blob at the muzzle, and keeps at least 2 pixels of
  half-width with distance. Grenade-round bounces show as separate legs; a
  hand grenade's hops and roll follow its points along the floor.
- **The impact:** an orange ring on the surface hit, where the blast
  does at least half its damage as it starts: half the standard explosion's
  starting reach (`explosion_range`, 300), so 150 units. Damage falls
  linearly from the centre to nothing at the reach, which grows to
  `dmg_range` (480) over the blast. The first version drew the ring at 480;
  the owner found it too big. The first two versions also drew a looping
  burst of the game's spark-explosion frames (`scattered_explosions`) as a
  HUD sprite at the impact; the owner asked on 2026-11-10 for it to go.
  The owner then found the ring hard to see far off: it lies nearly edge-on
  there, a band flat on the floor thins to nothing at its near and far
  sides, and only 2 units up the depth test broke it into dots against the
  floor. Since 2026-11-10 its line is camera-facing strips like the dashes
  (at least 4 pixels wide, as opaque), over a dark halo twice as wide so it
  reads on light and dark floors, around a faint orange fill flat on the
  surface, and lifted 2 units plus 0.4% of its distance. Captures on Dam at
  about 600 and 1,950 units show it as a solid line where it had been a
  dotted sliver. At the owner's request a see-through orange fence also
  stands on the ring, along the surface normal (upwards on a floor), 45
  units tall but never under 18 pixels on screen, fading from 31% opacity (first 47%; the owner asked for less)
  at its foot to nothing at its top; it does not flatten from afar, and
  the captures show it at both distances, over the barrier a grenade
  stops against. The ring is drawn in the world pass, so down the sights, where the impact lies
  right behind the launcher, the weapon can cover it. When the round would
  fly past the prediction (160 fields for a shell, about 10,700 units; 240
  for a grenade round; 200 for a rocket) there is no ring. A hand grenade
  always has one, where its fuse ends.
- The prediction aims along the crosshair without the launchers' random
  spread (`bullet_path_from_screen_center` draws the game RNG), so it shows
  the round's average path.

Down the sights the path itself projects to a short line straight below the
crosshair, right behind the launcher or the tank's barrel; from the hip it
runs out from the muzzle. A second, undepth-tested pass of the whole
overlay after the gun was tried and removed: the weapon pass lands on top of
anything drawn after it in `gunRenderFirstPersonGunModels`. (That is why the
removed burst had been drawn in the HUD pass.)

**Prediction.** `port_projectile_arc.c`, `port_projectile_arc_rocket.c` and
`port_projectile_arc_thrown.c` are ROM-free: the option, the flight models
and the dash layout.

- *Shells and grenade rounds:* the model samples the exact parabola (the
  game's trapezoidal step is exact for constant acceleration, so the path is
  the same at any tick rate) in steps of three fields for a shell and two
  for a grenade round, testing each step's chord. The step that first dips
  below the floor is flown again one field at a time, as the game moves a
  round, against a floor clearance measured from the game's blasts (8.2
  units for a shell or rocket, one model, 5.5 for a grenade round: the game
  explodes a round once its origin is within its model's bottom offset of
  the floor, then lifts the blast 4 units above that). Grenade-round bounces
  follow `objectTick`: the speed is reflected about the hit normal with
  restitution 0.3; it explodes when it was falling and the bounce sends it
  up or leaves it no lower; an object or character hit leaves it at the
  tick's start position at the tick's new height, as
  `handles_projectile_motion` does. Up to five bounces are predicted.
- *Rockets* fly no parabola, so `portArcSimulateRocket` steps the game's
  integrator a field at a time (60 Hz ticks) and records each position as a
  polyline. While boosting (`PROJECTILEFLAG_00000020`) an ideal height climbs
  under the thrust alone while a lift ramps from 0 to gravity at 1/90 a
  field, so the rocket dips at first, then closes 7% of its gap to the ideal
  height a field (from a level shot it settles about 50 units under the aim
  line, as in the game); on reaching it, it is powered and accelerates along
  its thrust. Thrust stops once its speed² passes
  `ROCKET_SPEED_BREAK_THRESHOLD` (about 167 units a field) and after
  `GRENADE_SMOKE_FRAMES` (301 fields, US/JP) it loses lift and power and
  falls. It explodes like a shell. The floor is checked every field and
  collisions on three-field chords, the costly part, with positions past a
  hit dropped.
- *Hand grenades* (`portArcSimulateThrown`) step `objectTick` a field at a
  time to the end of the fuse (it explodes the tick after its timer runs
  out), recording each position. In the air it falls like a round; what it
  hits reflects its speed with restitution 0.3 (`Projectile.unk8C`), and it
  bounces once its origin dips 8.2 units over the floor, or on a hit that
  leaves it no lower while falling: it is placed 4 units above that height
  and its vertical speed reversed times 0.3, a first bounce hopping at least
  2.22 units a field and a slower later one settling it (`objSettle`).
  Settled, it slides at its horizontal speed while it turns flat, then loses
  0.133 units of speed a field (`unk94`) until it stops, resting 8.2 units
  over the floor. At 60 Hz the game scales that friction by the tick's step
  (`g_GlobalTimerDelta`), so a frame that runs two fields applies twice the
  friction each pass; the prediction follows (`slideFriction`, by the step
  of recent whole-field ticks, `portProjectileArcNoteTickStep`, smoothed and
  rounded to 0.02). Above 60 Hz the game used to scale it by the tick's
  fraction and slide grenades about 2.4 times as far at 144 Hz, which the
  owner saw on Runway, the ring well short of where grenades stopped;
  FORK-070 makes it a whole field's friction there, as the prediction now
  assumes. Settled objects move with `objTryMovePropWithCollision`,
  not the airborne point test, so the slide asks a new `slide` world
  callback that makes the same stan calls (the line to the target and the
  object's width there against walls, objects, doors and characters; when
  blocked, the move to its width short of the edge it met, width 10 from
  `objGetWidth`). *Knives and mines* use the same model with their own
  values: restitution 0.1 (`unk8C`), no `unk94`, so a settled one keeps
  `PROJECTILE_FRICTION_FACTOR` (0.9) of its speed a field; measured rest and
  bounce heights 5.2 (knife) and 5.5 (mine); turns of 8 and 6 fields, the
  medians of traced settles (knives 5 to 15, mines 5 to 9). A mine sticks to
  the first wall, ceiling or object it hits (`handles_projectile_motion`
  returns 2 when it may embed), not to a character (it falls past without
  bouncing). The level's floor usually catches it first: the game catches a
  falling object once a tick ends inside its clearance over the floor (the
  bottom of its bounding box as it spins, `chrpropSumMatrixPosY`), and it
  hops and slides like a grenade; it sticks only when one tick's drop takes
  it from above that band to below the floor. That hangs on where the ticks
  fall and on the random spin, so the model stepping through it flipped
  between sticking and hopping as the aim moved a hair (the owner saw the
  arc flicker and every mine hop, 2026-11-10; at 144 Hz a tick moves it
  60/144 as far, so nearly every mine is caught). The model now decides by
  the likelier: it sticks to the floor only once a tick's drop (the fall
  speed times `PortArcLaunch.tickStep`, the game's `g_GlobalTimerDelta`)
  exceeds twice the band it is caught in, `PORT_ARC_MINE_CATCH` 10, which
  takes a fall from a ledge; otherwise it hops. The band comes from the
  stick rate: at 60 Hz, throws falling 12.8 units a tick stuck about one
  time in five. (The first model let mines stick to the floor and put -15
  degree throws 500 units short; the clearance fix after it still predicted
  sticks the game seldom makes.) A knife's flight ends on the first character it meets before
  any bounce (`handles_shot_actors`); the world's hit now says whether it
  was a character (`PortArcHit.chr`). A field that finds the object under
  the floor's clearance is flown again with the hit test, since a chord
  between placed positions misses a floor crossing. The friction-free turn lasts as long as the landing spin
  allows: the throw spins the grenade randomly (`sub_GAME_7F057C14`). Of ten
  traced settles at 60 and 144 Hz (the latter with FORK-070), six turned at
  the game's fastest rate (5 fields) and the rest took 6 to 11, so the model
  uses 5: most grenades stop where the arc ends and the rest slide a few
  fields past it, never short. (It used 7 before, the middle of the first
  three traces.)
  The bounce and rest heights were measured from traced grenades. In the
  air, collisions are tested on three-field chords, and a chord that hits
  is flown again a field at a time.

`port_projectile_arc_launch.c` takes the launch where the game takes a real
one: a grenade round's or rocket's at the end of `gunUpdateAndFireBothHands`
(muzzle `field_B58`, `gunWeaponFovLaunch`; a rocket's thrust `D_80053DDC`
along the aim, launch speed three fields of it, or the recorded cadence in
demo playback); a hand grenade's there too, from the hand as drawn
(`throw_item_pos_related`, within about 4.4 units of the release point) with
its fuse less the fields held (`field_890` while the trigger is down,
`last_z_trigger_timer` during the throw); a tank shell's from the turret
(`bondviewSet3dCoord7F07CEB0`, model matrix 4) right after that player's
`propsTick` in `lv.c`, where `chraiCheckUseHeldItems` fires it, because by the
gun pass the tank's model matrices are no longer valid (reading them there
gave garbage). It was split out of `port_projectile_arc_world.c` to keep that
file within the line limit. `port_projectile_arc_world.c` predicts the
flight right after `propsTick` too, for each player, with the queries a real
round uses each tick: `bgTestBulletHitBackground` over the rooms along the
step plus the visible rooms (nearest hit; the game keeps the last valid one,
which only matters where rooms overlap), then `projectileFindCollidingProp`
for objects and characters, the stan floor via
`walkTilesBetweenPoints_NoCallback` / `stanFindTileBelowPos`, and, for a
settled grenade, `stanTestLineUnobstructed`, `stanTestVolume`,
`getCollisionEdge_maybe` and `calculateRayToSegmentIntersectionNormalized`.
Running it during the gun pass crashed: a character's hit list
(`ChrRecord.field_20`) is rebuilt by its tick in `propsTick` and freed again
while it draws, and the game's character test (`sub_GAME_7F041BB8`) does not
check for a missing one. The player's own collision is switched off as for
their own round (`sub_GAME_7F03D058`), rounds already in the air are passed
through (temporary `PROPFLAG2_THROWTHROUGH`; otherwise the prediction
bounced off the previous grenade), and the collision scratch state
(`stanSavedColl_*`, `g_portBlock*`, `D_80030B0C` and the projectile hit
globals) is put back, as `gunWeaponFovClearFrac` does. Nothing draws the game
RNG or changes game state, so demos and multiplayer stay in step. A path is
reused while the launch (and a hand grenade's fuse) holds still, refreshed
every 10 ticks so doors, guards and vehicles moving into it still show. When
the muzzle is behind something (the game would spawn the round at the
player) no path is shown.

**Hooks** (all inside `#ifndef TARGET_N64`): `lv.c` calls
`portProjectileArcTick` after `propsTick` beside the hit-map probe;
`gunfire.c` calls `portProjectileArcNoteLaunch` at the end of
`gunUpdateAndFireBothHands` and `portProjectileArcRender` at the start of
`gunRenderFirstPersonGunModels` (not during the hand gallery);
`gunFireTankShell` (`gunfire.c`, US/JP copy only), `gunSpawnGLGrenade`,
`generate_player_thrown_grenade`, `generate_player_thrown_knife` and
`generate_player_thrown_object` (`gun.c`) call `portProjectileArcShotFired`,
and `objectTick` (`propobj.c`) calls `portProjectileArcExploded` as a fired
round explodes; these only log, under `GE_ARCDBG`, except that a hand
grenade leaving the hand ends its throw's arc. The option is read and
written through `joy_port.c`'s option dispatch; `video.c` writes its default
into a new `midas.ini`.

**Diagnostics.** `GE_ARCDBG=1` logs, per round fired, the drawn arc's launch
(and its offset) and impact against the round's real launch, the flight
model's impact from that real launch, and where it really exploded (3D and
ground distances, at the round's own position, where `propExplode` puts the
blast; a round that has left the stan keeps a stale prop position). It also
logs the prediction's cost every 240 predictions, and how many frames had no
tick and kept the carried motion and how often that motion jumped
(`port_projectile_arc_log.c`, `port_projectile_arc_launch.c`).
`GE_ARC_AUDIT` (`port_projectile_arc_audit.c`, desktop video builds only)
turns the arc on in memory, equips the grenade launcher or (`rocket`) the
rocket launcher or (`grenade`, `knife`, `mine`, `shells`) hand grenades,
throwing knives, remote mines or tank shells on foot (`GE_ARC_AUDIT_DUAL`,
`-Dual`: the same in the left hand), holding aim only with
`GE_ARC_AUDIT_ADS`, or (`tank`) boards the level's tank and selects the
shells, steps the pitch, and requests screenshots. `GE_ARC_AUDIT_FACE`
(`-FaceChr`) turns the player each tick towards the nearest living character
in a shared room at least 250 units off, counting the pitches from the line
to its feet; `GE_ARC_AUDIT_STRIKE` (`-StrikeMarker`) draws the character-hit
marker (the stuck knife, or a round's or rocket's burst with the fenceless
ring) at every arc's end, 50 units up as if at a character's chest, to
capture its look without a character in view (finding one in clear view
from a spawn point proved unreliable); `GE_ARC_AUDIT_HIDDEN`
(`-HiddenCross`) draws every Arc Impact Crosshair as out of sight; each
capture logs the right hand's impact and whether it is out of sight, and
the prediction-cost line counts out-of-sight impacts; `GE_ARC_AUDIT_NOARC` (`-NoArc`)
leaves the arc itself off, for the Arc Impact Crosshair alone (with
`GE_ALWAYSCROSSHAIR=1` in the environment);
`scripts/port/audit_projectile_arc.ps1` runs it from a copied executable in
an isolated `build_win/arc-audit-*` folder with `GE_AUTOFIRE` (or `-NoFire`),
optionally drawing faster than the tick while walking about (`-MaxFps`,
`-Drive`), never touching the user's settings, and removes the copy
afterwards. `GE_AUTOFIRE` presses the trigger for 30 of every 120 polls
(drawn frames); `GE_AUTOFIRE_PERIOD=n` (`video.c`, debug input only)
changes the 120, and the script sets ten seconds' worth for hand grenades:
the first grenade audit threw every two seconds with a 3.5-second fuse, so
each blast set off the next grenade in mid-air, and at 144 Hz a five-second
cadence still let a grenade roll into the previous blast while it burned.

### FORK-068 — Wall bullet holes draw on the wall they hit

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-09 in the Windows build after the owner saw
bullet holes on Dam's walls stay invisible from a distance, appear only when
walking closer, and vanish again when turning away. The owner play-tested the
fixed build and approved it the same day. The browser player, without the HD
pack, never showed it.

Two separate causes, both fixed:

- **The HD pack's bullet hole (the main cause, a fork regression).** Brick and
  stone hits use `IMAGE_IMPACT2` (`s_impactimages[1]`), a 64x32 IA8 strip that
  holds a 32x32 crater plus its smaller mip levels; the game stretches the
  32x32 square over each hole's quad. The 2026-11-07 coverage audit (FORK-053,
  `9b9a862`) added the pack's `GOLDENEYE#8E4AB4BE#3#1` to the download scope,
  but that image is a different design: one small hole (about 15x10 at native
  scale) in the middle of the whole strip. Only its edge falls in the sampled
  square, so each hole drew as a sliver a few pixels wide beside the impact,
  which appeared or vanished as distance and camera angle changed its screen
  coverage. That audit had not checked the bullet hole in play. It is removed from `hd_effect_sources.json`, so the original hole
  draws with the HD pack on; the other impact effects keep their HD art. A
  custom pack that names the key still replaces it.
- **Room filing (inherited from upstream).** Upstream files each wall hole under
  one room (`bestroom` in `chrprop.c`) and draws it only while that room is
  drawn (`explosionRenderBulletImpactOnProp`, `getROOMID_isRendered`). A wall
  surface can exist in more than one room, and the hit search keeps the first
  copy it finds. Temporary logging in the owner's session showed nine holes
  filed under room 114 toggling between drawn and skipped while the owner stood
  in room 123. The PC build now also draws a wall hole while any drawn room has
  geometry right at it: when the hole's own room is not drawn, each drawn room
  is probed once per hole with a 16-unit segment through the hole along the
  wall normal (`bgTestBulletHitBackground`), and the answer is cached per hole.
  A first version that only compared rooms drawn at the moment of the shot
  missed rooms first seen later and was replaced. Holes on props, the hit
  search, impact sounds, sparks and the RNG are unchanged, and the N64 build
  keeps upstream's check. There is no setting.

**Upstream hooks:** `chrprop.c` calls `portBulletImpactNoteWall` (hit point and
normal) just before a wall hole's `explosionCreateBulletImpact`; `explosion.c`
calls `portBulletImpactAssign` as the slot is filled and
`portBulletImpactRoomDrawn` in place of the room check when drawing. All three
sit inside `#ifndef TARGET_N64`. The per-slot table is registered for suspend
images (`embed_state_layout.py` `PORT`), so a loaded suspend point keeps it with
the hole buffer it describes.

**Sources:** [hole rooms](port/src/port_bullet_rooms.c),
[interface](port/include/port_bullet_rooms.h), [hit hook](src/game/chrprop.c),
[create and draw hooks](src/game/explosion.c),
[suspend layout](scripts/port/embed_state_layout.py),
[HD effect scope](port/fast3d/texture_packs/hd_effect_sources.json).

**Checks:** the Docker MinGW Windows build compiles without warnings in the
touched files; `test_state_layout.py` passes and the link map shows the table's
`.bss` in the new object. Two owner sessions with temporary logging (since
removed) separated the causes: after the room fix, no hole was ever skipped,
yet holes still did not show. The owner's input recordings did not replay
deterministically (position drift from about tick 1950), so later checks spawned
Bond at the owner's recorded firing positions with the owner's settings
(isolated folders, `GE_SPAWNXYZ`). From about 725 and 2700 units, holes at the
crosshair were invisible with the HD pack on, unchanged by `GE_DEC_CLIP=0`,
`GE_XLU_NOPIN=1`, `GE_NOXLUSORT=1` or MSAA off, and appeared with
`texture_pack=0`. `GE_HD_TRACE` showed `8E4AB4BE` matched to a 256x128 image
before the fix and kept native after it, with the hole visible near and as
small marks far. A camera sweep across the holes (about 725 units, stick turn
after firing) showed the original texture at every sampled angle; the same
sweep with the pack's image restored as a custom pack showed none, and a
head-on capture from about 200 units showed the original's full crater against
the HD image's small clipped fragment. In the owner's second session (lazy
probes on), main-wall holes no longer toggled; one hole on a side face held by
room 114 alone still followed that room, whose face is undrawn whenever the
room is. Private captures were kept in ignored `build_win/holes-*` until the
2026-11-14 build-folder cleanup (FORK-001) removed them.

### FORK-067 — Player options survive a stage started before the saves are read

**Status:** Fixed on 2026-11-09 after the owner saw the corner ammo missing on
an iPad, with a one-time repair for settings already zeroed. Verified in the
Windows build and in a local web build (tablet and phone viewports).

The missing ammo was not the touch clearance of FORK-028. The game had switched
**Ammo On Screen** off, together with Auto-Aim, Sight On Screen and Look Ahead,
on every platform where a stage started before the title: the web player's
first-startup weapon icon stage (FORK-019, `91640bc`, 2026-11-07) and the
`GE_STAGE` / `GE_ICON_STAGE` harnesses. Each stage start loads the selected
folder's settings (`options.c` -> `fileLoadSettingsForFolder`). Before
`fileValidateSaves` has run, `saves[]` is all zeros, which
`fileGetSaveForFoldernum` accepts as the first folder's save with every option
bit clear. Upstream's global player options (`video.c` `s_CfgPlayerOpt`) are
then seeded from that load, so the zeros were written to `midas.ini` as
`auto_aim=0`, `sight_on_screen=0`, `look_ahead=0` and `ammo_on_screen=0`, and a
later real folder load, which only seeds unset keys, never corrected them. A
captured web `midas.ini` after a fresh start held exactly those values; a
native debug log traced the write to `fileLoadSettingsForFolder` reading slot
0 with options `0000`.

`file2.c` now records that `fileValidateSaves` ran (`s_PortSavesRead`), and
until then `fileLoadSettingsForFolder` skips the unread slots (demo playback's
RAMROM slot still loads) and applies the player's global options instead.
Both changes sit inside `#ifndef TARGET_N64` in this upstream file.

Settings already written as zeros by an affected build are repaired once, at
the owner's request (the owner's own iPad was affected). When `midas.ini` is
read, `videoRepairPlayerOpts` (`port/src/video.c`) checks for the bug's mark:
`auto_aim`, `sight_on_screen`, `look_ahead` and `ammo_on_screen` all present
and all 0. It sets the four back to 1, logs the repair, and writes the ini-only
marker `[display] player_opts_repaired=1`. The marker is written on the first
read of any existing `midas.ini`, repaired or not, so the repair never runs
twice. A fresh install has no `midas.ini` yet and writes the defaults instead;
the next start adds the marker. Trade-off: a player who deliberately switched
all four off gets them back on once, and the marker keeps the repair from
undoing that choice again. Auto-Aim back on does not give a mouse player
auto-aim, because `mouse_auto_aim` (default off) still decides that. A device
record (`Data/Devices/*.gedevice`) that saved `auto_aim=0` while affected can
still apply it when that device next becomes player 1. Like every ini write,
the marker and the repaired values are not saved during `GE_WINDOW` /
`GE_NOINISAVE` harness runs; those runs apply the repair in memory only. The
marker is internal, so it has no menu row, help line or
`settings_placement.py` entry.

**Sources:** [save settings](src/game/file2.c), the
[ini repair](port/src/video.c) and the
[touch audit](web/tools/touch-game-audit.mjs). The audit now waits for the icon
stage before navigating; it had been mistaking that hidden Dam stage for the
player's mission. It snapshots `midas.ini` once the icon stage is running and
fails unless the file is byte-identical when the stage ends. It also fails if
the icon stage or the first folder leaves any of the four options off. The render review gallery's fixture
(`scripts/port/hand_gallery.py`) starts its captures with `GE_STAGE`, so its
references had been taken with the counter hidden by this bug; the fixture
now sets `ammo_on_screen=0` beside its other hidden HUD overlays
(`sight_on_screen=0`, `weapon_hud=0`, `always_health=0`), keeping the images
unchanged. Without it, the fix added the counter to all 72 images and nothing
else.

**Checks:** The native HUD audit (`GE_HUD_AUDIT=4` on Dam) logged
`ammo-hide=1` (the option reason) before the fix and `ammo-hide=0` after, with
the counter drawn at the bottom right. Web (local `web_build.py video` build
served by `serve-site.mjs`, Edge): before the fix, a fresh profile's
`midas.ini` held the four zeros and neither the 1024x768 tablet nor the 844x390
phone viewport drew the counter; after it, `touch-game-audit.mjs` with
`MIDAS_TABLET=1` passes end to end (it had been failing at its intro check
since the icon stage arrived) and its tablet capture shows the counter with the
N64 cluster lifted above it by FORK-028. `test_hud.sh`,
`test_upstream_merge.sh`, `test_states.sh`, `settings_placement.py` and
`bright-builds-check.ts all` pass; the gallery regenerated with every image
identical to before (new manifest and index) and verifies. The repair was
checked with an isolated Windows build, a copied executable and seeded
`midas.ini` files, without the harness's ini guard. The four zeros came back as 1
with the marker written and the repair logged. A marked file with the four
zeros was left alone. Three zeros with `auto_aim=1` was left alone and only
gained the marker. The audit's unchanged-`midas.ini` check passes on the
fixed web build at the tablet viewport. With the `file2.c` guard temporarily
disabled, it failed with "The hidden icon stage wrote midas.ini". A
follow-up audit compared Windows first starts with and without the icon stage
(web-style starting `midas.ini`, an empty icon cache). `midas.ini`, the save
file and the device files came out the same, and the hidden stage made no
save writes. Not run: a physical iPad, the phone viewport audit after the
fix, WebKit, and the repair in a browser build. The repair uses the same C
code on the web.

### FORK-066 — Glass Reflections: the level reflected in glass and shards

**Status:** Spike implemented on 2026-11-09 at the owner's request ("all glass a
bit more reflective, and the shards when it breaks"); Windows built and
captured in an isolated folder, not yet play-tested, Linux and browser not
built locally.

Upstream already sphere-maps glass: shards (`glass.c` `glassRenderShards`)
draw with `G_LIGHTING | G_TEXTURE_GEN` and the shared `glassoverlayimage`, their
vertex colours standing in for normals, and the glass props' own display lists
turn on texture generation and lighting too (logged: `texgen=1 lit=1` with
blending for every glass prop triangle seen on Facility and Archives). Neither
reflects the level. Glass props are `PROPDEF_GLASS` (Archives' office windows,
Facility's lab glassware) and `PROPDEF_TINTED_GLASS` (Facility and Control
windows); windowed doors (`DOORFLAG_WINDOWED`) carry glass too.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > System > Glass Reflections** (`[display]
glass_reflections`: 0 Off, 1 On; default 1), after Gun Glint in the Options
folder and the watch. On, glass props and window doors (their blended,
see-through triangles only, so a door's frame keeps its look) and every broken
shard are drawn a second time, additively, like the Gun Glint pass: per pixel,
the view ray reflected off the face samples the level reflection cube of
FORK-058, weighted by Schlick's Fresnel term (head-on reflectance `glass_f0`
0.25, rising to full at a glancing angle), plus a soft Blinn-Phong highlight
from a world-fixed overhead light (`glass_glint` 0.6, `glass_power` 96). Shards
take a stronger look (`glass_shard` 1.25, `glass_shard_f0` 0.6) so they flash as
they tumble. The reflection fades with the game's fog on fogged draws. Off,
glass draws exactly as upstream (no tags are acted on). It is an ordinary
toggle row, so keyboard, mouse, gamepad and touch adjust it like any other.

- **Spans.** `port/src/port_glass.c` emits G_NOOP `0x63` with the kind in the
  low byte (1 pane, 2 window door, 3 shards; 0 closes), preceded by the sky
  colour tag `0x60` for the cube's empty space. Two hooks call it, inside
  `#ifndef TARGET_N64`: around `sub_GAME_7F04AC20` at the end of the object
  render in `propobj.c` (for the kinds `portGlassKindOfObject` names) and
  around the shard loop in `glass.c`.
- **Renderer.** `gfx_pc.cpp` decodes the tag (`gfx_glass_span`), builds this
  frame's cube if no span has yet, and turns the overhead light into camera
  space from the projection (GoldenEye keeps the camera rotation there,
  C = R x Pp). Inside a span, `gfx_sp_vertex` records camera-space positions
  from the clip ones (x / sx, y / sy, -w, with sx and sy the projection's
  column lengths, so no modelview split is needed), `gfx_sp_tri1` adds each
  glass triangle's corners (face normal turned to the viewer) to a buffer, and
  `gfx_flush` hands it to the backend's new optional `glass_draw`
  (`gfx_rendering_api.h`), implemented in `port/fast3d/gfx_glass.inl` (ONE/ONE,
  depth tested LEQUAL, not written; every GL state touched restored).
- **Shared cube.** `roc_env_cube` (`gfx_envcube.inl`) now remembers the frame
  and size it built for and returns that result to later spans in the same
  frame, so glass and the shiny guns share one cube per frame (the gun's span
  previously always rendered its own). `gfx_shiny_level_cube` asks for the
  room cache's capture-only mode 3 when either Richer Reflections or Glass
  Reflections is on, and `video.c` re-applies the mode when the glass setting
  changes.
- **Tuning.** `shiny_weapons.ini` (re-read twice a second) gains `glass`,
  `glass_f0`, `glass_shard`, `glass_shard_f0`, `glass_glint`, `glass_power`,
  `glass_blur` (cube mip level, 1) and `glass_split` (review aid: 1 applies the
  pass to the right half of the screen only, for an exact A/B in one frame),
  documented in `tools/midas_ini_help.txt`. They are file-only tuning keys, so
  they need no `settings_placement.py` entry or input handling.
- **Limits.** The cube holds only the level's rooms (no props, characters or
  glass) and is centred on the camera, so a pane does not mirror its own
  surroundings exactly; kept light, it reads as glass. Glass that is part of
  the level geometry (surfaces with the `HIT_GLASS_XLU` sound) is not covered,
  nor CCTV lens glass. With `room_cache = 2` (replay), model parts that the
  cache replays skip the interpreter and would skip the pass; the PC default
  (0) is unaffected. The cube costs 0.3-0.9 ms of CPU in a debug build on
  frames where glass or a shiny gun is drawn (FORK-058's measurement).

**Sources:** [tags](port/src/port_glass.c) with their
[header](port/include/port_glass.h), [prop hook](src/game/propobj.c),
[shard hook](src/game/glass.c), [renderer](port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp),
[glass pass](port/fast3d/gfx_glass.inl), [shared cube](port/fast3d/gfx_envcube.inl),
[backend API](port/fast3d/gfx_rendering_api.h), [backend](port/fast3d/gfx_opengl.cpp),
[API globals](port/fast3d/gfx_api.h), [tuning](port/fast3d/gfx_shiny.cpp) and
its [header](port/fast3d/gfx_shiny.h), [setting](port/src/video.c),
[options](port/src/port_options.c), [frontend row](src/game/front.c),
[watch row](port/src/port_watchpages.c), [help](port/src/port_option_help.c),
[ini reference](tools/midas_ini_help.txt) and the
[review gallery](review/hand-gallery/index.html).

**Checks:** The Windows build (isolated `build_win/hd-prototype`) compiles and

### FORK-065 — CI retries for transient network failures

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-09; ROM-free tests pass locally. Whether CI
stays green depends on the next runs.

Three of the last four `Windows builds and provenance` runs on `main`
(`ed0374a`, `2e4e578`, `d0eb2b8`) failed on the network, not the code:
GitHub release downloads answered `504 Gateway Time-out` (the Linux job's SDL
source and AppImage runtime, and the Sentry CLI for the Windows symbol upload),
and `archive.ubuntu.com` refused connections during `apt-get update` in the
tests job. Each download was a single attempt; APT's own `Acquire::Retries`
covers one slow file but not a mirror that is unreachable for a minute.

- `scripts/port/download_retry.py` fetches with four attempts, waiting 5, 15
  and 45 s, and retries only transient failures (HTTP 429 and 5xx, connection
  errors and timeouts). A 404 or other client error fails at once. Callers
  still check every byte against their pinned SHA256, so a retry never widens
  what is accepted. `linux_build.download` (SDL, the AppImage runtime via
  `package_linux.py`, and `make_brand_art.py`'s inputs) and `sentry_tools.cli`
  use it.
- `ci_dependencies.py` repeats `apt-get update` and the archive download after
  20 and 60 s (`apt_network`). Its script hash is part of the APT cache key,
  so the first run after this change refills that cache once.
- The Linux job restores and saves `build_linux_ci/deps/downloads` and
  `build_linux_ci/downloads` (key: the hashes of `linux_build.py` and
  `package_linux.py`), so later runs skip those GitHub downloads entirely. The
  cached files are re-verified before use. Editing `sentry_tools.py` also
  invalidates the Sentry SDK cache once (about a 54 s rebuild).

**Sources:** [retry helper](scripts/port/download_retry.py),
[tests](scripts/port/test_download_retry.py),
[dependency cache](scripts/port/ci_dependencies.py) and its
[tests](scripts/port/test_ci_dependencies.py),
[Linux build](scripts/port/linux_build.py),
[Sentry tooling](scripts/port/sentry_tools.py),
[workflow](.github/workflows/windows-release.yml) (runs the new test and caches
the Linux downloads).

**Checks:** `test_download_retry.py` (504/502 then success, connection errors
and timeouts, giving up after four attempts, 404 failing at once),
`test_ci_dependencies.py` (an unreachable mirror repeats the command, then
gives up) and `test_sentry_tools.py` pass; `actionlint` passes on the workflow.
The gallery's input fingerprint covers these scripts, so the pre-commit hook
regenerated it: zero changed image cells, new manifest and index only.

### FORK-064 — Taser and watch laser ADS

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-08 at the owner's request and built into
the main Windows executable; the owner reviewed it and approved it on
2026-11-09.
Linux and browser builds not run locally.

Inherited behaviour (and FORK-003 until now): ADS covered the items from the
PP7 to the Moonraker laser, the grenade and rocket launchers and the throwing
knife. The watch laser (item 23, just past that range) and the taser (31)
fell back to the original aim mode with its red reticle, even with Aim Mode
set to ADS. Upstream draws both at the hip with a fixed rotation in
`gunUpdateAndFire` (`D_80035C70`, shared with the detonator, and
`D_80035C7C`, which turns the taser about 52 degrees so its face shows).

Both now use the normal ADS controls, the 150 ms raise and lower, half-speed
movement, ADS zoom (75% FOV), ADS Spread/Recoil and the existing single-item,
tank, switch and reload gates. Neither has sights, so each pose is a sight
picture of its own, calibrated with ADS Crosshair's aim point:

- **Taser:** turned a quarter turn to face the camera, its prongs tipped
  0.5 radian towards the target. The two prongs straddle the aim point with
  their tips level with it (measured within 2 px at 960x540).
- **Watch laser:** the arm rolls 0.35 radian and the watch face sits below
  the aim point, where the beam leaves it, so the hand stays below and right
  of the aim point instead of covering it.

`portAdsBlendRotation` (`joy_port.c`) eases each item's native hip rotation to
its ADS orientation with the blend, each angle the shorter way round (the watch
laser's native angles sit near a full turn, which would otherwise spin), and
leaves hip-fire angles untouched. The taser model has no muzzle node
(`Switches[3]`), so `gunfire.c` now poses an item without one from its model
origin; every earlier supported weapon has that node and is unchanged. Both get
pose-table entries but no generated grips: their native hands and the watch
laser's native arm move rigidly, without changing vertices, UVs, materials or
render setup, and the detonator keeps its pose. Weapon Kick and tracers already
leave both native.

**Shared hooks:** two `portAdsBlendRotation` calls in `gunUpdateAndFire`'s
taser and detonator/watch-laser rotation branches, and the muzzle-node fallback
in its ADS block (`src/game/gunfire.c`), all outside `TARGET_N64`.

**Sources:** [poses, rotation and gates](port/src/joy_port.c),
[interface](port/include/port_ads.h), [gun pose hooks](src/game/gunfire.c),
[capture driver](scripts/port/audit_ads.ps1) (now 23 items, with labels),
[alignment guide](scripts/port/ads_alignment.md),
[arm contracts note](scripts/port/arm_rendering.md).

**Checks:** `test_ads.c` covers both items' poses, gates and the rotation blend
(hip angles kept bit for bit, the halfway and settled taser turn, and the watch
laser easing the short way). `test_ads.sh`, `test_wardrobe.sh`,
`test_upstream_merge.sh`, `test_hud.sh`, `test_states.sh` and
`bun scripts/bright-builds-check.ts all` pass. Native ADS audits
(`audit_ads.ps1 -Item 31` and `-Item 23 -Transitions`, Runway, 960x540) were
reviewed settled and through 11 raise/lower frames each: no flips or spins.
Firing in ADS was not captured; the play-test covers it. The review gallery
was regenerated from the isolated build (both passes, 72 views): zero changed
image cells, so only its manifest and index record the new rendering inputs.

### FORK-063 — Shotgun Tracers: a tracer per pellet, and Decorative Pellets

**Status:** Implemented on 2026-11-08 and built for Windows; a scripted Dam
capture showed the player's pellet tracers. The owner then asked for other
players' pellets and guards' shotguns too; those were added the same day and
smoke-tested (a solo shotgun run and a two-player Temple run both exit
cleanly) but have not been seen in a capture. Decorative Pellets followed at
the owner's request. After play-testing, the owner made both settings on by
default (they were off at first), then asked for enemy pellet tracers to be
toned down with fixed values, without a new setting.
Linux and browser builds not run locally.

Inherited behaviour: a Shotgun or Automatic Shotgun blast fires
`NUMBER_SHOTGUN_BULLETS` (5) pellets through `chraiDefaultWeaponFireHandler`
in `chraiCheckUseHeldItem` (`chrprop.c`). Each pellet's hit calls
`gunSetTracerTarget`, but tracers are only created for the weapons listed in
`gunUpdateAndFire`, which leave out both shotguns, and each hand has one
`weapon_beam`, so shotguns draw no tracer. Guards fire a shotgun as a single
shot (`chrlvFireWeaponRelated` in `chraction.c`), and its tracer list leaves
shotguns out too.

**Gameplay > Iron Sights > Combat Feedback > Shotgun Tracers**
(`[display] shotgun_tracers`: 0 Off, 1 On; default 1), after Tracer Strength
in the Options folder and on the watch. When on, each pellet of a player's
blast draws its own tracer from the drawn muzzle to that pellet's hit. In
multiplayer each pellet also gets a beam from the shooter's third-person gun
(`field_2A18`) for the other players' views, under the same 5-degree
agreement check `gunCreateBeamForHand` applies to a bullet
(`portPelletSameDirection`). A guard's shotgun shot draws one beam from its
muzzle to the shot's end (the guard fires one shot, so there are no pellets
to draw).

**Decorative Pellets** (`[display] decorative_pellets`: 0 Off, 1 On; default
1), after Shotgun Tracers in both menus, takes effect only while Shotgun
Tracers is on (`portDecorativePelletsEnabled`). A guard's shotgun shot then
also draws four fake pellet tracers whose directions lie uniformly in a
3-degree cone around the real shot (`portPelletDecorativeEnd`,
`PORT_DECORATIVE_PELLET_CONE_TAN`), each as long as the real shot. They are
not tested against walls, so one can pass slightly into the surface the real
shot hit. Its help line says why: enemies really fire a single shot, which
alone can hit. The label is shorter than the requested "Decorative Enemy
Pellet Tracers" because that would be ten characters longer than any existing
row; the help line names enemies instead.

- **Hooks.** The pellet loop calls `portPelletTracerRecord(hand, i)` after
  each pellet, copying the tracer target it just set. `gunUpdateAndFire`'s
  tracer switch gains a shotgun case that places the muzzle with
  `gunWeaponFovPlaceWorld` and calls `portPelletTracersCreate`, which skips a
  hit nearer than the muzzle as `gunCreateBeamForHand` does. The player
  branch of the beam-timer tick in `chrprop.c` calls
  `portPelletTracersAdvance`, and `gunRenderFirstPersonGunModels` draws them
  with `portPelletTracersDraw` right after the hand's own tracer. The other
  players' beams are drawn by `portPelletTracersDrawOther` beside the native
  multiplayer character beams in `propobj.c`. `chrlvFireWeaponRelated` calls
  `portChrShotgunTracer` when a guard's shotgun fires a traced shot (`sp264`,
  every shot for single-shot weapons), before its weapon list would discard
  it; the NPC branch of the beam tick advances it
  (`portChrShotgunTracersAdvance`) and the character branch of the beam draw
  draws it (`portChrShotgunTracersDraw`).
- **Muzzle.** Pellet beams start at `field_B58`, the muzzle of the pose drawn
  on the firing frame. With Weapon Kick on, that pose no longer includes the
  firing round's kick (FORK-061, 2026-11-14), so the pellets leave the barrel
  before it rises.
- **Same look, own timing.** Pellet beams are drawn by the native tracer
  draw, so Tracer Strength styles them, at `PORT_PELLET_TRACER_SCALE` (60%)
  of a bullet tracer's width and glow alpha (60% of the native width even at
  100%). `portPelletBeamInit` and `portPelletBeamAdvance` reproduce the native
  setup and timer numbers (10000-unit path cap, a fifth of the path per field
  with a 500-unit floor, the 3000-unit streak cap, a start up to one step
  either side) but take their random start from a private xorshift generator
  and always advance by `g_GlobalTimerDelta`. The native setup and timer draw
  `randomGetNext`, so reusing them would shift the game RNG; these never do,
  so hits, AI and demos are unchanged.
- **State.** Five first-person beams, five third-person beams and five
  recorded hits per player and hand in `port_pellet_tracers.c`, started spent.
  A new blast replaces the hand's previous pellet beams. Guards' beams live in
